positiveFlows.title: ALABAMA AGRICULTURAL AND MECHANICAL UNIVERSITY (AAMU) CONDUCTS RESEARCH PROJECTS THAT MEET THE NEEDS OF THE CITIZENS OF ALABAMA AND THE NATION. TO FULFILL OUR OBLIGATIONS UNDER USDA-NIFA EVANS ALLEN ACT OF 1890 (SECTION 1445) FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024, THERE ARE SEVERAL APPROVED PROJECTS. BROADLY, RESEARCH AREAS OF INTERESTS ARE: FOOD SYSTEMS AND FOOD SAFETY; GLOBAL FOOD SECURITY AND HUNGER; NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY; HUMAN NUTRITION, WELL-BEING, HEALTH AND OBESITY; AND COMMUNITY AND REGIONAL PLANNING. FOOD SYSTEMS AND FOOD SAFETY: RESEARCH AND EXTENSION INTEGRATED ACTIVITIES ENHANCE FOOD SYSTEMS, FOOD SAFETY AND AGRICULTURAL BIOSECURITY. THE GOAL OF THIS CRITICAL ISSUE IS TO DEVELOP TECHNOLOGY AND METHODS TO PROTECT AND ENHANCE THE SAFETY OF AGRICULTURE AND FOOD, REDUCE EPIDEMICS OF FOOD-BORNE ILLNESSES, AND TO DEVELOP THE KNOWLEDGE AND METHODOLOGIES FOR RAPID DETECTION OF THREAT AGENTS, INCLUDING EXISTING AND EMERGING DISEASES OF PLANTS AND ANIMALS, RISK ASSESSMENT, AND FACILITY AND PERSONNEL SECURITY. GLOBAL FOOD SECURITY AND HUNGER: THE GOAL IS TO ENHANCE COMPETITIVENESS AND SUSTAINABILITY OF FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL INDUSTRIES IN ALABAMA THROUGH DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF BEST PRACTICES OR TECHNOLOGIES. THIS CRITICAL ISSUE ADDRESSES TWO BROADLY DEFINED PRIORITY AREAS; I) PLANT HEALTH AND PRODUCTION AND PLANT PRODUCTS, INCLUDING IMPROVED CROPPING SYSTEMS, PLANT BREEDING/GENOMICS, INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT, PRECISION AGRICULTURE, ALTERNATIVE SPECIALTY CROPS; AND II) ANIMAL HEALTH AND PRODUCTION, INCLUDING IMPROVED FOOD-ANIMAL SYSTEMS AND STOCKS. OF PARTICULAR INTEREST ARE PROGRAMS AND PROJECTS THAT INCLUDE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES AND THAT PRESENT INNOVATIVE SYNERGIES OF DISCIPLINES AND PERSPECTIVES. HUMAN NUTRITION, WELL-BEING, HEALTH AND OBESITY: OBESITY, DIABETES, HIGH BLOOD PRESSURE, AND VASCULAR ISSUES ARE MOSTLY CAUSED BY THE LACK OF NUTRIENTS, THE LACK OF EXERCISE, POOR LIFESTYLE CHOICES, AND STRESS OF THE INVOLVED INDIVIDUALS. AS A RESULT OF THE GROWING HEALTH CONCERNS FOR ALABAMA CITIZENS, THERE HAS BEEN A COMBINED EFFORT TO EDUCATE AND MOTIVATE CITIZENS THROUGHOUT THE STATE TO MAKE BETTER HEALTH DECISIONS. THE OBJECTIVE IS TO IMPROVE THE HEALTH OF ALABAMIANS, TARGETING LIMITED-RESOURCE FAMILIES, THROUGH CHRONIC DISEASE AWARENESS, PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, NUTRITION EDUCATION, HEALTH LITERACY AND ACCESS TO AND CONSUMPTION OF FRESH FRUITS AND VEGETABLES. NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY: THIS PROGRAM PLAN WILL GENERATE KNOWLEDGE TO MANAGE AGRICULTURAL AND NATURAL SYSTEMS IN THE FACE OF CLIMATE CHANGE AND THE NEED TO SUSTAIN NATURAL RESOURCES. SPECIFIC AREAS INCLUDE: CLIMATE-SMART SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS, ENERGY CONSERVATION AND UTILIZATION OF RENEWABLE ENERGY RESOURCES; UNDERSTANDING THE LAND-WATER INTERFACE; CONSEQUENCES AND SOLUTIONS OF GLOBAL CLIMATE CHANGE; WATER QUALITY AND QUANTITY, CARBON SEQUESTRATION, NATURAL SYSTEMS RESTORATION, SURFACE AND GROUND WATER CONSERVATION; MANAGEMENT OF AGRICULTURAL WASTE RESIDUE; SUSTAINABLE SOIL HEALTH ENHANCEMENT; SUSTAINABLE ECOAND AGRI-TOURISM; RURAL-URBAN INTERFACE ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES; REMOTE SENSING AND PRECISION AGRICULTURE. COMMUNITY AND REGIONAL PLANNING: THIS AREA IS DESIGNED TO MAINTAIN THE INTEGRITY OF AGRICULTURAL LANDS THROUGH RURAL AND URBAN PLANNING PROGRAMS. APPROPRIATED FUNDS WILL BE USED FOR EXPENSES IN CONDUCTING RESEARCH TO INCLUDE FACULTY AND STAFF SALARIES, STUDENT SUPPORT, DISSEMINATION OF RESEARCH RESULTS, ADMINISTRATIVE PLANNING AND DIRECTION, EQUIPMENT PURCHASE AND MAINTENANCE, AND SUPPLIES PURCHASE (AMONG OTHER APPROVED SPENDING).

ALABAMA'S RESEARCH AND EXTENSION SEEK TO ADDRESS SELECTED QUESTIONS THAT LEAD TO IDENTIFICATION OF CRITICAL ISSUES OF STRATEGIC IMPORTANCE. THESE ISSUES INCLUDE, BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO: (1) ENHANCING THE SUSTAINABILITY, COMPETITIVENESS, BIOSECURITY, AND PROFITABILITY OF U.S. FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS; (2) PLAYING A GLOBAL LEADERSHIP ROLE TO ENSURE A SAFE, SECURE, NUTRITIOUS, AND ABUNDANT FOOD SUPPLY FOR THE U.S. AND THE WORLD; (3) HEIGHTENING ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT OF SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT PRACTICES (FOOD/WATER); AND ADAPTING TO AND MITIGATING THE IMPACTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE ON FOOD, FEED, FIBER, AND FUEL SYSTEMS IN THE U.S.; (4) IMPROVING HUMAN HEALTH, NUTRITION, AND WELLBEING OF THE US POPULATION; (5) PROMOTING COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT, RURAL HEALTH, PROSPERITY AND RESILIENCE; (6) BUILDING CAPACITY OF INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES IN THE CONTEXT OF LEARNING, CULTURE, AND COMMUNITY; AND (7) SUPPORTING ENERGY SECURITY AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE BIO-ECONOMY FROM RENEWABLE NATURAL RESOURCES IN THE U.S. AS PART OF THE COMBINED ALABAMA LAND GRANT PLAN OF WORK, TUSKEGEE UNIVERSITY'S INTEGRATIVE RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS ARE PLANNED TO ADDRESS THE NATIONAL USDA FOOD, AGRICULTURE, NATURAL RECOURSES AND HUMAN SCIENCES STRATEGIC GOALS; NIFA PRIORITY SCIENCE AREAS AND THE ALABAMA AGRICULTURAL CRITICAL ISSUES AS IDENTIFIED BY THE STAKEHOLDERS. OUR PROGRAMS ARE THEREFORE FOCUSED ON THE FOLLOWING CRITICAL ISSUES: (1) GLOBAL FOOD SECURITY AND HUNGER; (2) NATURAL RESOURCES CONSERVATION AND MANAGEMENT, ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY AND CLIMATE CHANGE; (3) FOOD SYSTEM AND FOOD SAFETY; (4) HUMAN NUTRITION, WELL-BEING, HEALTH AND OBESITY; (5) SUSTAINABLE ENERGY; (6) COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT; AND (7) FAMILY, HOME AND 4-H AND YOUTH DEVELOPMENT. OUR PROGRAMS ARE DESIGNED TO PARTICULARLY ADDRESS THE ALABAMA BLACK BELT REGION AND HISTORICALLY DISADVANTAGED AND UNDERSERVED LIMITED RESOURCE PRODUCERS AND LAND OWNERS. SPECIFIC RESEARCH PROJECTS ARE THEREFORE FOCUSED ON: EFFICIENT WATER USE AND ADAPTATION TO CLIMATE VARIABILITY: A SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTION SOLUTION FOR HISTORICALLY DISADVANTAGED AND LIMITED RESOURCE FARMERS AND LANDOWNERS; SUSTAINABLE MEAT GOAT PRODUCTION SYSTEMS FOR LIMITED- RESOURCE PRODUCERS; SUSTAINABLE AND RELIABLE APPROACHES AND MARKETING STRATEGIES TO INCREASE YIELD OF VEGETABLES AND FRUITS FOR SOCIALLY DISADVANTAGED FARMERS IN ALABAMA; ALTERNATIVE POULTRY PRODUCTION: A SUSTAINABLE INTEGRATIVE POULTRY PRODUCTION MODEL FOR SMALL SCALE PRODUCERS; INTEGRATIVE APPROACHES TO OBESITY PREVENTION IN ALABAMA BLACK BELT COUNTIES; STRENGTHENING PROGRAMS IN ORGANIC FARMING IN ALABAMA THROUGH RESEARCH AND EDUCATION; AND DEVELOPMENT AND EVALUATION OF INTEGRATIVE ALTERNATIVE ENERGY SOURCES FOR LIMITED-RESOURCE FARMERS AND UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES IN ALABAMA.

IN ALIGNMENT WITH THE USDA-NIFA'S TOP RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PRIORITY AREAS, LINCOLN UNIVERSITY'S COOPERATIVE EXTENSION AND RESEARCH PROGRAM CONDUCT RESEARCH AND EXTENSION ACTIVITIES IN ANIMAL SCIENCE, PLANT SCIENCE, FOOD SAFETY, NATURAL RESOURCE, SOCIAL ECONOMICS, HUMAN HEALTH, AND YOUTH AREAS THAT ADDRESS EMERGENT AND CRITICAL ISSUES FACING MISSOURI FARMS AND AGRICULTURE COMMUNITIES. THE PROGRAM ESPECIALLY TARGETS UNDERREPRESENTED, UNDERSERVED, SMALL FAMERS AND COMMUNITY AND FIRSTGENERATION STUDENTS. THE EXTENSION AND RESEARCH PROGRAM IS CURRENTLY FOCUSED ON FIVE (5) IDENTIFIED CRITICAL ISSUES OF SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE, HEALTH, SOCIAL JUSTICE AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT, ENVIRONMENTAL AND NATURAL RESOURCES, AND EDUCATION AND COMMUNICATION WITH UNDERSERVED POPULATIONS IN MISSOURI THROUGH THE INTEGRATIVE, INNOVATIVE APPROACH FOR RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMMING. THE PROGRAM IS LAUNCHING SIX INITIATIVES: ORGANIC FARMING, URBAN AGRICULTURE, INDUSTRIAL HEMP, FOOD SAFETY TRAINING, AND FOREST ECOSYSTEM, AND SMALL RUMINANT, IN AN EFFORT TO MEET THE CRITICAL, GROWING NEEDS OF THE STATE AND STAKEHOLDERS. IN ADDITION, IN 2022, THE EXTENSION AND RESEARCH PROGRAM HAS ALSO JOINED THE GROUP EFFORTS OF THE 1890 MULTISTATE CLIMATE CHANGE PROJECT AND PARTICIPATED IN ALL FOUR PROJECT OBJECTIVES FOCUSING ON 1) SOIL HEALTH AND ADOPTIVE AG PRACTICES NEEDS ASSESSMENT AND TRAINING PROGRAM FOR SOCIALLYDISADVANTAGED FARMERS; 2) WATER RESOURCE AND CLIMATE CHANGE ASSESSMENT; 3) ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE AND EQUITY FOR LOW-INCOME COMMUNITIES; AND 4) ANALYSIS OF CLIMATE CHANGE POLICY. THE LU RESEARCH PROGRAM CONTINUES TO CONDUCT CUTTING-EDGE, IMPACTFUL FOOD AND AGRICULTURE RESEARCH THROUGH MULTI-INSTITUTION AND MULTIDISCIPLINARY COLLABORATIONS. THROUGH THE EVANS ALLEN (EA) PROGRAM, CENTRAL STATE UNIVERSITY (CSU) IS FOCUSED ON CONDUCTING FOOD, AGRICULTURE, NUTRITION AND HEALTH SCIENCES RESEARCH TO ADDRESS THE FOLLOWING SIX CRITICAL ISSUES IN THE STATE OF OHIO: DEVELOPING AND INFUSING EMERGENT TECHNOLOGIES IN AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS, SUSTAINING PLANT AND ANIMAL SYSTEMS, SECURING NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL SYSTEMS, ENHANCING FOOD NUTRITION AND HEALTH SYSTEMS, FOSTERING WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, ENGAGING COMMUNITIES AND TRANSFORMING LIVES. THE AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM (ARDP) WHICH SERVES AS THE RESEARCH PILLAR FOR THE LAND GRANT PROGRAM AT CENTRAL STATE UNIVERSITY CURRENTLY SUPPORTS NINE FULL TIME RESEARCH FACULTY AND TWO HYBRID FACULTY (50% RESEARCH) CONDUCTING RESEARCH TO ADDRESS THE CRITICAL ISSUES IDENTIFIED ABOVE. RESEARCH PROJECTS INCLUDE DEVELOPING ADVANCE PRECISION AGRICULTURAL TECHNOLOGIES FOR SMALL FARM AND SPECIALTY CROP AGRICULTURE; SOIL AND WATER CONSERVATION STUDIES FOR TARGETED IMPLEMENTATION OF AGRICULTURAL BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES IN OHIO FOR IMPROVING PRODUCTIVITY, SUSTAINABILITY AND CLIMATE MITIGATION AND ADAPTION IN AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS; IDENTIFYING ALTERNATE CROPPING SYSTEMS FOR OHIO SUCH AS HEMP, SPECIALTY CROPS AND SPECIALTY CORN THROUGH PLANT BREEDING AND GENOTYPE SCREENING; FOSTERING BIOECONOMY THROUGH PLANT BASED NATURAL PRODUCTS; GENOMIC AND GENETIC ENGINEERING STUDIES FOR IMPROVING POLLINATOR HEALTH; PRECISION NUTRITION MANAGEMENT AND HEALTHY LIFESTYLE STUDIES TO ADDRESS NUTRITION DRIVEN CHRONIC ILLNESSES INCLUDING DIABETES, OBESITY AND CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES IN MINORITY POPULATIONS; FOOD SAFETY STUDIES FOR IMPROVED UNDERSTANDING OF PATHOGEN VIRULENCE IN CONVENTIONAL AND ALTERNATE AGRICULTURAL AND FOOD PRODUCTION SYSTEMS; AND FOREST MANAGEMENT, FOREST FARMING AND URBAN FORESTRY STUDIES TO IMPROVE ECONOMY FROM TIMBER BASED AND NON-TIMBER BASED FOREST PRODUCTS AND TO ACHIEVE ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY IN FOREST LANDSCAPES IN SOUTHEASTERN OHIO. BEING AN 1890 LAND GRANT INSTITUTION, THE EA RESEARCH AT CSU PUTS A SPECIAL EMPHASIS ON SERVING SOCIALLY DISADVANTAGED FARMERS, RANCHERS AND LANDOWNERS INCLUDING MINORITY FARMERS, BEGINNING FARMERS AND LIMITED RESOURCE FARMERS. THIS FACILITY IS PART OF CSU'S VISION FOR ESTABLISHING A LARGER AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH AND DEMONSTRATION COMPLEX COMPRISING OF A SEVERAL OTHER FACILITIES AS CSU ENVISIONS TO EXPAND ITS FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH FOOTPRINT IN OHIO. THE NEW FACILITIES WILL ALSO INCLUDE GREENHOUSES AND HIGH TUNNELS FOR CONTROLLED EN VIRONMENT FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH. ALCORN STATE UNIVERSITY, FOUNDED IN 1871, IS AN 1890 HBCU LAND GRANT UNIVERSITY LOCATED IN LORMAN, MISSISSIPPI. IT PROVIDES A WIDE RANGE OF AGRICULTURAL SERVICES TO THE MINORITY COMMUNITIES IT SERVES. ALCORN HAS PROGRAMS IN AGRICULTURE RESEARCH, EDUCATION AND EXTENSION. AGRICULTURE RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EDUCATION AT ALCORN BOASTS DIVERSE FIELDS SUCH AS AGRONOMY, PLANT BREEDING, PLANT PATHOLOGY, ENTOMOLOGY, MYCOLOGY, VIROLOGY, SOIL SCIENCE, ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCE, ANIMAL SCIENCE, PLANT BIOTECHNOLOGY, BIOFUELS AND BIOPROCESSING, AGRICULTURE ECONOMICS, AGRIBUSINESS AND AGRICULTURE MECHANICS AND ITS APPLICATIONS. THESE DISCIPLINES AT ALCORN'S AGRICULTURE RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EDUCATION PROGRAMS HAVE BEEN ESTABLISHED TO SERVE SMALL FARMERS, LIMITED RESOURCE FARMERS AND DISADVANTAGED FARMERS OF MISSISSIPPI. ANOTHER SIGNIFICANT COMPONENT ALCORN STATE'S AGRICULTURE RESEARCH ACTIVITY AIMS AT ENHANCING AWARENESS OF AGRICULTURE AND THE RECRUITMENT OF MINORITY YOUTH FROM HIGH SCHOOL AND COMMUNITY COLLEGE. THE AGRICULTURE PROGRAMS AT ALCORN STATE CONTRIBUTE TO WORKFORCE TRAINING AT VARIOUS LEVELS, ANNUALLY PREPARING A SIGNIFICANT NUMBER OF SKILLED PROFESSIONALS FOR THE AGRICULTURE WORKFORCE. THE PROPOSED WORK IS OUTLINED TO INCLUDE 1) SOIL AND WATER QUALITY DEGRADATION, COVER CROPS AND SOIL AND WATER DEGRADATION MITIGATION; 2) CROP, VEGETABLES AND FRUITS PRODUCTION, PROCESSING AND STORAGE; 3) NATIVE AND NOVEL BIOFUEL CROPS SUCH AS SWITCHGRASS AND MISCANTHUS AS BIOFUELS FOR BIOMASS PRODUCTION; 4) PLANTS AS FEED FOR ANIMAL CONSUMPTION AND ANIMAL NUTRITIONAL RESEARCH; 5) SOIL SURVEY AND CLIMATE CHANGE INVESTIGATION; 6) EVALUATION OF IRRIGATION AND NATURAL WATER MOVEMENT ON COVER CROP AND VEGETABLE CROP POTENTIAL TO INCREASE SOIL AND WATER QUALITY; 7) DEVELOP AND APPLY TRADITIONAL AND LATEST TECHNOLOGY FOR PLANT PESTS DIAGNOSIS AND MANAGEMENT; 8) EVALUATION OF NOVEL AND SPECIALTY CROPS FOR INTEGRATION INTO SMALL FARMERS' FARM OPERATION AND THEIR ECONOMIC IMPACTS ON SMALL FARM'S OPERATION; 9) ADOPTION AND APPLICATION OF NOVEL BIOTECHNOLOGY SUCH AS GENOME EDITING FOR CROP GENETIC IMPROVEMENT; 10) SMART AGRICULTURE AND APPLICATIONS OF ROBOTICS AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN BROAD AGRICULTURE PRODUCTIONS; 11) ANIMAL PRODUCTION, PHYSIOLOGY, GENETICS, ZOONOTIC DISEASE INVESTIGATION AND PUBLIC HEALTH EDUCATION; 12) DEMONSTRATION OF AGRICULTURE RESEARCH FOR SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY, ENGINEERING AND MATH (STEM) OUTREACH TO PREK-12 SCHOOLS AND COMMUNITY COLLEGES FOR WORKFORCE CULTIVATION; 13) PRESENT RESEARCH FINDINGS AT LOCAL, REGIONAL, AND NATIONAL CONFERENCES; 14) PUBLISH RESEARCH RESULT.

EVANS ALLEN PROJECT ABSTRACT THROUGH THE INSTITUTE OF AGRICULTURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL RESEARCH, THE GOAL OF AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH AT TENNESSEE STATE UNIVERSITY IS TO CREATE AND COMMUNICATE NEW KNOWLEDGE IN THE AGRICULTURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCES. THROUGH OUR INNOVATIVE RESEARCH, WE ADDRESS THE NEEDS OF HUMANKIND, FOCUSING ON FINDING SOLUTIONS TO CHALLENGES FACED BY SOCIALLY AND ECONOMICALLY DISADVANTAGED GROUPS, AND CONTRIBUTING TO THE PROSPERITY OF THE CITIZENS OF TENNESSEE, THE NATION, AND THE WORLD. RESEARCH IN TENNESSEE STATE UNIVERSITY AGRICULTURE IS ORGANIZED TO ADDRESS THE CRITICAL ISSUES DESCRIBED BELOW. ENHANCING BIODIVERSITY AND ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY SAFEGUARDING AND ENHANCING THE NATURAL RESOURCE ENVIRONMENT HAS BECOME INCREASINGLY COMPLEX WITHIN ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL, RESOURCE AND PERSONAL CONTEXTS. THROUGH COLLABORATION AMONG RESEARCHERS, INDUSTRY, PRODUCERS, ENVIRONMENTAL GROUPS, AND GOVERNMENT, WE ARE HELPING PRESERVE A DIVERSE AND RESILIENT ENVIRONMENT FOR FUTURE GENERATIONS. ENRICHING OUR ECONOMY HELPING FARMS AND AGRICULTURE BUSINESSES BECOME MORE PROFITABLE AND INDIVIDUALS BECOME FINANCIALLY SECURE BOOSTS THE LOCAL, STATE, AND NATIONAL ECONOMIES. OUR PROGRAMS STRIVE TO STRENGTHEN THE ECONOMIC VIABILITY OF ALL FACETS OF AGRIBUSINESS, AND IMPROVE THE FINANCIAL LITERACY OF TENNESSEANS AND BEYOND SO THEY MAY BUILD AND PROTECT WEALTH FOR THEMSELVES AND FUTURE GENERATIONS. STRENGTHENING OUR HEALTH MAKING HEALTHY CHOICES IS IMPORTANT FOR HUMANS, ANIMALS, AND EVEN OUR PLANET. AS A LEADER IN NUTRITION, ANIMAL WELFARE, AND ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION, WE ARE WORKING TO UNDERSTAND HOW FOOD, PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, AND SOCIAL CONNECTIONS AFFECT OVERALL HEALTH. SUPPORTING FOOD, FIBER, AND ENERGY SYSTEMS SAFE, SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS THAT ARE SOCIALLY, ECONOMICALLY, AND ENVIRONMENTALLY RESPONSIBLE ARE KEY TO ENHANCING THE LIVES OF TENNESSEANS AND SUPPORTING A GROWING GLOBAL POPULATION. WE ARE EXPLORING WAYS TO DELIVER DISCOVERIES USING A SYSTEMS APPROACH TO AGRICULTURE PRODUCTIVITY THAT WILL PROVIDE CUSTOMIZABLE SOLUTIONS FOR PRODUCERS. 2 OUR RESEARCH ADDRESSES THESE CRITICAL ISSUES THROUGH FACULTY GROUPS IN THE PLANT, ANIMAL, FOOD, AND HUMAN SCIENCES. WE CONDUCT RESEARCH IN AGRICULTURAL LEADERSHIP, EDUCATION AND COMMUNICATION THAT BRIDGES THE GAP BETWEEN THE GENERAL PUBLIC AND SCIENTISTS WORKING TO SOLVE CURRENT AND EMERGING CHALLENGES RELATED TO SUSTAINABLY FEEDING AN EVER-GROWING POPULATION UNDER VARIOUS ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIETAL COMPLICATIONS. IN THE AREA OF AGRIBUSINESS, WE PREPARE STUDENTS, FARMERS, AND STAKEHOLDERS IN THE USE OF ECONOMIC ANALYSIS AND MANAGEMENT COMPETENCIES TO TAKE ON THE CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES OF A DYNAMIC AGRI-FOOD SYSTEM. RESEARCH IN ANIMAL SCIENCE IS DIRECTED AT IMPROVING LIVESTOCK PRODUCTION SYSTEMS BY GENERATING NOVEL FINDINGS THAT IMPACT ANIMAL WELL-BEING AND PERFORMANCE. ONGOING FOOD SCIENCE RESEARCH FOCUSES ON IMPROVING THE SAFETY, QUALITY, SHELF-LIFE, NUTRIENT PROFILE AND SENSORY ATTRIBUTES OF NOVEL FOOD INGREDIENTS, DEVELOPING AND VALIDATING ADVANCED AND INNOVATIVE TECHNOLOGIES FOR FOOD PROCESSING, MANUFACTURING, PACKAGING, AND SANITATION TO EFFECTIVELY REDUCE THE PRESENCE OF FOODBORNE PATHOGENS. RESEARCH IN NATURAL RESOURCES USES MULTIDISCIPLINE APPROACHES TO UNDERSTAND AND ATTENUATE PROBLEMS CAUSED BY CLIMATE CHANGE, LAND DEGRADATION, LOSS OF BIODIVERSITY, EMERGING CONTAMINANTS, AND ANTHROPOGENIC STRESSORS. PLANT SCIENCE RESEARCH INCLUDES DIVERSE FIELDS IN AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION SYSTEMS WITH A FOCUS ON DEVELOPING AND APPLYING SCIENTIFIC AND BIOTECHNOLOGICAL PRINCIPLES TO IMPROVE CROP PRODUCTIVITY, REDUCE LOSSES FROM DISEASE, INSECT PESTS, AND TOXIC METAL STRESS. TO ADDRESS THE WELL-BEING AND HEALTH OF INDIVIDUALS, FAMILIES AND COMMUNITIES, RESEARCH IN FAMILY AND CONSUMER SCIENCES IS FOCUSED ON IMPROVING THE LIVES OF OUR STAKEHOLDERS THROUGH EDUCATION, LEADERSHIP AND COMMUNICATION TO IMPROVE NOT ONLY THEIR HEALTH AND WELL-BEING, BUT ALSO THEIR RELATIONSHIPS AND RESOURCES.

OUR RESEARCH PROGRAMS HAVE A PARTICULAR FOCUS TO THE NEEDS OF SMALL TO MEDIUM SCALE, LIMITED RESOURCE FARMERS AND INDUSTRY STAKEHOLDERS. NINETY PERCENT OF FLORIDA'S FARMS FIT THE DEFINITION OF A SMALL FARM, WHICH MAKES OUR MISSION PARTICULARLY CRUCIAL IN ENHANCING THE OVERALL ECONOMY OF THE STATE. THE MAJOR AREAS OF NEED ARE CAPTURED IN THE FOLLOWING PLANNED PROGRAMS: 1. VITICULTURE AND SMALL FRUITS RESEARCH, 2. PRESERVING WATER QUALITY OF NORTH FLORIDA WATERSHEDS RESEARCH 3. STRATEGIC RESEARCH FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF INVASIVE PEST SPECIES, AND 4. FAMU LIVESTOCK AND CROP IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM. THE VITICULTURE AND SMALL FRUITS RESEARCH PROVIDES LEADERSHIP IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE GRAPE AND WINE INDUSTRY IN FLORIDA THROUGH QUALITY RESEARCH AND STATEWIDE EXTENSION AND OUTREACH ACTIVITIES THAT ADDRESS THE NEEDS AND CONCERNS OF STAKEHOLDERS. PRESERVING WATER QUALITY OF NORTH FLORIDA WATERSHEDS RESEARCH IS ADMINISTERED THROUGH THE CENTER FOR WATER RESOURCES. THE CENTER CONTINUES TO WORK WITH UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS, CONDUCT NEED-BASED RESEARCH AND WORK WITH THE COOPERATIVE EXTENSION PROGRAM AND THE U.S. FOREST SERVICE, SOUTHERN RESEARCH STATION, AS WELL AS A NUMBER OF DIVERSE STAKEHOLDERS. STRATEGIC RESEARCH FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF INVASIVE PEST SPECIES IS IMPLEMENTED BY THE CENTER FOR BIOLOGICAL CONTROL. THE PROBLEMS POSED BY INVASIVE ALIEN SPECIES (IAS) ARE BROAD, WITH IMPACTS AT THE LOCAL, STATE, NATIONAL AND GLOBAL LEVELS. IAS POSE MAJOR THREATS TO AGRICULTURE AND THE ENVIRONMENT. LASTLY, FAMU LIVESTOCK AND CROP IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM WILL INCLUDE LIVESTOCK IMPROVEMENT, HAY PRODUCTION, FORAGE SYSTEMS IMPROVEMENT, SPECIALIZED HORTICULTURAL CROPS, AND BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES FOR LIVESTOCK AND CROP PRODUCTION.

THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS AT PINE BLUFF (UAPB), SCHOOL OF AGRICULTURE, FISHERIES AND HUMAN SCIENCES, COMPRISES THREE ACADEMIC DEPARTMENTS; OUR RESEARCH FACULTY ARE INTEGRATED INTO THE ACADEMIC DEPARTMENTS. PERSONNEL WITH A MAJORITY RESEARCH APPOINTMENT ARE UNDER THE SUPERVISION OF THE DEPARTMENT CHAIRS, THE ASSISTANT DEAN FOR RESEARCH, AND THE ASSOCIATE RESEARCH DIRECTOR. THEREFORE, UAPB RESEARCHERS DELIVER EVIDENCE-BASED DATA AND DATA-DRIVEN RESEARCH TO THEIR CLIENTELE. EMPLOYING DIVERSE ASSESSMENTS THROUGHOUT THE DURATION OF THEIR EVANS-ALLEN PROJECT AND SERVE BOTH AS A FORMATIVE AND SUMMATIVE FUNCTION. QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DATA COLLECTION METHODS WILL BE UTILIZED. FOR EXAMPLE, A SUMMARY OF THE PROJECT UAPB SWEET POTATO FOUNDATION SEED PROGRAM: IMPROVING SWEET POTATO PRODUCTION IN ARKANSAS. IN THIS PROJECT, SWEET POTATOES ARE PROPAGATED BY STEM CUTTINGS, MAKING THE CROP SUSCEPTIBLE TO VIRUS ACCUMULATION. MORE THAN 30 VIRUSES ARE KNOWN TO INFECT SWEET POTATOES. THUS, THE USE OF VIRUS-INFECTED SLIPS CAN ULTIMATELY AFFECT THE YIELD AND QUALITY OF SWEET POTATO ROOTS. PROBLEMS WITH YIELD REDUCTION CAN BE SOLVED BY PROVIDING VIRUS-FREE PLANTING SLIPS TO FARMERS. DURING THE LAST DECADE, THE PLANTED ACREAGE OF SWEET POTATOES WITHIN ARKANSAS HAS INCREASED. THE MARKET DEMAND FOR SWEET POTATOES AND PRODUCTS MADE FROM THE CROP HAS CONTINUED TO GROW THE NEED FOR HIGH-QUALITY, VIRUS-INDEXED PLANTING MATERIAL. ANOTHER EXAMPLE WILL BE THE SCHOOL OF AGRICULTURE, FISHERIES AND HUMAN SCIENCES (SAFHS) RESEARCH APPRENTICESHIP PROGRAM (RAP), WHICH WILL BE FOR UNIVERSITY AND HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS. THIS REWARDING, HANDS-ON PROGRAM IN THE FOOD, AGRICULTURE, NUTRITION, AND HUMAN SCIENCES WILL BE FOR THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS AT PINE BLUFF AND HIGH SCHOOL RISING JUNIORS AND SENIORS STUDENTS IN SURROUNDING AREAS. THIS PROGRAM WILL BE WORKING OPPORTUNITIES FOR STUDENTS TO PARTICIPATE IN A RESEARCH AND APPRENTICESHIP PROGRAM, PERFORMING HANDS-ON RESEARCH ACTIVITIES TO PREPARE AGRICULTURE AND STEM STUDENTS FOR FUTURE USDA CAREERS. HENCE, THESE STUDENTS WILL ASSIST SAFHS RESEARCH FACULTY AND SCIENTISTS ON RESEARCH PROJECTS IN LABORATORIES AND FIELD EXPERIMENTS. IN ADDITION, COWPEA (VIGNA UNGUICULATA L. WALP.) IS AN IMPORTANT ANNUAL LEGUME WIDELY GROWN IN AFRICA, ASIA, THE MIDDLE EAST, SOUTHERN EUROPE, SOUTHERN AND WESTERN U.S., AND CENTRAL AND SOUTH AMERICA, CHIEFLY USED AS A GRAIN CROP FOR FOOD, OR AS ANIMAL FODDER AND AS A FRESH VEGETABLE WITH MORE THAN 14 MILLION HECTARES WORLDWIDE GROWN AND MORE THAN 5.4 MILLION TONS HARVESTED ANNUALLY. CONSIDERED ONE OF THE MOST NUTRITIOUS CROPS WITH A HIGH PROTEIN CONTENT (~23% DRIED SEED WEIGHT), THE PROJECT WILL EVALUATE AND IMPROVE COWPEA GERMPLASM FOR INCORPORATION INTO AND UTILIZATION IN THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS AT PINE BLUFF) TO EVALUATE SEED PROTEIN CONTENT IN WORLDWIDE COWPEA-IMPROVED LINES AND CHARACTERIZE THESE LINES ON THEIR SEED PHENOTYPE STRAITS. EXPECTED IMPACT OUTCOMES FROM THIS PROJECT INCLUDE ENHANCED READY-TO-USE SCIENTIFIC COWPEA RESOURCES; ENHANCED BREEDING OPPORTUNITIES TO DEVELOP MULTIPLE HIGH SEED PROTEIN CONTENT COWPEA VARIETIES WITH DIFFERENT SEED COAT COLOR BACKGROUNDS, HENCE OFFERING MORE CONSUMER CHOICES, AND BREEDING OPPORTUNITIES TO DEVELOP VARIETIES WITH PHENOTYPIC TRAITS CONDUCIVE TO MECHANICAL COWPEA PRODUCTION, HENCE ENABLING FARMERS TO PRODUCE MORE COWPEA. HENCE, IT COULD STIMULATE HIGHER COWPEA CONSUMPTION AND PRODUCTION. THIS ONE-PAGE ABSTRACT IS JUST A SNAPSHOT OF THE EVIDENCE-BASED, DATA-DRIVEN RESEARCH UAPB RESEARCHERS DO TO FURTHER THE LAND GRANT MISSION. TODAY, THIS PROGRAM IS INTEGRAL IN HELPING THE UNIVERSITY PRESERVE ITS 1890 LAND-GRANT LEGACY OF SERVICE TO THE CITIZENS OF THE DELTA REGION IN ARKANSAS. ADDITIONALLY, THE 1890 RESEARCH PROGRAM FUNDS RESEARCH PROJECTS TO ENCOURAGE AND COORDINATE UNIVERSITY-WIDE AND EXTERNAL COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH TO BENEFIT THE WHOLE STATE OF ARKANSAS, NATIONALLY AND INTERNATIONALLY.

THE UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE, FOOD AND ENVIRONMENT AND KENTUCKY STATE UNIVERSITY (KSU) COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE, COMMUNITIES, AND THE ENVIRONMENT WERE FOUNDED AS LAND-GRANT INSTITUTIONS (1862 AND 1890, RESPECTIVELY), OFFERING ACCESS TO KNOWLEDGE AND LEARNING TO ENHANCE THE LIVES OF KENTUCKIANS. THE TWO PROGRAMS ARE FUNDAMENTALLY INTERDISCIPLINARY, APPLYING THE BIOLOGICAL, PHYSICAL, AND SOCIAL SCIENCES TO CHALLENGES IN AGRICULTURAL, FOOD, AND ENVIRONMENTAL SYSTEMS. OUR WORK ENCOMPASSES FARMS AND FORESTS, FOOD AND FIBER, FAMILIES, AND COMMUNITIES. THE UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE, FOOD AND ENVIRONMENT HOLDS A UNIQUE POSITION AS THE HOME OF THE KENTUCKY AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION AND THE KENTUCKY COOPERATIVE EXTENSION SERVICE (KCES). THE TEACHING, RESEARCH, AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS ARE PART OF A NATIONAL SYSTEM THAT MAINTAINS A STATEWIDE PRESENCE AND LINKS LOCAL, STATE, NATIONAL AND GLOBAL ISSUES. THE KSU LAND GRANT PROGRAM AND COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE, COMMUNITIES AND THE ENVIRONMENT FOCUSES ON TEACHING, RESEARCH, AND EXTENSION TO ADDRESS THE NEEDS OF THE SMALL-SCALE AND LIMITED- RESOURCE FARMERS; MINORITY AND UNDERSERVED/DISPARITY COMMUNITIES, AS WELL AS DIVERSE AND AT-RISK YO UTHS. THESE PROGRAMS INCLUDE RESEARCH TO IDENTIFY NEW AND NICHE PRODUCTS AND MARKETS FOR SMALL-SCALE, LIMITED RESOURCE, AND MINORITY FARMERS, TO ENHANCE AVAILABILITY AND SAFETY OF LOCALLY PRODUCED, NUTRITIOUS FOODS, AND REDUCE FERTILIZER AND PESTICIDE RUNOFF TO IMPROVE SOIL AND WATER QUALITY WHILE REDUCING FARMER AND FORESTER EXPENSES. OUR VISION IS TO BE RECOGNIZED FOR EXCELLENCE IN FOSTERING LEARNING THAT CHANGES LIVES, DISCOVERIES THAT CHANGE THE WORLD AND OPPORTUNITIES THAT SHAPE THE FUTURE. RESEARCH AND EXTENSION, AS FULL PARTNERS WITH EXPANDING LINKAGES THROUGHOUT THE UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY AND KSU AND WITH SUPPORT FROM EVERY KENTUCKY COUNTY, SEEK TO 1) FACILITATE LIFELONG LEARNING INFORMED BY SCHOLARSHIP AND RESEARCH, 2) EXPAND KNOWLEDGE THROUGH CREATIVE RESEARCH AND DISCOVERY, AND 3) SERVE KENTUCKIANS BY SHARING AND APPLYING KNOWLEDGE. RESEARCH AND EXTENSION SEEK TO SUSTAIN THE LAND-GRANT HERITAGE OF ACHIEVEMENT IN THESE CHALLENGING TIMES, BUT THE COMMONWEALTH AND THE UNIVERSITIES ARE UNDERGOING MANY SIGNIFICANT CHANGES. AS KENTUCKY CONTINUES TO MOVE FROM A TOBACCO-BASED AGRICULTURAL ECONOMY AND EXPLORES NEW OPTIONS AND COMMODITIES, LAND-GRANT PROGRAMS FACE INCREASED DEMANDS AND EXPECTATIONS. TECHNOLOGY IS REDEFINING THE WAY PEOPLE ACQUIRE AND DISTRIBUTE INFORMATION AND HOW THEY SOLVE PROBLEMS. WHILE URBANIZATION IS CLAIMING FARMLAND, IT IS ALSO CREATING NEW MARKETS FOR TRADITIONAL AND NON-TRADITIONAL AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS. CHANGING LIFESTYLES AND DEMOGRAPHICS ARE CHALLENGING US WITH OPPORTUNITIES FOR GREATER INVOLVEMENT IN YOUTH, FAMILY, AND COMMUNITY PROGRAMS. WITH NEARLY 80,000 FARMS IN THE STATE AND AN AVERAGE 171 ACRES PER OPERATION, KENTUCKY IS DOMINATED BY SMALL FAMILY FARMS. HOWEVER, MANY OF THESE FARMS ARE MAJOR PRODUCERS OF TRADITIONAL AGRICULTURAL COMMODITIES, SUCH AS LIVESTOCK, TOBACCO, AND GRAIN. SOME SEEK NEW OPPORTUNITIES IN SPECIALTY CROPS AND INDUSTRIAL HEMP. OTHERS OPERATE ON A PART- TIME BASIS OR INVOLVE LIMITED RESOURCES. THE RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS AT BOTH LAND-GRANT INSTITUTIONS PROVIDE THE BREADTH NEEDED TO ADDRESS THE STATE'S DIVERSITY OF AGRICULTURAL OPERATIONS AND AGROECOSYSTEMS. MORE THAN HALF OF THE STATE'S CASH RECEIPTS FROM FARM MARKETS RESULT FROM ANIMALS AND ANIMAL PRODUCTS. SIGNATURE INDUSTRIES INCLUDE BEEF AND EQUINE, WHICH RELY ON CUTTING-EDGE RESEARCH TO MITIGATE FESCUE TOXICOSIS, CONTROL INFECTIOUS DISEASES AND IMPROVE REPRODUCTIVE EFFICIENCIES. ANIMAL PRODUCTION SYSTEMS, INCLUDING POULTRY, SWINE, SMALL RUMINANTS AND AQUACULTURE, ARE FACED WITH INCREASING PUBLIC PRESSURE TO ENSURE HIGH LEVELS OF ANIMAL WELFARE AND OPERATE IN ENVIRONMENTALLY SUSTAINABLE WAYS. THERE IS INCREASING INTEREST AMONG PRODUCERS FOR PRECISION ANIMAL MANAGEMENT TOOLS THAT CAN HELP INCREASE MARGINS AND A CONTINUED NEED FOR ASSISTANCE DEVELOPING AND MARKETING VALUE-ADDED PRODUCTS, PARTICULARLY FOR THE STATE'S DECLINING DAIRY INDUSTRY AND FOR SMALL AND LIMITED-RESOURCE FARMERS. SOYBEANS AND GRAIN CROPS HAVE BECOME INCREASINGLY IMPORTANT TO KENTUCKY AS THE TOBACCO INDUSTRY CONTINUES TO DECLINE. PRODUCERS RELY ON THE LAND-GRANTS FOR RESEARCH-BASED GUIDANCE ON MANAGING INTENSIVE PRODUCTION WITH MINIMAL ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT. RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS ADDRESS MANAGEMENT OF NUTRIENTS, PESTS AND DISEASES, VARIETY SELECTION IN A CHANGING CLIMATE AND WATER MANAGEMENT. THEY HELP PRODUCERS EFFECTIVELY USE PROVEN PRECISION FARMING AND LAND MANAGEMENT TOOLS. ADDITIONALLY, FORAGE SYSTEMS UNDERPIN THE STATE'S SIGNATURE EQUINE AND BEEF INDUSTRIES; THEIR MANAGEMENT CONTINUES TO BE A FOCUS FOR RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS IN THE STATE. HISTORICALLY, RURAL COMMUNITIES HAVE HAD MAJOR DEPENDENCE ON FARM INCOMES FOR THEIR ECONOMIC VIABILITY. WITH THE DECLINING POTENTIAL OF TOBACCO TO GENERATE FARM INCOME, DEVELOPMENT AND DISCOVERY OF NEW ENTERPRISES AND MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES ARE ESSENTIAL. THE LAND-GRANT SYSTEM WILL BE CHALLENGED TO FIND NEW STRATEGIES TO MEET THE DEMANDS FOR INCREASED DIVERSIFICATION IN RURAL COMMUNITIES. PROGRAMS IN SUPPORT OF HIGH-VALUE HORTICULTURAL CROPS, AQUACULTURE, INDUSTRIAL HEMP, DISTILLATION, WINE MAKING, BREWING AND NICHE-MARKET ANIMAL PRODUCTS ARE CRITICAL TO PROVIDING VIABLE ALTERNATIVES TO TOBACCO PRODUCTION. IN THE POST-TOBACCO-GROWING ERA, SUCCESSFUL RISK MANAGEMENT IS IMPORTANT IN MAINTAINING COMPETITIVENESS IN THE STATE'S AGRICULTURAL ECONOMY. VALUE OPPORTUNITIES IN AGRICULTURE CREATES JOBS, MANY WITHIN RURAL COMMUNITIES. VALUE OPPORTUNITIES ALSO CREATE EXPANDED DEMAND FOR LOCAL AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS. INITIATIVES ARE REQUIRED TO ENCOURAGE LOCAL ENTREPRENEURIAL CREATIVITY AND RISK-TAKING AND TO BUILD A NETWORK OF SUPPORT RESOURCES. KENTUCKY IS MAKING SUBSTANTIAL RESOURCE COMMITMENTS TO SUPPORT THE CREATION OF AN "AGRITECH" ECOSYSTEM, AS WELL AS VALUE-ADDED INNOVATIONS THAT UTILIZE LOCAL AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS, PARTICULARLY IN THE AREAS OF LIVESTOCK, HORTICULTURE, SECONDARY WOOD PRODUCTS, AND AGRITOURISM. THE CURRENT PUBLIC INTEREST IN COMMUNITY- AND REGION-BASED LOCAL FOOD SYSTEMS PROVIDES KENTUCKY'S RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS AN IDEAL OPPORTUNITY TO SHOWCASE RELEVANCE TO ALL CITIZENS ACROSS THE STATE AND ADDRESS ISSUES OF FOOD SECURITY, NUTRITION, PROSPERITY, AND SUSTAINABILITY IN BOTH RURAL AND URBAN COMMUNITIES. THE MISSION OF AN EFFECTIVE FOOD SAFETY SYSTEM IS TO PROTECT AND IMPROVE PUBLIC HEALTH BY ENSURING THAT FOODS MEET SCIENCE-BASED SAFETY STANDARDS. OVER 50% OF ALL FOOD-BORNE ILLNESS CAN BE ATTRIBUTED TO MISTAKES MADE IN FOOD SERVICE ESTABLISHMENTS AND RESTAURANTS, WHILE 20% ARE TRACEABLE TO CONSUMERS IN THEIR HOMES. CHANGES IN THE RISK OF FOOD-BORNE DISEASE ARE DUE PRIMARILY TO CHANGES IN DIET, INCREASED USE OF COMMERCIAL FOOD SERVICE AND FOOD PREPARED AND EATEN AWAY FROM HOME, NEW METHODS OF PRODUCING AND DISTRIBUTING FOOD, AND THE GROWING NUMBER OF AT-RISK INDIVIDUALS, SUCH AS THE ELDERLY AND THOSE WITH ELEVATED RISKS TO THEIR IMMUNE SYSTEMS. EDUCATIONAL TRAINING ON THE SAFE PRODUCTION, PREPARATION, HANDLING, AND STORAGE OF FOOD FOR PRODUCERS, PROCESSORS, CONSUMERS, AND AT-RISK GROUPS IS THE TRADITIONAL APPROACH TO DECREASE THE RISKS OF FOOD-BORNE ILLNESS. THREE LEADING CAUSES OF MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY IN KENTUCKY ARE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE, CANCER, AND DIABETES. THE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR THEIR PREVENTION AND TREATMENT OF THESE CHRONIC DISEASES INCLUDE STRONG NUTRITIONAL AND PHYSICAL ACTIVITY COMPONENTS. OBESITY IS A CONTRIBUTING FACTOR IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF THESE DISEASES. IN KENTUCKY, THE PREVALENCE OF OVERWEIGHT ADULTS HAS ESCALATED OVER THE LAST DECADES. EARLY DIAGNOSIS OF CANCER, DIABETES, AND CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE IS ASSOCIATED WITH IMPROVED OUTCOMES, INCLUDING IMPROVED QUALITY OF LIFE AND LONGEVITY. PREVENTION, DETECTION, AND TREATMENT OF CHRONIC DISEASE IN KENTUCKY IS PARTICULARLY IMPORTANT IN TODAY'S CHANGING HEALTHCARE ENVIRONMENT. PEOPLE WITH CHRONIC DISEASES REQUIRE SKILLS FOR SELF-CARE. PUBLIC CONCERN OVER ECOSYSTEM ISSUES AS WELL AS NATIONAL AND STATE GOVERNMENT HAS GENERATED RECOGNITION OF THE NEED FOR RESEARCH AND EDUCATION PROGRAMS. KENTUCKY'S BIOLOGICAL WEALTH MAY CONTINUE TO BE THREATENED UNLESS COMPREHENSIVE AND SUSTAINABLE APPROACHES ARE RESEARCHED AND UTILIZED FOR ENJOYING, STUDYING, AND, AT THE SAME TIME, HARVESTING THE FRUITS OF THE LAND THROUGH LOGGING, MINING, AND AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION. ECOSYSTEM SERVICES MUST BE PRESERVED, ANTI-MICROBIAL RESISTANCE MUST BE MITIGATED AND POLLINATOR POPULATIONS MUST BE PROTECTED. APPROACHES MUST ALSO CONSIDER HOW THESE SYSTEMS ADAPT TO AND MITIGATE CLIMATE CHANGE. PROGRAMS MUST STRIVE TO ELUCIDATE HOW CLIMATE CHANGE WILL IMPACT AGRICULTURAL AND NATURAL RESOURCE SYSTEMS WHILE DEVELOPING PROGRAMS AND TECHNOLOGIES THAT WILL HELP FARMERS, FORESTERS, AND OTHERS ADAPT. THE LAND GRANT SYSTEM'S MISSION OF ENHANCING ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITY AND IMPROVING THE QUALITY OF LIFE FOR AMERICANS GOES WELL BEYOND A GRICULTURAL PRODUCTION. IT INCLUDES THE EMPOWERMENT OF PEOPLE AND COMMUNITIES THROUGH RESEARCH-BASED INFORMATION AND EDUCATION TO ADDRESS ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL CHALLENGES FACING OUR YOUTH, FAMILIES, AND COMMUNITIES. SOME CHALLENGES ARE: BOTH URBAN AND RURAL AREAS OF THE STATE CONTINUE TO BE PLAGUED BY HIGH UNEMPLOYMENT AND UNDEREMPLOYMENT. NEARLY 30% OF KENTUCKY'S YOUTH FAIL TO GRADUATE FROM HIGH SCHOOL. WITH MANY INDUSTRIES RELOCATING TO OTHER COUNTRIES, JOB CLOSINGS HAVE AFFECTED MANY AREAS OF THE STATE. MANY KENTUCKIANS LACK THE EDUCATIONAL PREPARATION AND SKILLS NEEDED TO SECURE AND MAINTAIN EMPLOYMENT OR QUALIFY FOR NEW-ERA JOBS. THROUGHOUT THEIR LIVES, BOTH YOUTH AND ADULT KENTUCKIANS NEED TO DEVELOP SKILLS ESSENTIAL TO BECOME PRODUCTIVE MEMBERS OF THE COMMUNITY AND WORKFORCE. BEING A PRODUCTIVE MEMBER OF SOCIETY AS AN ADULT REQUIRES YOUNG PEOPLE TO GAIN EXPERIENCE AS ACTIVE CITIZENS ATAN EARLY AGE. 4-H COMMUNITY SERVICE ACTIVITIES PROVIDE LEARNING EXPERIENCES THAT HELP YOUTH DEVELOP LIFE SKILLS NEEDED TO BE EFFECTIVE IN VARIOUS ADULT ROLES IN SOCIETY. OUR GOAL IS TO IMPROVE THE CAPACITY OF COMMUNITIES TO IDENTIFY AND ADDRESS THESE CRITICAL ISSUES, AND OTHERS THAT AFFECT THE LIVES OF CITIZENS. WE CAN BEST DO THIS BY FOSTERING THE DEVELOPMENT OF PERSONAL AND INTERPERSONAL SKILLS, STIMULATING VOLUNTEER LEADERSHIP, AND PROMOTING ACTIVE PARTICIPATION IN COMMUNITY PROBLEM-SOLVING. WITHOUT THE ACQUISITION OF LIFE SKILLS NEEDED BY YOUNG PEOPLE AND ADULTS, IT IS DOUBTFUL THE CITIZENS OF KENTUCKY WILL REACH THEIR FULL POTENTIAL AS BOTH INDIVIDUALS AND AS MEMBERS OF FAMILIES. WE APPROACH KENTUCKY'S CHALLENGES THROUGH AN INTEGRATED MODEL THAT INCLUDES A NEEDS ASSESSMENT CONDUCTED AT THE GRASSROOTS LEVEL THROUGH THE COOPERATIVE EXTENSION SERVICE, ADVISORY GROUPS, COUNCILS, AND COMMITTEES. ONCE IDENTIFIED AS PRIORITIES, SPECIFIC PROBLEMS AND NEEDS ARE ADDRESSED BY OUR RESEARCHERS AND EXTENSION SPECIALISTS. THE RESEARCH, DEVELOPMENTS, FINDINGS, AND TECHNOLOGIES ARE TRANSFERRED THROUGH TRADITIONAL AND INNOVATIVE MECHANISMS, INCLUDING EDUCATIONAL AND TRAINING PROGRAMS, TECHNOLOGY TRANSFER, RESEARCH REPORTS, AND PARTNERSHIPS WITH OTHER COLLEGES, UNIVERSITIES, AND STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS. WHETHER IT IS PRESERVING OUR RICH AGRICULTURAL TRADITION BY HELPING FARMERS, FOOD PROCESSORS, AND AGRIBUSINESS COPE WITH TECHNICAL ISSUES, REACHING GOALS, OR ENHANCING THE LIFE SKILLS OF FAMILIES, OUR RESEARCH, EDUCATION, AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS ARE HELPING SHAPE THE FUTURE OF KENTUCKY'S AGRICULTURE, FOOD SYSTEMS, AND COMMUNITIES AS WELL AS THE QUALITY OF LIFE OF ITS CITIZENS. CRITICAL ISSUES FOR RESEARCH AND EXTENSION LIFE SKILLS DEVELOPMENT DESCRIPTION: THIS CRITICAL ISSUE PROMOTES THE ACQUISITION OF LIFE SKILLS NEEDED BY YOUTH AND ADULTS TO REACH THEIR FULL POTENTIAL. ISSUES ABOUND IN EARLY CHILDHOOD DEVELOPMENT, YOUTH DEVELOPMENT, FAMILY WELL-BEING, ETHICS, CHARACTER EDUCATION, LIFE SKILLS, MONEY AND RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, RETIREMENT SAVINGS, SOCIAL ENTREPRENEURSHIP, COMMUNICATION AND INFORMATION DELIVERY, AND MORE. KCES WILL EXPAND EDUCATIONAL OUTREACH IN STEM/STEAM AREAS THAT WILL INCREASE ENROLLMENT OF LIMITED-RESOURCE FAMILIES AND COMMUNITIES WHO ARE AT OR BELOW THE POVERTY LEVEL AND WHO QUALIFY FOR SUPPORT SERVICES TERM: INTERMEDIATE SCIENCE EMPHASIS AREAS EDUCATION AND MULTICULTURAL ALLIANCES FAMILY <(>&<)> CONSUMER SCIENCES YOUTH DEVELOPMENT NUTRITION AND HEALTHY LIFESTYLES

NC A<(>&<)>T ENCOURAGES INNOVATIVE AND INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH NECESSARY TO ADVANCE AGRICULTURAL TECHNOLOGY, SOLVE THE PROBLEM OF FOOD INSECURITY AND SAVE THE ENVIRONMENT. CAES CONDUCTS RESEARCH ON THE UNIVERSITY FARM, AT THE CENTER FOR ENVIRONMENTAL FARMING SYSTEMS IN GOLDSBORO (CEFS); AT THE CENTER OF EXCELLENCE IN POST-HARVEST TECHNOLOGIES (CEPHT) IN KANNAPOLIS; AND ON CAMPUS IN LABORATORIES WHERE INVESTIGATIONS INCLUDE AGRICULTURAL ECONOMICS, ANIMAL SCIENCE, SOIL SCIENCE, PLANT SCIENCE, HUMAN NUTRITION, FOOD SCIENCE AND BIOENERGY. THUS, CAES ENGAGES IN CUTTING-EDGE RESEARCH AND PROMOTES THE APPLICATION OF INTER- AND TRANS-DISCIPLINARY INTEGRATIVE APPROACHES THAT INCLUDE THE OUTREACH OF EXTENSION TO INCREASE CRITICAL MASS AND IMPACT. TO MOVE FORWARD WITH THIS AIM WE ARE FOCUSING ON FOUR INTEGRATIVE CLUSTERS (PRIORITIES): (1) PLANT AND ANIMAL AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS; (2) FOOD SAFETY, NUTRITION AND HEALTH; (3) YOUTH, FAMILY AND COMMUNITY WELL-BEING; AND (4) ENVIRONMENTAL AND NATURALRESOURCES. SPECIFICALLY, RESEARCH AND EXTENSION AT NCA<(>&<)>T WILL CONTINUE TO OPEN DOORS AND MAKE AN IMPACT IN THE FOLLOWING WAYS: IMPROVING PLANT AND ANIMAL AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS: WITHIN THIS AREA, WE WILL WORK TO ADDRESS CROSS-CUTTING AND EMERGING ISSUES OF ANIMAL AND PLANT HEALTH AND PRODUCTION. IN ANIMAL SYSTEM, RESEARCHERS WILL STUDY THE EFFICIENCY OF DIFFERENT FEEDING SOURCES TO IMPROVE ANIMAL PRODUCTIVITY AND GUT HEALTH. IN PLANT SYSTEMS, THE FOCUS WILL BE IN SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE, ALTERNATIVE AND HIGH VALUE CROP PRODUCTION, SEASON EXTENSION, CLIMATE CHANGE ADAPTATION, VALUE ADDED AGRICULTURE, DIGITAL AGRICULTURE, SOIL HEALTH, PEST CONTROL, AGRO ECONOMICS. ENHANCING FOOD SAFETY, NUTRITION AND HEALTH: WITHIN THIS AREA, WE WILL WORK TO ADDRESS ISSUES OF HUMAN HEALTH, FOOD SAFETY AND HEALTHY LIVING HABITS. THE RESEARCH WILL FOCUS ON WHOLE GRAIN CEREALS, HUMAN HEALTH AND HUMAN NUTRITION, PROBIOTICS STRAINS, FOOD ALLERGY, FOOD PRODUCTION PROCESS, BIOACTIVE COMPOUNDS OF FOOD, POST-HARVEST TECHNOLOGY AND FOOD SECURITY. ENRICHING YOUTH, FAMILY AND COMMUNITY WELL-BEING: CAES RESEARCHERS ARE DEDICATED TO WORKING WITH NC'S MINORITY POPULATION, SOCIALLY DISADVANTAGED AND DISABLED GROWERS, ELDERLY POPULATION, YOUTH, AND CHILDREN TO IMPROVE THEIR LIFESTYLE. RESEARCHERS WILL FOCUS ON THE CHALLENGES OF ELDERLY POPULATION, TEXTILE AND FASHION DESIGN, HEALTHY EATING HABITS AND CHILDHOOD OBESITY. ENVIRONMENTAL AND NATURAL RESOURCES: IN THIS AREA WE WILL WORK TO PROTECT THE NATURAL ENVIRONMENT, PROVIDE SOLUTIONS FOR WASTE MANAGEMENT AND CONVENTIONAL ENERGY. CAES RESEARCHERS WILL INVESTIGATE AN ADVANCED BIOLOGICAL SYSTEM TO PRODUCE ALTERNATIVE ENERGY, TREAT THE AGRICULTURAL AND INDUSTRIAL WASTE, AND PROTECT AND IMPROVE WATER QUALITY. CAES RESEARCHERS WILL BE INVOLVED IN A MULTISTATE CLIMATE CHANGE PROJECT TO STUDY THE IMPACT OF CLIMATE CHANGE ON SOCIALLY DISADVANTAGED FARMERS AND COMMUNITIES OF COLOR. RESEARCHERS WILL BE DEVELOPING THE ADAPTATION AND MITIGATION SOLUTION TO IMPROVE AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCES, AND WILL BE PROPOSING POLICIES TO ADDRESS THE ISSUE OF ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE AND CLIMATE CHANGE.

negativeFlows.title: ALCORN STATE UNIVERSITY, FOUNDED IN 1871, IS AN 1890 HBCU LAND GRANT UNIVERSITY LOCATED IN LORMAN, MISSISSIPPI PROVIDING BROAD AGRICULTURE SERVICES TO HER SERVING MINORITY COMMUNITIES. ALCORN HAS PROGRAMS IN AGRICULTURE RESEARCH, EDUCATION AND EXTENSION. AGRICULTURE RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EDUCATION AT ALCORN BOASTS DIVERSE FIELDS SUCH AS AGRONOMY, PLANT BREEDING, PLANT PATHOLOGY, ENTOMOLOGY, MYCOLOGY, VIROLOGY, SOIL SCIENCE, ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCE, ANIMAL SCIENCE, PLANT BIOTECHNOLOGY, BIOFUELS AND BIOPROCESSING, AGRICULTURE ECONOMICS, AGRIBUSINESS AND AGRICULTURE MECHANICS AND ITS APPLICATIONS. THESE DISCIPLINES AT ALCORN'S AGRICULTURE RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EDUCATION PROGRAMS HAVE BEEN ESTABLISHED TO SERVE SMALL FARMERS, LIMITED RESOURCE FARMERS AND DISADVANTAGED FARMERS OF MISSISSIPPI. ANOTHER SIGNIFICANT COMPONENT ALCORN STATE'S AGRICULTURE RESEARCH ACTIVITY AIMS AT ENHANCING AWARENESS OF AGRICULTURE AND THE RECRUITMENT OF MINORITY YOUTH FROM HIGH SCHOOL AND COMMUNITY COLLEGE. THE AGRICULTURE PROGRAMS AT ALCORN STATE CONTRIBUTES TO WORKFORCE TRAINING AT DIFFERENCE LEVELS PREPARING A SIZEABLE NUMBER OF SKILLED AND TRAINED AGRICULTURE PROFESSIONALS ANNUALLY INTO THE AGRICULTURE WORKFORCE. THE PROPOSED WORK IS OUTLINED TO INCLUDE 1) SOIL AND WATER QUALITY DEGRADATION, COVER CROPS AND SOIL AND WATER DEGRADATION MITIGATION; 2) CROP, VEGETABLES AND FRUITS PRODUCTION, PROCESSING AND STORAGE; 3) NATIVE AND NOVEL BIOFUEL CROPS SUCH AS SWITCHGRASS AND MISCANTHUS AS BIOFUELS FOR BIOMASS PRODUCTION; 4) PLANTS AS FEED FOR ANIMAL CONSUMPTION AND ANIMAL NUTRITIONAL RESEARCH; 5) SOIL SURVEY AND CLIMATE CHANGE INVESTIGATION; 6) EVALUATION OF IRRIGATION AND NATURAL WATER MOVEMENT ON COVER CROP AND VEGETABLE CROP POTENTIAL TO INCREASE SOIL AND WATER QUALITY; 7) DEVELOP AND APPLY TRADITIONAL AND LATEST TECHNOLOGY FOR PLANT PESTS DIAGNOSIS AND MANAGEMENT; 8) EVALUATION OF NOVEL AND SPECIALTY CROPS FOR INTEGRATION INTO SMALL FARMERS' FARM OPERATION AND THEIR ECONOMIC IMPACTS ON SMALLFARM'S OPERATION; 9) ADOPTION AND APPLICATION OF NOVEL BIOTECHNOLOGY SUCH AS GENOME EDITING FOR CROP GENETIC IMPROVEMENT; 10) SMART AGRICULTURE AND APPLICATIONS OF ROBOTICS AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN BROAD AGRICULTURE PRODUCTIONS; 11) ANIMAL PRODUCTION, PHYSIOLOGY, GENETICS, ZOONOTIC DISEASE INVESTIGATION AND PUBLIC HEALTH EDUCATION; 12) DEMONSTRATION OF AGRICULTURE RESEARCH FOR SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY, ENGINEERING AND MATH (STEM) OUTREACH TO PREK-12 SCHOOLS AND COMMUNITY COLLEGES FOR WORKFORCE CULTIVATION; 13) PRESENT R ESEARCH FINDINGS AT LOCAL, REGIONAL, AND NATIONAL CONFERENCES; 14) PUBLISH RESEARCH RESULTS.

THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS AT PINE BLUFF (UAPB), SCHOOL OF AGRICULTURE, FISHERIES AND HUMAN SCIENCES HAS THREE ACADEMIC DEPARTMENTS, THE 1890 EXTENSION PROGRAM, THE 1890 RESEARCH PROGRAM, THE AQUACULTURE AND FISHERIES CENTER OF EXCELLENCE AND THE REGULATORY SCIENCE CENTER OF EXCELLENCE. RESEARCH FACULTY ARE INTEGRATED INTO THE ACADEMIC DEPARTMENTS. PERSONNEL WITH A MAJORITY EXTENSION APPOINTMENT ARE UNDER THE SUPERVISION OF THE ASSISTANT DEAN FOR EXTENSION. CONSISTENT WITH THE LAND GRANT MISSION, UAPB RESEARCH AND EXTENSION FACULTY HAVE A LONG HISTORY OF PROVIDING LEADERSHIP IN DEVELOPING AND DISSEMINATING INNOVATIVE PRACTICES AND EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES. HENCE, UAPB EXTENSION EDUCATORS DELIVER RESEARCHBASED EDUCATION TO THEIR CLIENTELE. OUR EXTENSION EDUCATORS EMPLOY DIVERSE EDUCATIONAL METHODS TO THEIR CLIENTELE, INCLUDING EDUCATIONAL FACETOFACE AND VIRTUAL FORUMS, LANDOWNER VISITS, INDIVIDUAL CONSULTATIONS, DEMONSTRATIONS, AND FIELD DAYS AND TOURS. ALTHOUGH THE INFORMATION IS READILYAVAILABLE IN THE DIGITAL AGE, UAPB REMAINS A DATA PROVIDER INDEPENDENT OF FINANCIAL OR PHILOSOPHICAL INTERESTS. THUS, THE PRIMARY CLIENTELE SERVED BY UAPBS EXTENSION PROGRAM ARE THE SOCIALLY DISADVANTAGED, LIMITED RESOURCE AND UNDERSERVED FARMERS, RURAL FAMILIES, UNDERSERVED AND VULNERABLE YOUTH, THE ARKANSAS AQUACULTURE INDUSTRY, AND INDIVIDUALS AND AGENCIES WITH AN INTEREST IN FISHERIES AND FISH HABITATS. THESE CLIENTELE ARE SERVED THROUGH FIVE CRITICAL ISSUES OUTLINED BELOW. ENVIRONMENT, ENERGY AND CLIMATE: ARKANSAS HAS AN ABUNDANCE OF NATURAL RESOURCES, INCLUDING 19 MILLION ACRES OF FORESTS, 122,312 MILES OF RIVERS AND STREAMS, AND MORE THAN 600,000 ACRES OF LAKES AND RESERVOIRS. ARKANSAS HAS APPROXIMATELY 13,639,300 ACRES OF AGRICULTURAL LAND. MANY AFRICAN AMERICANS DO NOT SEE THEIR FOREST LAND AS AN ASSET BUT AS A LIABILITY. THE UAPB SUSTAINABLE FORESTRY AND LAND RETENTION PROGRAM WILL HELP PRODUCERS IMPROVE THEIR FOREST LAND AND SEE IT AS AN ASSET, TO EDUCATE AND ASSIST WITH HEIR PROPERTY ISSUES, AND ADDRESS THE LACK OF GOVERNMENT TRUST. ADDITIONALLY, SOCIALLY DISADVANTAGED PRODUCERS ARE TAUGHT HOW TO USE SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL PRACTICES THAT KEEP SOILS, NUTRIENTS, AND PESTICIDES ON THEIR LAND AND PREVENT SOIL FROM SILTING AND POLLUTING STREAMS. ACCESS TO SAFE AND NUTRITIOUS FOOD: THE FOOD SAFETY MODERNIZATION ACT (FSMA) MADE FOOD SAFETY EDUCATION MANDATORY FOR LARGE FRESH FRUIT AND VEGETABLE PRODUCERS. UAPBS EXTENSION WILL PROVIDE GAP AND FSMA TRAINING REQUIRED TO OBTAIN CERTIFICATION AND WE WILL STRENGTHEN AND ESTABLISH INFRASTRUCTURE TO IMPROVE FOOD SAFETY AWARENESS AND PRACTICES AMONG THE LOCAL SMALL, MEDIUM, AND LARGE SIZED FARMING OPERATIONS. INCREASING OPPORTUNITIES FOR YOUTH, FAMILIES AND COMMUNITIES: UAPBS EXTENSION ACTIVITIES FOCUS ON INCREASING OPPORTUNITIES FOR YOUTH, FAMILIES, AND COMMUNITIES. THE PROJECT WILL TARGET THE FAMILY WITH THE DESIRE TO SERVETHE COMMUNITY AT LARGE. 4H, FAMILY AND CONSUMER SCIENCE, AQUACULTURE/FISHERIES, AGRICULTURE AND HUMAN SCIENCES, AND EXTENSION PROFESSIONALS WILL ADDRESS ISSUES THAT IMPACT YOUTH, FAMILIES, AND COMMUNITIES. EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING CURRICULA AND PROGRAMS THAT REINFORCE COLLABORATION WITH YOUTH AND COMMUNITY BUSINESSES WILL ENSURE A COMPETENT WORKFORCE FOR COMMUNITIES. AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION AND PROCESSING: CHALLENGES FACING THIS CRITICAL ISSUE INCLUDE PRODUCTION EFFICIENCY, ADEQUATE WATER, SOIL HEALTH, RESISTANT PESTS, CLIMATE, ENVIRONMENTAL CONCERNS, ENERGY, RISING PRODUCTION COSTS, AND FOOD SAFETY. AQUACULTURE/FISHERIES EXTENSION PROVIDES FISH DISEASE DIAGNOSTICS SERVICES WHICH SAVE FARMERS THOUSANDS OF DOLLARS PER YEAR. SPECIALTY CROP EXTENSION ACTIVITIES PRODUCE VIRUSINDEXED SWEET POTATO PLANTING MATERIALS FOR GROWERS AND DEVELOP VALUEADDED PRODUCTS SUCH AS SWEET POTATO WINES. TO MEET THE FINANCIAL PLANNING NEEDS OF THIS GROUP OF EXISTING AND BEGINNING PRODUCERS, THE UAPB SMALL FARM PROGRAM CONTINUES TO OFFER FARM FINANCIAL PLANNING AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO PRODUCERS. MOSTLY, THIS WILL BE THE ONLY FARM BUSINESS TRAINING THAT THESE PRODUCERS N OBTAIN WITHIN THE REGION.

ALABAMA AGRICULTURAL AND MECHANICAL UNIVERSITY (AAMU) CONDUCTS RESEARCH PROJECTS THAT MEET THE NEEDS OF THE CITIZENS OF ALABAMA AND THE NATION. TO FULFILL OUR OBLIGATIONS UNDER USDA-NIFA EVANS ALLEN ACT OF 1890 (SECTION 1445) FOR FISCAL YEAR 2023, THERE ARE SEVERAL APPROVED PROJECTS. BROADLY, RESEARCH AREAS OF INTERESTS ARE: FOOD SYSTEMS AND FOOD SAFETY; GLOBAL FOOD SECURITY AND HUNGER; NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY; HUMAN NUTRITION, WELL-BEING, HEALTH AND OBESITY; AND COMMUNITY AND REGIONAL PLANNING. FOOD SYSTEMS AND FOOD SAFETY: RESEARCH AND EXTENSION INTEGRATED ACTIVITIES ENHANCE FOOD SYSTEMS, FOOD SAFETY AND AGRICULTURAL BIOSEC URITY. THE GOAL OF THIS CRITICAL ISSUE IS TO DEVELOP TECHNOLOGY AND METHODS TO PROTECT AND ENHANCE THE SAFETY OF AGRICULTURE AND FOOD, REDUCE EPIDEMICS OF FOOD-BORNE ILLNESSES, AND TO DEVELOP THE KNOWLEDGE AND METHODOLOGIES FOR RAPID DETECTION OF THREAT AGENTS, IN CLUDING EXISTING AND EMERGING DISEASES OF PLANTS AND ANIMALS, RISK ASSESSMENT, AND FACILITY AND PERSONNEL SECURITY. GLOBAL FOOD SECURITY AND HUNGER: THE GOAL IS TO ENHANCE COMPETITIVENESS AND SUSTAINABILITY OF FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL INDUSTRIES IN ALABAMA THROUGH DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF BEST PRACTICES OR TECHNOLOGIES. THIS CRITICAL ISSUE ADDRESSES TWO BROADLY DEFINED PRIORITY AREAS; I) PLANT HEALTH AND PRODUCTION AND PLANT PRODUCTS, INCLUDING IMPROVED CROPPING SYSTEMS, PLANT BREEDING/GENOMICS, INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT, PRECISION AGRICULTURE, ALTERNATIVE SPECIALTY CROPS; AND II) ANIMAL HEALTH AND PRODUCTION, INCLUDING IMPROVED FOOD-ANIMAL SYSTEMS AND STOCKS. OF PARTICULAR INTEREST ARE PROGRAMS AND PROJECTS THAT INCLUDE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES AND THAT PRESENT INNOVATIVE SYNERGIES OF DISCIPLINES AND PERSPECTIVES. HUMAN NUTRITION, WELL-BEING, HEALTH AND OBESITY: OBESITY, DIABETES, HIGH BLOOD PRESSURE, AND VASCULAR ISSUES ARE MOSTLY CAUSED BY THE LACK OF NUTRIENTS, THE LACK OF EXERCISE, POOR LIFESTYLE CHOICES, AND STRESS OF THE INVOLVED INDIVIDUALS. AS A RESULT OF THE GROWING HEALTH CONCERNS FOR ALABAMA CITIZENS, THERE HAS BEEN A COMBINED EFFORT TO EDUCATE AND MOTIVATE CITIZENS THROUGHOUT THE STATE TO MAKE BETTER HEALTH DECISIONS. THE OBJECTIVE IS TO IMPROVE THE HEALTH OF ALABAMIANS, TARGETING LIMITED-RESOURCE FAMILIES, THROUGH CHRONIC DISEASE AWARENESS, PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, NUTRITION EDUCATION, HEALTH LITERACY AND ACCESS TO AND CONSUMPTION OF FRESH FRUITS AND VEGETABLES. NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY: THIS PROGRAM PLAN WILL GENERATE KNOWLEDGE TO MANAGE AGRICULTURAL AND NATURAL SYSTEMS IN THE FACE OF CLIMATE CHANGE AND THE NEED TO SUSTAIN NATURAL RESOURCES. SPECIFIC AREAS INCLUDE: CLIMATE-SMART SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS, ENERGY CONSERVATION AND UTILIZATION OF RENEWABLE ENERGY RESOURCES; UNDERSTANDING THE LAND-WATER INTERFACE; CONSEQUENCES AND SOLUTIONS OF GLOBAL CLIMATE CHANGE; WATER QUALITY AND QUANTITY, CARBON SEQUESTRATION, NATURAL SYSTEMS RESTORATION, SURFACE AND GROUND WATERCONSERVATION; MANAGEMENT OF AGRICULTURAL WASTE RESIDUE; SUSTAINABLE SOIL HEALTH ENHANCEMENT; SUSTAINABLE ECO- AND AGRI-TOURISM; RURAL-URBAN INTERFACE ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES; REMOTE SENSING AND PRECISION AGRICULTURE. COMMUNITY AND REGIONAL PLANNING: THIS AREA IS DESIGNED TO MAINTAIN THE INTEGRITY OF AGRICULTURAL LANDS THROUGH RURAL AND URBAN PLANNING PROGRAMS. APPROPRIATED FUNDS WILL BE USED FOR EXPENSES IN CONDUCTING RESEARCH TO INCLUDE FACULTY AND STAFF SALARIES, STUDENT SUPPORT, DISSEMINATION OF RESEARCH RESULTS, ADMINISTRATIVE PLANNING AND DIRECTION, EQUIPMENT PURCHASE AND MAINTENANCE, AND SUPPLIES PURCHASE (AMONG OTHER APPROVED SPENDING).

ALABAMAS RESEARCH AND EXTENSION SEEK TO ADDRESS SELECTED QUESTIONS THAT LEAD TO IDENTIFICATION OF CRITICAL ISSUES OF STRATEGIC IMPORTANCE. OUR PROGRAMS ARE THEREFORE FOCUSED ON THE FOLLOWING CRITICAL ISSUES: (1) GLOBAL FOOD SECURITY AND HUNGER; (2) NATURAL RESOURCES CONSERVATION AND MANAGEMENT, ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY AND CLIMATE CHANGE; (3) FOOD SYSTEM AND FOOD SAFETY; (4) HUMAN NUTRITION, WELL-BEING, HEALTH AND OBESITY; (5) SUSTAINABLE ENERGY; (6) COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT; AND (7) FAMILY, HOME AND 4-H AND YOUTH DEVELOPMENT. OUR PROGRAMS ARE DESIGNED TO PARTICULARLY ADDRESS THE ALABAMA BLACK BELT REGION AND HISTORICALLY DISADVANTAGED AND UNDERSERVED LIMITED RESOURCE PRODUCERS AND LAND OWNERS. SPECIFIC RESEARCH PROJECTS ARE THEREFORE FOCUSED ON:EFFICIENT WATER USE AND ADAPTATION TO CLIMATE VARIABILITY: A SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTION SOLUTION FOR HISTORICALLY DISADVANTAGED AND LIMITED RESOURCE FARMERS AND LANDOWNERS; SUSTAINABLE MEAT GOAT PRODUCTION SYSTEMS FOR LIMITED- RESOURCE PRODUCERS; SUSTAINABLE AND RELIABLE APPROACHES AND MARKETING STRATEGIES TO INCREASE YIELD OF VEGETABLES AND FRUITS FOR SOC IALLY DISADVANTAGED FARMERS IN ALABAMA; ALTERNATIVE POULTRY PRODUCTION: A SUSTAINABLE INTEGRATIVE POULTRY PRODUCTION MODEL FOR SMALL SCALE PRODUCERS; INTEGRATIVE APPROACHES TO OBESITY PREVENTION IN ALABAMA BLACK BELT COUNTIES; STRENGTHENING  PROGRAMS IN ORGANIC FARMING IN ALABAMA THROUGH RESEARCH AND EDUCATION; AND DEVELOPMENT AND EVALUATION OF INTEGRATIVE ALTERNATIVE ENERGY SOURCES FOR LIMITE D-RESOURCE FARMERS AND UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES IN ALABAMA.

negativeFlows.title: THROUGH THE INSTITUTE OF AGRICULTURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL RESEARCH, THE GOAL OF AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH AT TENNESSEE STATE UNIVERSITY IS TO CREATE AND COMMUNICATE NEW KNOWLEDGE IN THE AGRICULTURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCES. THROUGH OUR INNOVATIVE RESEARCH, WE ADDRESS THE NEEDS OF HUMANKIND, FOCUSING ON FINDING SOLUTIONS TO CHALLENGES FACED BY SOCIALLY AND ECONOMICALLY DISADVANTAGED GROUPS, AND CONTRIBUTING TO THE PROSPERITY OF THE CITIZENS OF TENNESSEE, THE NATION, AND THE WORLD. RESEARCH IN TENNESSEE STATE UNIVERSITY AGRICULTURE IS ORGANIZED TO ADDRESS THE CRITICAL ISSUES DESCRIBED BELOW. ENHANCING BIODIVERSITY AND ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY SAFEGUARDING AND ENHANCING THE NATURAL RESOURCE ENVIRONMENT HAS BECOME INCREASINGLY COMPLEX WITHIN ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL, RESOURCE AND PERSONAL CONTEXTS. THROUGH COLLABORATION AMONG RESEARCHERS, INDUSTRY, PRODUCERS, ENVIRONMENTAL GROUPS, AND GOVERNMENT, WE ARE HELPING PRESERVE A DIVERSE AND RESILIENT ENVIRONMENT FOR FUTURE GENERATIONS. ENRICHING OUR ECONOMY HELPING FARMS AND AGRICULTURE BUSINESSES BECOME MORE PROFITABLE AND INDIVIDUALS BECOME FINANCIALLY SECURE BOOSTS THE LOCAL, STATE, AND NATIONAL ECONOMIES. OUR PROGRAMS STRIVE TO STRENGTHEN THE ECONOMIC VIABILITY OF ALL FACETS OF AGRIBUSINESS, AND IMPROVE THE FINANCIAL LITERACY OF TENNESSEANS AND BEYOND SO THEY MAY BUILD AND PROTECT WEALTH FOR THEMSELVES AND FUTURE GENERATIONS. STRENGTHENING OUR HEALTH MAKING HEALTHY CHOICES IS IMPORTANT FOR HUMANS, ANIMALS, AND EVEN OUR PLANET. AS A LEADER IN NUTRITION, ANIMAL WELFARE, AND ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION, WE ARE WORKING TO UNDERSTAND HOW FOOD, PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, AND SOCIAL CONNECTIONS AFFECT OVERALL HEALTH. FROM FOOD SAFETY TO DISEASE PREVENTION AND MAINTENANCE TO THE STATE OF OUR ENVIRONMENT, THESE EFFORTS WILL HELP AMERICANS AND THE REST OF THE WORLD LEAD HEALTHIER LIVES FOR GENERATIONS TO COME. SUPPORTING FOOD, FIBER, AND ENERGY SYSTEMS SAFE, SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS THAT ARE SOCIALLY, ECONOMICALLY, AND ENVIRONMENTALLY RESPONSIBLE ARE KEY TO ENHANCING THE LIVES OF TENNESSEANS AND SUPPORTING A GROWING GLOBAL POPULATION. WE ARE EXPLORING WAYS TO DELIVER DISCOVERIES USING A SYSTEMS APPROACH TO AGRICULTURE PRODUCTIVITY THAT WILL PROVIDE CUSTOMIZABLE SOLUTIONS FOR PRODUCERS. UTILIZING FACULTY IN THE IN THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCES AND THE DEPARTMENT OF HUMAN SCIENCES, OUR RESE ARCH ADDRESSES THESE CRITICAL ISSUES THROUGH FACULTY GROUPS IN THE PLANT, ANIMAL, FOOD, AND HUMAN SCIENCES. THESE FACULTY-LED GROUPS FACILITATE THE IDENTIFICATION OF RESEARCH PRIORITIES WITHIN OUR CRITICAL ISSUES THAT ARE OF IMPORTANCE TO STAKEHOLDER GROUPS. WE CONDUCT RESEARCH IN AGRICULTURAL LEADERSHIP, EDUCATION AND COMMUNICATION THAT BRIDGES THE GAP BETWEEN THE GENERAL PUBLIC AND SCIE NTISTS WORKING TO SOLVE CURRENT AND EMERGING CHALLENGES RELATED TO SUSTAINABLY FEEDING AN EVER-GROWING POPULATION UNDER VARIOUS ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIETAL COMPLICATIONS. THIS RESEARCH ALSO BUILDS HUMAN AND INSTITUTIONAL CAPACITYNEEDED BY A VARIETY OF PUBLIC, PRIVATE, AND NONPROFIT EMPLOYERS IN THE AGRICULTURE SECTOR. ALSO STUDIED ARE WAYS TO DEVELOP HUMAN CAPACITY AND PROVIDE LEADERSHIP WITHIN COMMUNITIES. MUCH RESEARCH IN THIS AREA ALSO IDENTIFIES THE IMPACT OF TECHNOLOGY IN AGRICULTURAL EDUCATION, TECHNOLOGIES SUCH AS LECTURE-CAPTURE, DRONES, ROBOTS, EXTENDED REALITY, AND 360-DEGREE VIDEO. IN THE AREA OF AGRIBUSINESS, WE HAVE STRONG APPLIED-RESEARCH COMPONENT. WE PREPARE STUDENTS, FARMERS, AND STAKEHOLDERS IN THE USE OF ECONOMIC ANALYSIS AND MANAGEMENT COMPETENCIES TO TAKE ON THE CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES OF A DYNAMIC AGRI-FOOD SYSTEM. THE RESEARCH AREA EMPHASIZES PROMOTING, DEVELOPING, AND IMPROVING THE UTILIZATION OF RESEARCH, OUTREACH CAPABILITIES AND OPPORTUNITIES INVOLVING AGRIBUSINESSES, NATURAL RESOURCES AND COMMUNITIES. MAIN ACTIVITIES INCLUDE INVESTIGATIONS ON THE SOLE OR COMBINATION OF STRATEGIES FOR PROFITABILITY, AND THE SUSTAINABILITY, SURVIVAL, EFFICIENCY AND EFFECTIVENESS OF AGRICULTURALOPERATIONS, PARTICULARLY SMALL FARM OPERATIONS. ANTICIPATED RESULTS INCLUDE FARMERS' ADOPTION OF NEW CROPS; INVESTMENT FOR ALTERNATE INCOME DIVERSIFICATION STRATEGIES SUCH AS AGRITOURISM; ENHANCED KNOWLEDGE ON BENEFITS AND COSTS OF SUSTAINABLE PRACTICES; IMPROVED FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT AND MARKETING STRATEGIES AND DEVELOPMENT OF ENTREPRENEURSHIP SKILLS. RESEARCH IN ANIMAL SCIENCE IS DIRECTED AT IMPROVING LIVESTOCK PRODUCTION SYSTEMS BY GENERATING NOVEL FINDINGS THAT IMPACT ANIMAL WELL-BEING AND PERFORMANCE. SUB-DISCIPLINES SUCH AS GENETICS, HEALTH, NUTRITION, AND REPRODUCTIVE PHYSIOLOGY ARE INTEGRATED IN THE POULTRY AND RUMINANT LIVESTOCK RESEARCH ENDEAVORS. RESEARCH SPANS FROM BASIC, MOLECULAR MODELS TO APPLIED, WHOLE-ANIMAL SYSTEMS. PRIMARY END-USERS OF THE RESEARCH FINDINGS ARE LIVESTOCK PRODUCERS THAT ARE OFTEN SOCIALLY-DISADVANTAGED, RESOURCE-LIMITED OWNER-OPERATORS OF SMALL-SCALE ENTERPRISES. WE HAVE RESEARCH EFFORTS DIRECTED AT ELUCIDATING, MOLECULARLY AND FUNCTIONALLY, ANIMAL IMMUNE AND METABOLIC GENES. IN PARTICULAR, THOSE GENES THAT HAVE ANTIMICROBIAL ACTIVITIES AND THERAPEUTIC POTENTIAL. WE ARE USING COMBINED APPROACHES OF BIOINFORMATICS, GENETICS AND MOLECULAR BIOLOGY TO ELUCIDATE GENES OR GENE FAMILIES THAT ARE POTENTIALLY IMPORTANT IN ANIMAL HEALTH. SOME OF OUR ANIMAL PRODUCTION RESEARCH EMPHASIZES GOAT PRODUCTION. PROJECTS HAVE FOCUSED ON EVALUATING BREEDS TO GENERATE RECOMMENDATIONS ON HOW TO BEST USE THE DIFFERENT BREEDS FOR ENHANCED COMMERCIAL MEAT GOAT PRODUCTION. PRODUCERS HAVE MODIFIED THEIR GENETIC MANAGEMENT DECISION-MAKING LEADING TO IMPROVED HERD HEALTH, PERFORMANCE, AND ECONOMIC RETURN. IN POULTRY RESEARCH, THE CURRENT DEMAND FOR POULTRY AND POULTRY PRODUCTS REQUIRES A GAIN IN GENETIC POTENTIAL COMPLEMENTED WITH NUTRITIONAL REGIMENS THAT MAXIMIZE GROWTH AND IMPROVE EFFICIENCY OF FEED UTILIZATION. EXAMINATION OF OPTIMAL FEED COMPOSITION AND ALLOCATION IS OPTIMIZING SPECIFIC AMINO ACID CONCENTRATIONS. FEEDING THESE NEW LEVELS OF AMINO ACIDS WILLREDUCE FEEDING COST IN GUINEA FOWL PRODUCTION. OBESITY AND CHRONIC DISEASE PREVENTION IS ADDRESSED IN A PROGRAM THAT FOCUSES ON DEVELOPING A SMARTPHONE APPLICATION FOR WIC FAMILIES THAT WILL PROVIDE TOOLS TO MAKE USING THEIR BENEFITS EASIER WHILE PROVIDING HEALTHY RECIPES, NUTRITION EDUCATION, AND A GOAL TRACKING TOOL. HEALTHY EATING EXTENDS BEYOND LIMITING INTAKE OF FATS AND CALORIES. OUR NUTRITION RESEARCH IS AIMED AT UNDERSTANDING THE EFFECTS AND MECHANISMS OF FOOD-DERIVED BIOACTIVE COMPOUNDS AND THEIR ROLE IN COMBATING HUMAN CHRONIC DISEASES SUCH CANCER, OBESITY, AND DIABETES. RESEARCH WILL PROVIDE DIRECT EVIDENCE THAT HUMAN CHRONIC DISEASE CAN BE PREVENTED OR TREATED BY SELECTING FOODS HAVING HIGH LEVELS OF BIOACTIVE COMPOUNDS. FOOD IS A CORNERSTONE OF HUMAN EXISTENCE. ONGOING FOOD SCIENCE RESEARCH FOCUSES ON IMPROVING THE SAFETY, QUALITY, SHELF-LIFE, NUTRIENT PROFILE AND SENSORY ATTRIBUTES OF NOVEL FOOD INGREDIENTS, DEVELOPING AND VALIDATING ADVANCED AND INNOVATIVE TECHNOLOGIES FOR FOOD PROCESSING, MANUFACTURING, PACKAGING, AND SANITATION TO EFFECTIVELY REDUCE THE PRESENCE OF FOODBORNE PATHOGENS. ALSO, WE ARE DEVELOPING AND VALIDATING NOVEL STRATEGIES FOR THE EFFECTIVE CONTROL OF PERSISTENT RESERVOIRS OF FOODBORNE PATHOGENS AND MITIGATING ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE ACROSS THE FOOD CHAIN. FOR EXAMPLE, WE ARE LOOKING AT NEW WAYS TO REMOVE PATHOGENS FROM FOODS BY PRECISELY DEFINING THE LIMITS OF USING UV LIGHT AS A SUBSTITUTE FOR PASTEURIZATION TO ACHIEVE A SPECIFIED LETHALITY FOR DEADLY AGENTS IN FOODS. THIS PROCESS IS USING ADVANCED MATHEMATICAL AND COMPUTATIONAL MODELS. TECHNIQUES DEVELOPED IN THIS PROGRAM ARE ALSO BEING INVESTIGATED FOR POSSIBLE APPLICATION TO CONTROL THE SPREAD OF SARS-COV-2 AND OTHER VIRUSES. OTHER FOOD SCIENCE RESEARCH IS ADDRESSING THE PROBLEM OF CAMPYLOBACTER. THIS ORGANISM IS ONE OF THE MOST COMMON CAUSES OF DIARRHEAL ILLNESS IN THE UNITED STATES. DUE TO THE PREVALENCE OF CAMPYLOBACTER IN RAW CHICKEN PRODUCTS, ROUTINE AND RELIABLE MONITORING IS NECESSARY TO REDUCE ITS IMPACT UPON HUMAN HEALTH. THE METHOD BEING DEVELOPED IS INTENDED TO BE USED BY FOOD INDUSTRY AND REGULATORY TESTING LABORATORIES TO FACILITATE IMPROVED IDENTIFICATION OF CAMPYLOBACTER IN PROCESSING FACILITIES AND FINAL PRODUCTS. TO MITIGATE THE SPREAD OF ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANT CONTAMINANTS IN FOODS, WE HAVE RESEARCH THAT HAS GENERATED A SERIES OF HOTSPOT MAPS THAT WILL BE USED IN WORKSHOPS/WEBINARS TO ILLUSTRATE ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANT BACTERIAL COMMUNITIES ON PRODUCER'S FARMS. BY USING PERSONALIZED HOTSPOT MAPS THAT DISPLAY THE FREQUENCY OF ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANT BACTERIA IN FARMS, PRODUCERS WILL MAKE INFORMED DECISIONS ON THE USAGE OF ANTIBIOTICS IN THEIR LIVESTOCK, THUS REDUCING THE THREAT OF CONTAMINATION OF FOOD CROPS FERTILIZED WITH THE ANTIMICROBIAL-RESISTANT MANURE. RESEARCH IN NATURAL RESOURCES USES MULTIDISCIPLINE APPROACHES TO UNDERSTAND AND ATTENUATE PROBLEMS CAUSED BY CLIMATE CHANGE, LAND DE GRADATION, LOSS OF BIODIVERSITY, EMERGING CONTAMINANTS, AND ANTHROPOGENIC STRESSORS. TRADITIONAL AND CUTTING-EDGE CHEMISTRY METHODS ARE USED TO STUDY FATE OF CHEMICALS IN THE ENVIRONMENT, THE INTERACTION OF HAZARDOUS SUBSTANCES WITH SOILS AND WATER AND BIOGEOCHEMICAL CYCLES. BIOTECHNOLOGY IS USED TO STUDY AND RECTIFY HARMFUL ALGAL BLOOMS, WILDLIFE DISEASES AND PARASITES, MONITOR RARE AND ENDANGERED SPECIES, AND SOIL HEALTH. GEOGRAPHIC INFORMATION SYSTEMS, REMOTE SENSING AND ADVANCED STATISTICS ARE USED TO MODEL CLIMATE CHANGE ON A LARGE SCALE, WILDLIFE ECOSYSTEMS, DETERMINE THE VALUE OF ECOSYSTEM SERVICES AND DOCUMENT WATER RESOURCES. OUR RESEARCH TAKES PLACE IN CHEMISTRY LABS, COMPUTER LABS, RURAL AND URBAN SETTINGS AS WE SEEK TO SUSTAIN AND IMPROVE THE NATION'S NATURAL RESOURCES. IN ADDITION TO RESEARCH, WE BUILD INSTITUTIONAL CAPACITY AND STRENGTHEN OUR ENVIRONMENTAL PROGRAM THROUGH BRIDGE PROGRAMS, STUDENT RECRUITMENT AND MENTORING, STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIPS, AGGRESSIVE PROPOSAL WRITING AND CURRICULUM DEVELOPMENT. THE GOAL IS TO DEVELOP A STRONG DIVERSE WORKFORCE IN THE NATURAL RESOURCES THAT REFLECTS OUR NATION'S DEMOGRAPHICS. PLANT SCIENCE RESEARCH INCLUDES DIVERSE FIELDS IN AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION SYSTEMS WITH A FOCUS ON DEVELOPING AND APPLYING SCIENTIFIC AND BIOTECHNOLOGICAL PRINCIPLES TO IMPROVE CROP PRODUCTIVITY, REDUCE LOSSES FROM DISEASE, INSECT PESTS, AND TOXIC METAL STRESS; IN ADDITION TO IMPROVING THE UNDERSTANDING OF PLANT STRESS TOLERANCE MECHANISMS FOR HANDLING HEAT, DROUGHT AND OTHER STRESS FACTORS. RESEARCH INCLUDES THE DEVELOPMENT OF NEW TECHNOLOGIES FOR IMPROVING THE PRODUCTION OF RENEWABLE ENERGY SOURCES AND DEVELOPMENT OF ALTERNATIVE PRODUCTS FOR REDUCING PESTICIDE INPUTS IN CROP PRODUCTION SYSTEMS SUCH AS MICROBIAL-BASED PRODUCTS, PHEROMONES, AND PLANT OILS, PLANT GENETIC RESISTANCE AND BY BROADENING SOYBEAN GENETIC DIVERSITY FOR FUTURE GAINS IN CROP PRODUCTIVITY AND PREPAREDNESS FOR EMERGING NEW DISEASES AND INSECT PESTS. CROPS ADDRESSED ARE DIVERSE, INCLUDING VEGETABLES, CORN, SOYBEANS, ORNAMENTAL NURSERY CROPS, BIOENERGY CROPS, HYDROPONICS, AND URBAN AGRICULTURE. TECHNOLOGICAL CONTRIBUTIONS FROM THIS RESEARCH INCLUDE INCREASING CROP DIVERSITY BY INTRODUCING NEW EXOTIC VEGETABLES AND AMARANTH, DEVELOPING NEW CROP ALTERNATIVES LIKE HEMP, AND BIOFUEL ALTERNATIVES SUCH AS PERENNIAL SWITCHGRASS AND WINTER CANOLA THAT HAVE IMPROVED DIGESTIBILITY AND PROCESSING, AND DEVELOPING NEW PLANTS TOLERANT TO HEAT STRESS. OTHER RESEARCH ACTIVITIES ON BEST CROP MANAGEMENT PRACTICES, NITROGEN APPLICATION RATES TO ENHANCE YIELD AND FEEDSTOCK CHARACTERISTICS, THE BEST WINTER CANOLA VARIETIES AND NITROGEN RATES FOR TENNESSEE DELIVER SERVICES OF VALUE TO SOCIETY. AN OVERALL LACK OF CROP DIVERSITY IN THE AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS OF THE SOUTHEASTERN UNITED STATES INCREASES THE THREATS OF DISEASE EPIDEMICS, INSECT PEST OUTBREAKS OR RISKS OF CROP FAILURE DUE TO ABIOTIC STRESSES. IT IS IMPORTANT TO DEVELOP ALTERNATIVE CROPS FOR PRODUCTIVE SYSTEMS. RESEARCH TO ADDRESS THIS ISSUE HAS PRODUCED THE RELEASE OF TWO GRAIN AMARANTH VARIETIES AND THE RELEASE OF TWO GRAIN LEGUME VARIETIES. THESE ALTERNATIVE CROPS GIVE PRODUCERS OPTIONS IN SELECTING PRODUCTION MARKETS. ANOTHER PROGRAM LEADING TO CROP DIVERSITY IS EXAMINING THE ROLE OF SWEET SORGHUM AS A POTENTIAL DEDICATED US BIOFUEL CROP. THIS PROGRAM IS ESTABLISHING INNOVATIVE PROTOCOLS FOR SWEET SORGHUM GENETIC ENHANCEMENT. AS MORE KNOWLEDGE IS GAINED ABOUT THE INTERCONNECTEDNESS OF HUMAN IMPACTS ON THE EARTH, THE ROLE OF ANTIBIOTIC CONTAMINATION ON SOIL HEALTH IS BEING EXAMINED. MICRONUTRIENT DEFICIENCY IS A MAJOR CONCERN IN THE PRODUCTION OF SOME CROPS, SOME OF OUR RESEARCH WILL SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVE THE UNDERSTANDING THE BIOGEOCHEMICAL CYCLING OF MICRONUTRIENTS IN THE PRESENCE OF ANTIBIOTICS. THREATS FROM DISEASE AND INSECT PESTS ARE BEING ADDRESSED IN A NUMBER OF RESEARCH PROGRAMS. PLANT DISEASE IS A MAJOR THREAT TO GLOBAL FOOD PRODUCTION COSTING THE US ECONOMY AN ESTIMATED $33 BILLION ANNUALLY IN YIELD LOSS. WE HAVE RESEARCH THAT IS FOCUSED ON UNEARTHING THE MOLECULAR SECRETS OF PLANT-BACTERIAL INTERACTIONS THAT RESULT IN TWO IMPORTANT DISEASES OF VEGETABLES - BACTERIAL SOFT ROT OF ALL VEGETABLES AND BACTERIAL WILT OF CUCURBITS CROPS. RESEARCH HAS IDENTIFIED ACCESSIONS RESISTANT TO WILT DISEASE AND WHICH CAN BE EMPLOYED IN A BREEDING PROGRAM FOR RESISTANCE CULTIVARS. OTHER DISEASE RESEARCH IS EXAMINING THE USE OF BIOCONTROL AGENTS FOR DISEASE MANAGEMENT. THESE ALTERNATIVES TO CHEMICAL FUNGICIDES WILL PROVIDE TOOLS FOR DISEASE MANAGEMENT IN VEGETABLE PRODUCTION ESPECIALLY IN ORGANIC FARMING AND REDUCE USAGE OF TOXIC CHEMICALS IN CONVENTIONAL FARMING. INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT (IPM) OF INSECT PESTS IS A HOLISTIC APPROACH TO SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE THAT FOCUSES ON MANAGING PESTS THROUGH A COMBINATION OF CULTURAL, PHYSICAL, BIOLOGICAL AND CHEMICAL METHODS. IPM IS A CROP PROTECTION PRACTICE THAT IS COST EFFECTIVE, ENVIRONMENTALLY SOUND AND SOCIALLY ACCEPTABLE. TO FULFILL THIS NEED, WE CONDUCT RESEARCH FOCUSED ON CONDUCTING APPLIED RESEARCH EXPERIMENTS AND EDUCATING STAKEHOLDERS ON IPM THROUGH TRAINING AND PUBLICATIONS. IN-SERVICE TRAINING PROGRAMS FOR EXTENSION AGENTS AND IPM WORKSHOPS FOR OTHER STAKEHOLDERS ARE CONDUCTED ON STATE-WIDE BASIS IN EAST, MIDDLE AND WEST TENNESSEE REGIONS. IN OTHER INSECT RESEARCH, JAPANESE MAPLE SCALE RESEARCH, TIMED APPLICATIONS OF GROWTH REGULATORS AND ANNUAL MANAGEMENT PLANS DEVELOPED AT THE TSU NURSERY RESEARCH CENTER HAVE BEEN ADOPTED BY TENNESSEE GROWERS, REDUCING THE NUMBER OF REJECTED SHIPMENTS AND CULLED TREES. INVASIVE INSECTS ARE A MAJOR CONCERN IN NURSERY PRODUCTION. OUR RESEARCH IS PRODUCING DATA FOR NEW PESTICIDE REGULATIONS FOR FIRE ANT, JAPANESE BEETLE AND OTHER IMPORTANT INSECTS THAT ARE REDUCING WORKER EXPOSURE RISK, SAVING PRODUCERS TIME, AND OVERALL REDUCING THE COST OF PRODUCTION. MORE PRODUCER SAVINGS ARE EXPECTED WITH NEW PROTOCOLS UNDER DEVELOPMENT. SUSTAINABILITY RESEARCH WILL LEAD TO NEW PRACTICES THAT RESULTS IN REDUCTION OF INPUTS (PESTICIDES, FERTILIZER, WATER, LABOR, ETC.) IN THE NURSERY PRODUCTION SYSTEM, THUS ENHANCING THE SUSTAINABILITY OF THE INDUSTRY, IMPROVING OUR ENVIRONMENT, REDUCING PRODUCTION COSTS FOR GROWERS, IMPROVING CROP QUALITY, AND BROADENING THE MARKET FOR TENNESSEE GREEN INDUSTRY PRODUCTS. TO ADDRESS THE WELL-BEING AND HEALTH OF INDIVIDUALS, FAMILIES AND COMMUNITIES, RESEARCH IN FAMILY AND CONSUMER SCIENCES IS FOCUSED ON IMPROVING THE LIVES OF OUR STAKEHOLDERS THROUGH FCS EDUCATION, LEADERSHIP AND COMMUNICATION TO IMPROVE NOT ONLY THEIR HEALTH AND W ELL-BEING, BUT ALSO THEIR RELATIONSHIPS AND RESOURCES. THIS GROUP IS CONTINUING TO FOCUS ON EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS, LIVING WITH CHRONIC DISEASES, FOOD SECURITY VIA FOOD RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, AND OF COURSE, MITIGATING THE EFFECTS OF COVID-19 AS WE LIVE THROUGH THE P ANDEMIC. TSU AGRICULTURE IS PROUD OF THE RESEARCH CONDUCTED BY OUR FACULTY AND STAFF AS WE CONTINUE TO ADDRESS ISSUES THAT ARE CRITICAL TO THE WELFARE OF OUR STAKEHOLDERS, AND CONTRIBUTING TO THE PROSPERITY OF THE CITIZENS OF TENNESSEE, THE NATION, AND THE WORLD. WE LOOK FORWARD TO CONTINUING TO FULFILL OUR UNIQUE ROLE AS AN HBCU LAND-GRANT INSTITUTION IN TENNESSEE AND TO CONTINUED GROWTH AND SUCCESS.

VIRGINIA STATE UNIVERSITY'S (VSU) AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH STATION (ARS) GENERATES SCIENTIFIC INFORMATION DESIGNED TO EXPAND KNOWLEDGE THAT WILL HELP SMALL, PART-TIME AND LIMITED-RESOURCE FARMERS BE PROFITABLE. THE RESEARCH FOCUS INCLUDES DEVELOPING PRODUCTION SYSTEMS THAT CONSERVE NATURAL RESOURCES, IMPROVING THE SUSTAINABILITY AND PROFITABILITY OF INDOOR AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION, DEVELOPING SUSTAINABLE PEST MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS FOR SMALL-SCALE AGRICULTURE AND IDENTIFYING NOVEL GENES THAT CAN BE USED TO IMPROVE CROP TOLERANCES TO ENVIRONMENTAL STRESSES. THE RESEARCH ALSO GENERATES SCIENTIFIC INFORMATION THAT IMPROVES THE PROFITABILITY AND HEALTH OF SMALL RUMINANTS. SCIENTISTS AT ARS WORK TO DEVELOP A RESILIENT FARMING SYSTEM THAT CAN COPE WITH THE ADVERSE IMPACTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE, COMPETITIVE AND SUSTAINABLE SMALL-SCALE AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS, AND BIO-BASED ENERGY PRODUCTION SYSTEMS. THEY FURTHER AIM TO IMPROVE FOOD SAFETY AND QUALITY, AND TO GENERATE SCIENTIFIC INFORMATION ON VALUE-ADDED PLANT AND ANIMAL PRODUCTS TO IMPROVE THE PROFITABILITY OF FARMS. RESEARCH IS CONDUCTED ON CAMPUS AND AT A NEARBY VSU FARM TO ADDRESS THE FOLLOWING CRITICAL ISSUES: 1: AGRICULTURAL VIABILITY, PROFITABILITY AND SUSTAINABILITY O DEVELOP LOW-INPUT AND PROFITABLE INDOOR AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION SYSTEMS O IMPROVE THE SUSTAINABILITY AND PROFITABILITY OF SMALL RUMINANT PRODUCTION 2: BIOTECHNOLOGY, BIOMATERIALS, AND BIOENERGY O IDENTIFY NOVEL GENES THAT CAN BE USED TO IMPROVE CROP TOLERANCES TO ENVIRONMENTAL STRESSES, ESPECIALLY DROUGHT, HEAT AND METAL TOXICITY O USE GENETIC AND GENOME APPROACHES FOR BREEDING NEW CROPS TO ADDRESS GLOBAL CLIMATE CHANGE. 3: NATURAL RESOURCES, ENVIRONMENT AND CLIMATE CHANGE O DEVELOP A RESILIENT FARMING SYSTEM THAT CAN COPE WITH THE ADVERSE IMPACTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE O MINIMIZE THE EFFECTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE ON LOW INCOME COMMUNITIES

NCA<(>&<)>T ENCOURAGES INNOVATIVE AND INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH NECESSARY TO ADVANCE AGRICULTURAL TECHNOLOGY INCLUDING, SOLVE THE P ROBLEM OF FOOD INSECURITY AND SAVE THE ENVIRONMENT. CAES USES DIGITAL AND PRECISION INSTRUMENTS ALONG WITH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES TO CONDUCT CLIMATE SMART RESEARCH ON THE UNIVERSITY FARM, AT THE CENTER FOR ENVIRONMENTAL FARMING SYSTEMS IN GOLDSBORO (CEFS); AT THE CENTER OF EXCELLENCE IN POST-HARVEST TECHNOLOGIES (CEPHT) IN KANNAPOLIS; AND ON CAMPUS IN LABORATORIES WHERE INVESTIGATIONS INCLUDE AGRICULTURAL ECONOMICS, ANIMAL SCIENCE, SOIL SCIENCE, PLANT SCIENCE, HUMAN NUTRITION, FOOD SCIENCE AND BIOENERGY. THUS, CAES ENGAGES IN CUTTING-EDGE RESEARCH AND PROMOTES THE APPLICATION OF INTER-AND-TRANS-DISCIPLINARY INTEGRATIVE APPROACHES THAT INCLUDE THE OUTREACH OF EXTENSION TO INCREASE CRITICAL MASS AND IMPACT. TO MOVE FORWARD WITH THIS AIM WE ARE FOCUSING ON FOUR INTEGRATIVE CLUSTERS (PRIORITIES): PLANT AND ANIMAL AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS; FOOD SAFETY, NUTRITION, AND HEALTH; YOUTH, FAMILY AND COMMUNITY WELL-BEING; AND ENVIRONMENTAL AND NATURAL RESOURCES. SPECIFICALLY, RESEARCH AND EXTENSION AT NCA<(>&<)>T WILL CONTINUE TO OPEN DOORS AND MAKE AN IMPACT IN THE FOLLOWING WAYS: IMPROVING PLANT AND ANIMAL AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS: WITHIN THIS AREA, WE WILL WORK TO ADDRESS CROSSCUTTING AND EMERGING ISSUES OF ANIMAL AND PLANT HEALTH AND PRODUCTION. IN ANIMAL SYSTEMS, RESEARCHERS WILL STUDY THE EFFICIENCY OF DIFFERENT FEEDING SOURCES TO IMPROVE ANIMAL PRODUCTIVITY AND GUT HEALTH. ALSO, RESEARCHERS WILL STUDY TO FIND THE SOLUTION FOR VIRAL, BACTERIAL, AND PARASITIC EFFECTS IN ANIMALS AND POULTRY. IN PLANT SYSTEMS, THE FOCUS WILL BE ON SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE, ALTERNATIVE AND HIGH VALUE CROP PRODUCTION, SEASON EXTENSION, CLIMATE CHANGE ADAPTATION, VALUE ADDED AGRICULTURE, DIGITAL AGRICULTURE, SOIL HEALTH, PEST CONTROL, AND AGRO ECONOMICS. ENHANCING FOOD SAFETY, NUTRITION AND HEALTH: WITHIN THIS AREA BOTH RESEARCHERS WILL WORK TO ADDRESS THE ISSUE OF HUMAN HEALTH, FOOD SAFETY AND HEALTHY LIVING HABITS. THE RESEARCH WILL FOCUS ON WHOLE GRAIN CEREALS, HUMAN HEALTH AND HUMAN NUTRITION, PROBIOTICS STRAINS, FOOD ALLERGY, FOOD PRODUCTION PROCESS, BIOACTIVE COMPOUNDS OF FOOD, POST-HARVEST TECHNOLOGY AND FOOD SECURITY. ENRICHING YOUTH, FAMILY AND COMMUNITY WELL-BEING: CAES RESEARCHERS ARE DEDICATED TO WORKING WITH NC'S MINORITY POPULATION, SOCIALLY DISADVANTAGED AND DISABLED GROWERS, ELDERLY POPULATION, YOUTH, AND CHILDREN TO IMPROVE THEIR LIFESTYLE. RESEARCHERS WILL FOCUS ON THE CHALLENGES OF ELDERLY POPULATION, TEXTILE AND FASHION DESIGN, HEALTHY EATING HABITS, EARLY CHILDHOOD DEVELOPMENT AND CHILDHOOD OBESITY. ENVIRONMENTAL AND NATURAL RESOURCES: IN THIS AREA WE WILL WORK TO PROTECT THE NATURAL ENVIRONMENT, PROVIDE THE SOLUTION FOR WASTE MANAGEMENT AND CONVENTIONAL ENERGY. CAES RESEARCHERS WILL INVESTIGATE AN ADVANCED BIOLOGICAL SYSTEM TO PRODUCE ALTERNATIVE ENERGY, TREAT AGRICULTURAL AND INDUSTRIAL WASTE, AND PROTECT AND IMPROVE WATER QUALITY. CAES RESEARCHERS WILL BE INVOLVED IN A MULTISTATE CLIMATE CHANGE PROJECT TO STUDY THE IMPACT OF CLIMATE CHANGE ON SOCIALLY DISADVANTAGED FARMERS AND COMMUNITIES OF COLOR. RESEARCHERS WILL DEVELOP ADAPTATION AND MITIGATION SOLUTIONS TO IMPROVE AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCES AND WILL PROPOSE POLICIES TO ADDRESS THE ISSUE OF ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE AND CLIMATE CHANGE. SUBRECIPIENT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE COLLABORATING WITH THE UNIVERSITY OF NORTH CAROLINA AT GREENSBORO TO UNDERSTAND THE PHYSIOLOGICAL AND MOLECULAR RESPONSES TO DROUGHT STRESS OF INDIGENOUS VEGETABLES WITH UNTAPPED POTENTIAL FOR NUTRITION, HEALTH, AND FOOD SECURITY IN THE FACE OF GLOBAL CHANGE. CAES RESEARCHERS WORK TOGETHER WITH COOPERATIVE EXTENSION TO SHARE THE RESEARCH OUTCOMES TO TARGETED POPULATIONS AS WELL AS DISSEMINATE OUTCOMES THROUGH CONFERENCE PRESENTATIONS AND PUBLICATIONS.
