positiveFlows.title: MISSOURI IS WELL-KNOWN FOR THE DIVERSITY OF ITS NATURAL RESOURCES THAT ARE ESSENTIAL TO THE ENVIRONMENTAL AND ECONOMIC VITALITY OF THE STATE. THE QUALITY OF LIFE OF THE STATE'S CITIZENS ALSO DEPENDS ON THE HEALTH OF ITS NATURAL RESOURCES AND THE SURROUNDING ENVIRONMENT, PARTICULARLY THAT OF THE AIR, LAND/SOIL, AND WATER RESOURCES. HOWEVER, THESE RESOURCES AND THE ENVIRONMENT ARE EXPERIENCING INCREASED PRESSURE DUE TO THE DOMINANCE OF INPUT (E.G., SYNTHETIC FERTILIZERS, TILLAGE, PESTICIDES)-DEPENDENT, HIGHLY SPECIALIZED CROP AND LIVESTOCK PRODUCTION SYSTEMS COMBINED WITH CLIMATE CHANGE-RELATED STRESSORS (E.G., RECORD SETTING HIGH AND LOW TEMPERATURES, FLOODING, AND DROUGHTS) - ALL OF WHICH HAVE POSED A SIGNIFICANT THREAT TO THE SUSTAINABLE PROVISION OF GOODS (E.G., FOOD PRODUCTION AND FOOD SAFETY) AND SERVICES (E.G., CLEAN AIR AND WATER) FOR THE MISSOURIANS. IN ALIGNMENT WITH THE USDA-NIFA'S RESEARCH PRIORITIES, LINCOLN UNIVERSITY'S COOPERATIVE RESEARCH (LUCR) PROGRAM HAS BEEN CONDUCTING RESEARCH IN THE FOLLOWING AREAS: 1) ANIMAL SCIENCE, 2) SOIL HEALTH AND CROP SCIENCES, 3) FOOD NUTRITION AND SAFETY, 4) NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, AND 5) SOCIAL-ECONOMICS. LUCR AIMS TO CONTINUE DEVELOPING IMPACTFUL, INNOVATIVE, AND MULTIDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH PROGRAMS THAT EFFECTIVELY ADDRESS EMERGING AND CRITICAL ISSUES FACING MISSOURI'S NATURAL RESOURCES, AGRICULTURAL INDUSTRY, AND RURAL COMMUNITIES AS WELL AS STRENGTHEN LINCOLN UNIVERSITY'S CAPACITY TO BETTER ADDRESS THE NEEDS OF MISSOURI FARMERS AND RANCHERS. LUCR FACULTY MEMBERS HAVE BEEN CONTRIBUTING TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF CLIMATE-RESILIENT AGRICULTURAL AND FOOD SYSTEMS FOR SUSTAINING PRODUCTION, ENHANCING ECOSYSTEM HEALTH, AND SAFEGUARDING HUMAN HEALTH AND QUALITY OF LIFE FOR MISSOURI RESIDENTS. THE LUCR PROGRAM AND ITS MULTIFACETED RESEARCH PROJECTS SPECIFICALLY TARGET THOSE WHO HAVE BEEN HISTORICALLY UNDERSERVED, WHILE ALSO CONTRIBUTING TO THE DIVERSITY OF THE NATION'S FUTURE STEM-AGRICULTURAL WORKFORCE. OF THE SIX CRITICAL ISSUES IDENTIFIED, LUCR CAPACITY RESEARCH EFFORTS ARE PRIMARILY FOCUSED ON THE FOLLOWING THREE AREAS: 1) SUSTAINABLE AND RESILIENT AGRICULTURE SYSTEMS, 2) ENVIRONMENTAL AND NATURAL RESOURCES, AND 3) HEALTH AND HEALTHY FUTURES. UNDER THE CRITICAL ISSUE OF ENVIRONMENT AND NATURAL RESOURCES, LUCR CURRENT CAPACITY RESEARCH PROJECTS THAT HAVE BEEN INITIATED AND APPROVED BY NIFA ARE FOCUSED ON THE AREAS OF CLIMATE CHANGE IMPACTS, SOIL HEALTH AND REGENERATIVE AGRICULTURE, AGROFORESTRY, RENEWABLE BIOENERGY, AND GIS/REMOTE SENSING TECHNOLOGY APPLICATIONS. ONGOING CAPACITY RESEARCH PROJECTS UNDER THE CRITICAL ISSUE OF SUSTAINABLE AND RESILIENT AGRICULTURE SYSTEMS ARE FOCUSED ON THE FOLLOWING AREAS: SMALL RUMINANT (SHEEP/GOAT) BREEDING, PRODUCTIVE PHYSIOLOGY, GRAZING MANA GEMENT, POULTRY OPERATION, AQUACULTURE, HYDROPONIC OPERATION, INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT, SPECIALTY CROPS AND VALUE-ADDED PRODUCTS, EMERGENT VEGETABLE DISEASE CONTROL, AND ORGANIC FARMING. CAPACITY RESEARCH PROJECTS UNDER THE CRITICAL ISSUE OF HEALTH AND HEALTHY FUTURES ARE CURRENTLY FOCUSED ON THE AREAS OF SENSOR DEVELOPMENT FOR DETECTION OF FOODBORNE PATHOGENS, DRINKING WATER QUALITY AND SAFETY, AND EMERGING ENVIRONMENTAL CONTAMINANTS. THE OVERALL GOAL OF CAPACITY RESEARCH EFFORTS IN THE LUCR PROGRAM IS TO HELP FARMERS AND RURAL COMMUNITIES - ESPECIALLY SMALL FARMERS, RANCHERS, AND FOREST LANDOWNERS - ADOPT CLIMATE-SMART MANAGEMENT PRACTICES FOR SUSTAINABILITY AND RESILIENCE OF AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCES TO WITHSTAND INCREASINGLY VARIABLE WEATHER CONDITIONS, PROMOTE ENVIRONMENTAL AWARENESS AND ECOSYSTEM HEALTH, AND PROTECT HUMAN HEALTH FROM FOOD AND DRINKING WATER CONTAMINATION. CONTINUED FINANCIAL SUPPORT FROM BOTH NIFA AND THE STATE OF MISSOURI IS THEREFORE CRITICAL TO STRENGTHEN THE RESEARCH CAPACITY OF LINCOLN UNIVERSITY TO BE ABLE TO ADDRESS THE NEEDS OF MISSOURI'S FARMERS AND RANCHERS, ESPECIALLY THOSE WHO HAVE BEEN HISTORICALLY MARGINALIZED AND UNDERSERVED.

THE EVANS ALLEN (EA) PROGRAM AT CENTRAL STATE UNIVERSITY (CSU), ALSO KNOWN AS THE AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM (ARDP), FOCUSES ON CRITICAL ISSUES WHICH ARE ALSO IDENTIFIED AND REFLECTED IN THE APPROVED 2024 PLAN OF WORK (POW). THESE ISSUES ARE WELL ALIGNED WITH THE USDA'S STRATEGIC GOALS. THE PLAN ADDRESSES FOUR CRITICAL AREAS, INCLUDING: (I)PLANT AND ANIMAL SYSTEMS, (II) FOOD NUTRITION AND HEALTH SYSTEMS (FNH); (III) NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL SYSTEMS, AND (IV) ADVANCED TECHNOLOGIES AND COMMERCIALIZATION SYSTEMS. TO HELP ADDRESS THESE CRITICAL AREAS, 12 FACULTY MEMBERS PROVIDE LEADERSHIP THROUGH NIFA-APPROVED RESEARCH PROJECTS. THESE ACTIVE PROJECTS FURTHER CONTRIBUTE TO ENSURE A SAFE FOOD SUPPLY, IMPROVE NUTRITION OUTCOMES, AND THE OVERALL GROWTH OF THE AGRICULTURAL SECTOR IN OHIO AND BEYOND. WITHIN THE SCOPE OF THIS PLAN, CSU ALSO SUPPORTS AND TRAINS MINORITY UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS WHO RECEIVE UNIQUE EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES, WHILE ARE ALSO BEING PREPARED TO EFFECTIVELY ENGAGE IN THE MUCH-NEEDED WORKFORCE THAT CAN TACKLE CURRENT CHALLENGES IN FOOD, AGRICULTURAL, AND NATURAL RESOURCES FACED BY OUR COUNTRY AND THE WORLD. AS GRADUATE PROGRAMS CONTINUE DEVELOPING AT CSU, RESEARCH ACTIVITIES ARE SUPPORTED BY EA PROGRAM BY THE INCLUSION OF UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS, R ESEARCH ASSISTANTS, AND POST-DOCTORAL STUDENT HIRES. IN FACT, POSTDOCTORAL STUDENTS (RESEARCHERS) SIGNIFICANTLY ASSIST OUR RESEARCH FACULTY IN ADVANCING RESEARCH RELATED TO SUSTAINABLE FARMING PRACTICES, CARBON SEQUESTRATION, IMPROVED CROP VARIETIES, GENOMIC AND GENETIC ENGINEERING STUDIES FOR IMPROVING POLLINATOR HEALTH, AFFORDABLE TECHNOLOGIES FOR SMALL AND MEDIUM-SCALE FARMERS, FOOD SAFETY AND SECURITY, AND NUTRITIONAL SCIENCES THAT ADDRESS USDA'S PRIORITIES. FACULTY AND STUDENTS ALSO ADDRESS RESEARCH RELATED TO FOREST FARMING AND URBAN FORESTRY AIMED AT IMPROVING THE ECONOMY FROM TIMBER-BASED AND NON-TIMBER-BASED FOREST PRODUCTS TO ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY IN URBAN FOREST LANDSCAPES IN OHIO. THE EA PROGRAM AT CSU IS ALSO DESIGNED TO PROVIDE SEED FUNDING FOR ACADEMIC FACULTY TO ADDRESS EMERGING AGRICULTURAL ISSUES OR SUPPORT EXISTING RESEARCH PROGRAMS, EITHER DURING THE SUMMER OR PARTIALLY, ALL YEAR ROUND. THESE NEW AND/OR COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH PROJECTS, THROUGH THE INCLUSION OF VARIOUS COLLEGES, DIRECTLY FOCUS ON NIFA'S STRATEGIC GOALS. AS THE YOUNGEST 1890 LAND-GRANT INSTITUTION, CSU CONTINUES BUILDING THE NEEDED RESEARCH CAPACITY AND INFRASTRUCTURE THROUGH ITS EA PROGRAM. IN FACT, CSU IS CURRENTLY ERECTING ITS RESEARCH AND DEMONSTRATION COMPLEX(RDC), WHICH PHYSICAL AND HUMAN RESOURCES WILL SIGNIFICANTLY CONTRIBUTE TO ADVANCE THE UNIVERSITY'S PLAN OF WORK, AND ASSOCIATED USDA'S STRATEGIC GOALS. THE RDC WILL CONCENTRATE EFFORTS ON DRIVING INNOVATION IN CLIMATE-SMART AGRICULTURE, PROMOTING EQUITY AND OPPORTUNITY, ENHANCING FOOD AND NUTRITION SECURITY, AND TRAINING AND ENGAGING STUDENTS TO BECOME THE FUTURE WORKFORCE TO MEET CURRENT AND FUTURE CHALLENGES IN AGRICULTURE. THE RDC WILL PROVIDE FACULTY WITH STATE-OF-THE-ART RESEARCH FACILITIES, EQUIPPED WITH ADVANCED INSTRUMENTATION AND SPECIALIZED LABORATORIES FOR CUTTING-EDGE RESEARCH. THESE ENHANCED CAPABILITIES WILL IN TUM ALLOW CSU FACULTY TO BECOME MORE COMPETITIVE, INNOVATIVE, AND RESOURCEFUL IN BRINGING ADDITIONAL RESOURCES (E.G. EXTRAMURAL FUNDING), STRATEGICALLY COLLABORATE WITH DOMESTIC AND INTERNATIONAL PARTNERS, AND PROVIDE INNOVATIVE SOLUTIONS IN SUPPORT OF REGIONAL AND NATIONAL ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, AND GLOBAL FOOD SECURITY. THE EA PROGRAM AT CSU IS CRITICAL TO BUILDING THE RESEARCH CAPACITY THROUGH THE STRATEGIC ADDITION OF CAPABLE HUMAN CAPITAL AND KEY INFRASTRUCTURE NEEDED FOR THE SUCCESSFUL ACHIEVEMENT OF PROGRAMMATIC GOALS.

ACCORDING TO THE 2022 U. S. CENSUS, KENTUCKY HAD 69,425 FARMS. MANY OF THESE FARMS ARE LIMITED RESOURCE OPERATIONS, WHICH IS ILLUSTRATED BY THE 196 LIMITED RESOURCE FARMERS FROM KENTUCKY WHO ATTENDED THE 2023 SMALL LIMITED-RESOURCE AND MINORITY FARMERS CONFERENCE IN 2023. ADDITIONALLY, THE NATIONAL SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE RESEARCH AND EDUCATION (SARE) ORGANIZATION REPORTED THAT 80 PERCENT OF KENTUCKY'S LIMITED-RESOURCE FARMERS HAD AN ANNUAL INCOME BELOW $25,000, MAKING IT CLEAR THE NEED AND IMPORTANCE OF 1890 LAND-GRANT PROGRAMS TO SUPPORT THESE FARMS AND UPSTREAM AND DOWNSTREAM INDUSTRIES RELATED TO THESE FARMS. KENTUCKY STATE UNIVERSITY'S 1890 LAND-GRANT PROGRAM IS LEADING THE WAY TO OBTAIN GREATER COMPREHENSIVE SUCCESS FOR LIMITED RESOURCE FARMS. THIS IS ACHIEVED PARTLY THROUGH AGRICULTURAL TECHNOLOGY SOLUTIONS FOR INCREASING PRODUCTIVITY AND DIVERSIFICATION THAT INCLUDE RESEARCH ON TOPICS SUCH AS ORGANIC AGRICULTURE, SPECIALTY CROPS, INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT, IMPROVING SOIL QUALITY, ETC. OTHER APPROACHES INCLUDE EXPANSION OF MARKETING ALTERNATIVES TO LIMITED RESOURCE FARMERS, FINANCING ALTERNATIVES, IMPROVEMENT OF MENTAL HEALTH, ETC. KENTUCKY STATE UNIVERSITY'S EVANS-ALLEN RESEARCH PROGRAM ALSO TOUCHES THE LIVES OF ALL OF THE STATES' CITIZENS WHEN IT COMES TO RESEARCH IN NUTRITION AND HEALT HY LIFESTYLES LEADING TO RESULTS TO MITIGATE OBESITY, DIABETES, AND CANCER. THE GAMUT OF OUR RESEARCH PROGRAMS IS EXPRESSED IN OUR MOST RECENT USDA PLAN OF WORK ADDRESSING THE FOLLOWING CRITICAL ISSUES: 1. ECONOMIC AND FINANCIAL WELL-BEING. 2. FOOD SAFETY AND SECURITY 3. LEADERSHIP AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT 4. LIFE SKILL DEVELOPMENT 5. NUTRITION AND HEALTHY LIFESTYLES 6. SMALL FARM DEVELOPING 7. SUBSTANCE USE RECOVERY AND MENTAL WELL-BEING.

THROUGH THE INSTITUTE OF AGRICULTURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL RESEARCH, THE GOAL OF AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH AT TENNESSEE STATE UNIVERSITY IS TO CREATE AND COMMUNICATE NEW KNOWLEDGE IN THE AGRICULTURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCES. THROUGH OUR INNOVATIVE RESEARCH, WE ADDRESS THE NEEDS OF HUMANKIND, FOCUSING ON FINDING SOLUTIONS TO CHALLENGES FACED BY SOCIALLY AND ECONOMICALLY DISADVANTAGED GROUPS, AND CONTRIBUTING TO THE PROSPERITY OF THE CITIZENS OF TENNESSEE, THE NATION, AND THE WORLD. RESEARCH IN TENNESSEE STATE UNIVERSITY AGRICULTURE IS ORGANIZED TO ADDRESS THE CRITICAL ISSUES DESCRIBED BELOW.  ENHANCING BIODIVERSITY AND ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY SAFEGUARDING AND ENHANCING THE NATURAL RESOURCE ENVIRONMENT HAS BECOME INCREASINGLY COMPLEX WITHIN ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL, RESOURCE AND PERSONAL CONTEXTS. THROUGH COLLABORATION AMONG RESEARCHERS, INDUSTRY, PRODUCERS, ENVIRONMENTAL GROUPS, AND GOVERNMENT, WE ARE HELPING PRESERVE A DIVERSE AND RESILIENT ENVIRONMENT FOR FUTURE GENERATIONS.  ENRICHING OUR ECONOMY HELPING FARMS AND AGRICULTURE BUSINESSES BECOME MORE PROFITABLE AND INDIVIDUALS BECOME FINANCIALLY SECURE BOOSTS THE LOCAL, STATE, AND NATIONAL ECONOMIES. OUR PROGRAMS STRIVE TO STRENGTHEN THE ECONOMIC VIABILITY OF ALL FACETS OF AGRIBUSINESS, AND IMPROVE THE FINANCIAL LITERACY OF TENNESSEANS AND BEYOND SO THEY MAY BUILD AND PROTECT WEALTH FOR THEMSELVES AND FUTURE GENERATIONS.  STRENGTHENING OUR HEALTH MAKING HEALTHY CHOICES IS IMPORTANT FOR HUMANS, ANIMALS, AND EVEN OUR PLANET. AS A LEADER IN NUTRITION, ANIMAL WELFARE, AND ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION, WE ARE WORKING TO UNDERSTAND HOW FOOD, PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, AND SOCIAL CONNECTIONS AFFECT OVERALL HEALTH.  SUPPORTING FOOD, FIBER, AND ENERGY SYSTEMS SAFE, SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS THAT ARE SOCIALLY, ECONOMICALLY, AND ENVIRONMENTALLY RESPONSIBLE ARE KEY TO ENHANCING THE LIVES OF TENNESSEANS AND SUPPORTING A GROWING GLOBAL POPULATION. WE ARE EXPLORING WAYS TO DELIVER DISCOVERIES USING A SYSTEMS APPROACH TO AGRICULTURE PRODUCTIVITY THAT WILL PROVIDE CUSTOMIZABLE SOLUTIONS FOR PRODUCERS.  2 OUR RESEARCH ADDRESSES THESE CRITICAL ISSUES THROUGH FACULTY GROUPS IN THE PLANT, ANIMAL, FOOD, AND HUMAN SCIENCES.  WE CONDUCT RESEARCH IN AGRICULTURAL LEADERSHIP, EDUCATION AND COMMUNICATION THAT BRIDGES THE GAP BETWEEN THE GENERAL PUBLIC AND SCIENTISTS WORKING TO SOLVE CURRENT AND EMERGING CHALLENGES RELATED TO SUSTAINABLY FEEDING AN EVER-GROWING POPULATION UNDER VARIOUS ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIETAL COMPLICATIONS.  IN THE AREA OF AGRIBUSINESS, WE PREPARE STUDENTS, FARMERS, AND STAKEHOLDERS IN THE USE OF ECONOMIC ANALYSIS AND MANAGEMENT COMPETENCIES TO TAKE ON THE CHALLENGES AND OPPORTUNITIES OF A DYNAMIC AGRI-FOOD SYSTEM.  RESEARCH IN ANIMAL SCIENCE IS DIRECTED AT IMPROVING LIVESTOCK PRODUCTION SYSTEMS BY GENERATING NOVEL FINDINGS THAT IMPACT ANIMAL WELL-BEING AND PERFORMANCE.  ONGOING FOOD SCIENCE RESEARCH FOCUSES ON IMPROVING THE SAFETY, QUALITY, SHELF-LIFE, NUTRIENT PROFILE AND SENSORY ATTRIBUTES OF NOVEL FOOD INGREDIENTS, DEVELOPING AND VALIDATING ADVANCED AND INNOVATIVE TECHNOLOGIES FOR FOOD PROCESSING, MANUFACTURING, PACKAGING, AND SANITATION TO EFFECTIVELY REDUCE THE PRESENCE OF FO ODBORNE PATHOGENS. RESEARCH IN NATURAL RESOURCES USES MULTIDISCIPLINE APPROACHES TO UNDERSTAND AND ATTENUATE PROBLEMS CAUSED BY CLIMATE CHANGE, LAND DEGRADATION, LOSS OF BIODIVERSITY, EMERGING CONTAMINANTS, AND ANTHROPOGENIC STRESSORS.  PLANT SCIENCE RESEARCH INCL UDES DIVERSE FIELDS IN AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION SYSTEMS WITH A FOCUS ON DEVELOPING AND APPLYING SCIENTIFIC AND BIOTECHNOLOGICAL PRINCIPLES TO IMPROVE CROP PRODUCTIVITY, REDUCE LOSSES FROM DISEASE, INSECT PESTS, AND TOXIC METAL STRESS.  TO ADDRESS THE WELL-BEING AND HEALTH OF INDIVIDUALS, FAMILIES AND COMMUNITIES, RESEARCH IN FAMILY AND CONSUMER SCIENCES IS FOCUSED ON IMPROVING THE LIVES OF OUR STAKEHOLDERS THROUGH EDUCATION, LEADERSHIP AND COMMUNICATION TO IMPROVE NOT ONLY THEIR HEALTH AND WELL-BEING, BUT ALSO THEIR RELATIONSHIPS AND RESOURCES.

THE GEORGIA PLAN OF WORK (POW) ENCOMPASSES A FIVE-YEAR PERIOD BEGINNING OCTOBER 1, 2023. THE PLAN ADDRESSES MAJOR AGRICULTURAL ISSUES AS WELL AS OTHER PROBLEMS FACING RURAL AND URBAN AREAS, NUTRITION, THE ENVIRONMENT, FAMILIES, AND YOUTH. GEORGIA'S POW REPRESENTS A COORDINATED EFFORT BETWEEN FORT VALLEY STATE UNIVERSITY AND THE UNIVERSITY OF GEORGIA THUS PRESENTING ONE JOINT POW AND ANNUAL REPORT TO USDA. THE JOINT POW INCLUDE CORE PROGRAMS AND TARGETED ISSUES SUCH AS ANIMAL PRODUCTION, COMMUNITY/HOME AND LIFE SKILLS, FOOD SAFETY AND QUALITY, HEALTH AND WELLNESS, PLANT PRODUCTION, SUSTAINABILITY/CONSERVATION AND THE ENVIRONMENT, YOUTH AND FAMILY DEVELOPMENT, URBAN AGRICULTURE, AND EMERGING ISSUES, SUCH AS BIOFUELS AND DRONE TECHNOLOGY. USDA FUNDS FOR THESE CORE PROGRAMS SUPPORT STATE-LEVEL CORE AND TARGETED ISSUES FACING GEORGIA CITIZENS. THE GEORGIA PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT IS A MULTISTEP PROCESS THAT IS OPERATIONAL ANNUALLY. THE MODEL INCLUDES A METHOD FOR ASSESSING NEEDS AND IDENTIFYING PROBLEMS. IT ALSO INCLUDES PROGRAM EVALUATION TO DETERMINE IMPACT OF EXTENSION EDUCATIONAL TRAININGS. THE MODEL WORKS IN UNISON WITH MULTIPLE ADVISORY SYSTEMS AT BOTH COUNTY AND STATE LEVELS. GOALS OF THESE PROGRAMS ARE TO DEMONSTRATE SHORT AND LONG-TERM IMPACTS. STATE FUNDING SUCH AS STATE MATCH, COUNTY FUNDING, GRANTS AND GIFTS LEVERAGED AS A DIRECT RESULT OF THE WORK IN THIS PLAN AIDS IN CREATING THE GREATEST FINAL IMPACTS. THE RESEARCH PORTION OF THE PLAN OF WORK UNDERGOES SCIENTIFIC PEER REVIEW PRIOR TO EACH PROJECT BEING SUBMITTED. ALL SCIENTISTS ARE REQUIRED TO HAVE ACTIVE PROJECTS FOR EXPENDITURES TO BE MADE. EACH PROJECT IS PEER-REVIEWED BY BOTH INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL REVIEWERS AND MUST BE APPROVED BY THE APPROPRIATE DEAN AND DIRECTOR PRIOR TO SUBMISSION TO THE NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF FOOD AND AGRICULTURE. MOST APPLIED RESEARCH PROGRAMS ARE DEVELOPED BASED ON FEEDBACK FROM THE STAKEHOLDERS THROUGH THE EXTENSION CONTACTS AND BASIC RESEARCH ARE CONDUCTED TO FIND SPECIFIC SCIENTIFIC ANSWERS OR TO MAKE DISCOVERY. CURRENT ANIMAL RELATED PROJECTS INVOLVE EFFICIENT PRODUCTION SYSTEMS INCLUDING ASSISTED REPRODUCTIVE TECHNOLOGY AND NUTRITION, ANIMAL HEALTH AND WELLBEING WITH INTERNAL PARASITE CONTROL, AND ECONOMIC PROSPERITY A ND MARKETING USING SHEEP, GOATS, AND CATTLE AS MODELS. CLIMATE SMART AGRICULTURE WAS INTRODUCED THIS YEAR ALONG WITH OTHER 1890 INSTITUTIONS UNDER THE 1890 MULTISTATE CLIMATE CHANGE PROJECT WITHIN THE EVANS-ALLEN PROGRAM. THE FOOD SAFETY PROGRAM EMPHASIZES NON-THERMAL METHODS TO CONTROL FOOD BORN PATHOGENS IN MEAT AND NUTS. PLANT PRODUCTION PROGRAM ENCOMPASS A BROAD ARRAY OF TARGETED FIELDS OF STUDY THAT INCLUDE ENTOMOLOGY, PLANT PATHOLOGY, NEMATOLOGY, PLANT BREEDING AND GENETICS, SOIL SCIENCE, POSTHARVEST PHYSIOLOGY. SOME OF THESE PROJECTS ARE DONE IN COLLABORATION WITH ARS SCIENTISTS ON COMMODITY OF GREAT IMPORTANCE TO THE STATE OF GEORGIA. FUNDING FROM THE FEDERAL ALLOCATION AND THE CORRESPONDING MATCHING FUND FROM THE STATE ARE USED TO COVER EXPENSES RELATED TO THESE ACTIVITIES. ADDITIONAL FUNDS COME FROM EXTERNAL GRANTS SECURED BY THE RESEARCH SCIENTISTS. APPLIED RESEARCH PROJECTS USING THESE FUNDS TARGET MAINLY LIMITED-RESOURCE PRODUCERS IN THE STATE BUT SCIENTIFIC DISCOVERIES IMPACT THE CITIZEN OF STATE OF GEORGIA, THE COUNTRY, AND THE WORLD.

VIRGINIA STATE UNIVERSITY'S (VSU) AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH STATION (ARS) GENERATES SCIENTIFIC INFORMATION DESIGNED TO EXPAND KNOWLEDGE THAT WILL HELP SMALL, PART-TIME AND LIMITED-RESOURCE FARMERS BE PROFITABLE. THE RESEARCH FOCUS INCLUDES DEVELOPING PRODUCTION SYSTEMS THAT CONSERVE NATURAL RESOURCES, IMPROVING THE SUSTAINABILITY AND PROFITABILITY OF INDOOR AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION, DEVELOPING SUSTAINABLE PEST MANAGEMENT SYSTEMS FOR SMALL-SCALE AGRICULTURE AND IDENTIFYING NOVEL GENES THAT CAN BE USED TO IMPROVE CROP TOLERANCES TO ENVIRONMENTAL STRESSES. THE RESEARCH ALSO GENERATES SCIENTIFIC INFORMATION THAT IMPROVES THE PROFITABILITY AND HEALTH OF SMALL RUMINANTS. SCIENTISTS AT ARS WORK TO DEVELOP A RESILIENT FARMING SYSTEM THAT CAN COPE WITH THE ADVERSE IMPACTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE, COMPETITIVE AND SUSTAINABLE SMALL-SCALE AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS, AND BIO-BASED ENERGY PRODUCTION SYSTEMS. THEY FURTHER AIM TO IMPROVE FOOD SAFETY AND QUALITY, AND TO GENERATE SCIENTIFIC INFORMATION ON VALUEADDED PLANT AND ANIMAL PRODUCTS TO IMPROVE THE PROFITABILITY OF FARMS. RESEARCH IS CONDUCTED ON CAMPUS AND AT A NEARBY VSU FARM TO ADDRESS THE FOLLOWING CRITICAL ISSUES: 1: AGRICULTURAL VIABILITY, PROFITABILITY AND SUSTAINABILITY: DEVELOP LOW-INPUT AND PROFITABLE INDOOR AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION SYSTEMS. IMPROVE THE SUSTAINABILITY AND PROFITABILITY OF SMALL RUMINANT PRODUCTION 2: BIOTECHNOLOGY, BIOMATERIALS, AND BIOENERGY: IDENTIFY NOVEL GENES THAT CAN BE USED TO IMPROVE CROP TOLERANCES TO ENVIRONMENTAL STRESSES, ESPECIALLY DROUGHT, HEAT AND METAL TOXICITY. USE GENETIC AND GENOME APPROACHES FOR BREEDING NEW CROPS TO ADDRESS GLOBAL CLIMATE CHANGE. 3: NATURAL RESOURCES, ENVIRONMENT AND CLIMATE CHANGE: DEVELOP A RESILIENT FARMING SYSTEM THAT CAN COPE WITH THE ADVERSE IMPACTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE. MINIMIZE THE EFFECTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE ON LOW INCOME COMMUNITIES.

ALABAMA AGRICULTURAL AND MECHANICAL UNIVERSITY (AAMU) CONDUCTS RESEARCH PROJECTS THAT MEET THE NEEDS OF THE CITIZENS OF ALABAMA AND THE NATION. TO FULFILL OUR OBLIGATIONS UNDER USDA-NIFA EVANS ALLEN ACT OF 1890 (SECTION 1445) FOR THE FISCAL YEAR 2025, THERE ARE SEVERAL PROJECTS BEING SUBMITTED FOR APPROVAL. RESEARCH AREAS OF INTEREST ARE: FOOD SYSTEMS AND FOOD SAFETY; GLOBAL FOOD SECURITY AND HUNGER; NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY; HUMAN NUTRITION, WELL-BEING, HEALTH AND OBESITY; AND COMMUNITY AND REGIONAL PLANNING. ALL THESE ARE ALIGNED WITH THE USDA STRATEGIC PLAN FY 2022-2026 GOALS AND USDA SCIENCE AND RESEARCH STRATEGY (2023-2026) PRIORITIES. FOOD SYSTEMS AND FOOD SAFETY: RESEARCH AND EXTENSION-INTEGRATED ACTIVITIES ENHANCE FOOD SYSTEMS, FOOD SAFETY AND AGRICULTURAL BIOSECURITY. THE GOAL OF THIS CRITICAL ISSUE IS TO DEVELOP TECHNOLOGY AND METHODS TO PROTECT AND ENHANCE THE SAFETY OF AGRICULTURE AND FOOD, REDUCE EPIDEMICS OF FOOD-BORNE ILLNESSES, AND TO DEVELOP THE KNOWLEDGE AND METHODOLOGIES FOR RAPID DETECTION OF THREAT AGENTS, INCLUDING EXISTING AND EMERGING DISEASES OF PLANTS AND ANIMALS, RISK ASSESSMENT, AND FACILITY AND PERSONNEL SECURITY. GLOBAL FOOD SECURITY AND HUNGER: THE GOAL IS TO ENHANCE THE COMPETITIVENESS AND SUSTAINABILITY OF FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL INDUSTRIES IN ALABAMA THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF BEST PRACTICES OR TECHNOLOGIES. THIS CRITICAL ISSUE ADDRESSES TWO BROADLY DEFINED PRIORITY AREAS; I) PLANT HEALTH AND PRODUCTION AND PLANT PRODUCTS, INCLUDING IMPROVED CROPPING SYSTEMS, PLANT BREEDING/GENOMICS, INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT, PRECISION AGRICULTURE, AND ALTERNATIVE SPECIALTY CROPS; AND II) ANIMAL HEALTH AND PRODUCTION, INCLUDING IMPROVED FOOD-ANIMAL SYSTEMS AND STOCKS. OF PARTICULAR INTEREST ARE PROGRAMS AND PROJECTS THAT INCLUDE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES THAT PRESENT INNOVATIVE SYNERGIES OF DISCIPLINES AND PERSPECTIVES. HUMAN NUTRITION, WELL-BEING, HEALTH AND OBESITY: OBESITY, DIABETES, HIGH BLOOD PRESSURE, AND VASCULAR ISSUES ARE MOSTLY CAUSED BY THE LACK OF NUTRIENTS, THE LACK OF EXERCISE, POOR LIFESTYLE CHOICES, AND STRESS OF THE INVOLVED INDIVIDUALS. AS A RESULT OF THE GROWING HEALTH CONCERNS FOR ALABAMA CITIZENS, THERE HAS BEEN A COMBINED EFFORT TO EDUCATE AND MOTIVATE CITIZENS THROUGHOUT THE STATE TO MAKE BETTER HEALTH DECISIONS. THE OBJECTIVE IS TO IMPROVE THE HEALTH OF ALABAMIANS, TARGETING LIMITED-RESOURCE FAMILIES, THROUGH CHRONIC DISEASE AWARENESS, PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, NUTRITION EDUCATION, HEALTH LITERACY, AND ACCESS TO AND CONSUMPTION OF FRESH FRUITS AND VEGETABLES. NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY: THIS PROGRAM PLAN WILL GENERATE KNOWLEDGE TO MANAGE AGRICULTURAL AND NATURAL SYSTEMS IN THE FACE OF CLIMATE CHANGE AND THE NEED TO SUSTAIN NATURAL RESOURCES. SPECIFIC AREAS INCLUDE: CLIMATE-SMART SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS, ENERGY CONSERVATION AND UTILIZATION OF RENEWABLE ENERGY RESOURCES; UNDERSTANDING THE LAND-WATER INTERFACE; CONSEQUENCES AND SOLUTIONS OF GLOBAL CLIMATE CHANGE; WATER QUALITY AND QUANTITY, CARBON SEQUESTRATION, NATURAL SYSTEMS RESTORATION, SURFACE AND GROUNDWATER CONSERVATION; MANAGEMENT OF AGRICULTURAL WASTE RESIDUE; SUSTAINABLE SOIL HEALTH ENHANCEMENT; SUSTAINABLE ECOAND AGRI-TOURISM; RURAL-URBAN INTERFACE ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES; REMOTE SENSING AND PRECISION AGRICULTURE. COMMUNITY AND REGIONAL PLANNING: THIS AREA IS DESIGNED TO MAINTAIN THE INTEGRITY OF AGRICULTURAL LANDS THROUGH RURAL AND URBAN PLANNING PROGRAMS. APPROPRIATED FUNDS WILL BE USED FOR EXPENSES IN RESEARCH WHICH WILL INCLUDE FACULTY AND STAFF SALARIES, STUDENT SUPPORT, DISSEMINATION OF RESEARCH RESULTS, ADMINISTRATIVE PLANNING AND DIRECTION, EQUIPMENT PURCHASE AND MAINTENANCE, AND SUPPLIES PURCHASE (AMONG OTHER APPROVED SPENDING).

ALABAMA'S RESEARCH AND EXTENSION SEEKS TO ADDRESS SELECTED QUESTIONS THAT LEAD TO THE IDENTIFICATION OF CRITICAL ISSUES OF STRATEGIC IMPORTANCE. OUR PROGRAMS ARE THEREFORE FOCUSED ON THE FOLLOWING CRUCIAL ISSUES: (1) GLOBAL FOOD SECURITY AND HUNGER; (2) NATURAL RESOURCES CONSERVATION AND MANAGEMENT, ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY, AND CLIMATE CHANGE; (3) FOOD SYSTEM AND FOOD SAFETY; (4) HUMAN NUTRITION, WELL-BEING, HEALTH, AND OBESITY; (5) SUSTAINABLE ENERGY; (6) COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT; AND (7) FAMILY, HOME AND 4-H AND YOUTH DEVELOPMENT. OUR PROGRAMS ARE DESIGNED TO ADDRESS THE ALABAMA BLACK BELT REGION AND HISTORICALLY DISADVANTAGED AND UNDERSERVED LIMITED RESOURCE PRODUCERS AND LANDOWNERS. SPECIFIC RESEARCH PROJECTS ARE THEREFORE FOCUSED ON: EFFICIENT WATER USE AND ADAPTATION TO CLIMATE VARIABILITY: A SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTION SOLUTION FOR HISTORICALLY DISADVANTAGED AND LIMITED RESOURCE FARMERS AND LANDOWNERS; SUSTAINABLE MEAT GOAT PRODUCTION SYSTEMS FOR LIMITED- RESOURCE PRODUCERS; SU STAINABLE AND RELIABLE APPROACHES AND MARKETING STRATEGIES TO INCREASE YIELD OF VEGETABLES AND FRUITS FOR SOCIALLY DISADVANTAGED FARMERS IN ALABAMA; ALTERNATIVE POULTRY PRODUCTION: A SUSTAINABLE INTEGRATIVE POULTRY PRODUCTION MODEL FOR SMALL SCALE PRODUCERS; INTEG RATIVE APPROACHES TO OBESITY PREVENTION IN ALABAMA BLACK BELT COUNTIES; STRENGTHENING PROGRAMS IN ORGANIC FARMING IN ALABAMA THROUGH RESEARCH AND EDUCATION; AND DEVELOPMENT AND EVALUATION OF INTEGRATIVE ALTERNATIVE ENERGY SOURCES FOR LIMITED-RESOURCE FARMERS AND UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES IN ALABAMA.

ALCORN STATE UNIVERSITY, FOUNDED IN 1871, IS AN 1890 HBCU LAND GRANT UNIVERSITY LOCATED IN LORMAN, MISSISSIPPI PROVIDING BROAD AGRICULTURE SERVICES TO HER SERVING MINORITY COMMUNITIES. ALCORN HAS PROGRAMS IN AGRICULTURE RESEARCH, EDUCATION AND EXTENSION. AGRICULTURE RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EDUCATION AT ALCORN BOASTS DIVERSE FIELDS SUCH AS AGRONOMY, PLANT BREEDING, PLANT PATHOLOGY, ENTOMOLOGY, MYCOLOGY, VIROLOGY, SOIL SCIENCE, ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCE, ANIMAL SCIENCE, PLANT BIOTECHNOLOGY, BIOFUELS AND BIOPROCESSING, AGRICULTURE ECONOMICS, AGRIBUSINESS AND AGRICULTURE MECHANICS AND ITS APPLICATIONS. THESE DISCIPLINES AT ALCORN'S AGRICULTURE RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EDUCATION PROGRAMS HAVE BEEN ESTABLISHED TO SERVE SMALL FARMERS, LIMITED RESOURCE FARMERS AND DISADVANTAGED FARMERS OF MISSISSIPPI. ANOTHER SIGNIFICANT COMPONENT ALCORN STATE'S AGRICULTURE RESEARCH ACTIVITY AIMS AT ENHANCING AWARENESS OF AGRICULTURE AND THE RECRUITMENT OF MINORITY YOUTH FROM HIGH SCHOOL AND COMMUNITY COLLEGE. THE AGRICULTURE PROGRAMS AT ALCORN STATE CONTRIBUTES TO WORKFORCE TRAINING AT DIFFERENCE LEVELS PREPARING A SIZEABLE NUMBER OF SKILLED AND TRAINED AGRICULTURE PROFESSIONALS ANNUALLY INTO THE AGRICULTURE WORKFORCE. THE PROPOSED WORK IS OUTLINED TO INCLUDE 1) SOIL AND WATER QUALITY DEGRADATION, COVER CROPS AND SOIL AND WATER DEGRADATION MITIGATION; 2) CROP, VEGETABLES AND FRUITS PRODUCTION, PROCESSING AND STORAGE; 3) NATIVE AND NOVEL BIOFUEL CROPS SUCH AS SWITCHGRASS AND MISCANTHUS AS BIOFUELS FOR BIOMASS PRODUCTION; 4) PLANTS AS FEED FOR ANIMAL CONSUMPTION AND ANIMAL NUTRITIONAL RES EARCH; 5) SOIL SURVEY AND CLIMATE CHANGE INVESTIGATION; 6) EVALUATION OF IRRIGATION AND NATURAL WATER MOVEMENT ON COVER CROP AND VEGETABLE CROP POTENTIAL TO INCREASE SOIL AND WATER QUALITY; 7) DEVELOP AND APPLY TRADITIONAL AND LATEST TECHNOLOGY FOR PLANT PESTS DIAGNOSIS AND MANAGEMENT; 8) EVALUATION OF NOVEL AND SPECIALTY CROPS FOR INTEGRATION INTO SMALL FARMERS' FARM OPERATION AND THEIR ECONOMIC IMPACTS ON SMALL FARM'S OPERATION; 9) ADOPTION AND APPLICATION OF NOVEL BIOTECHNOLOGY SUCH AS GENOME EDITING FOR CROP GENETIC IMPROVEMENT; 10) SMART AGRICULTURE AND APPLICATIONS OF ROBOTICS AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN BROAD AGRICULTURE PRODUCTIONS; 11) ANIMAL PRODUCTION, PHYSIOLOGY, GENETICS, ZOONOTIC DISEASE INVESTIGATION AND PUBLIC HEALTH EDUCATION; 12) DEMONSTRATION OF AGRICULTURE RESEARCH FOR SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY, ENGINEERING AND MATH (STEM) OUTREACH TO PREK-12 SCHOOLS AND COMMUNITY COLLEGES FOR WORKFORCE CULTIVATION; 13) PRESENT RESEARCH FINDINGS AT LOCAL, REGIONAL, AND NATIONAL CONFERENCES; 14) PUBLISH RESEARCH RESULTS.

positiveFlows.title: MISSOURI IS WELL-KNOWN FOR THE DIVERSITY OF ITS NATURAL RESOURCES THAT ARE ESSENTIAL TO THE ENVIRONMENTAL AND ECONOMIC VITALITY OF THE STATE. THE QUALITY OF LIFE OF THE STATE'S CITIZENS ALSO DEPENDS ON THE HEALTH OF ITS NATURAL RESOURCES AND THE SURROUNDING ENVIRONMENT, PARTICULARLY THAT OF THE AIR, LAND/SOIL, AND WATER RESOURCES. HOWEVER, THESE RESOURCES AND THE ENVIRONMENT ARE EXPERIENCING INCREASED PRESSURE DUE TO THE DOMINANCE OF INPUT (E.G., SYNTHETIC FERTILIZERS, TILLAGE, PESTICIDES)-DEPENDENT, HIGHLY SPECIALIZED CROP AND LIVESTOCK PRODUCTION SYSTEMS COMBINED WITH CLIMATE CHANGE-RELATED STRESSORS (E.G., RECORD SETTING HIGH AND LOW TEMPERATURES, FLOODING, AND DROUGHTS) - ALL OF WHICH HAVE POSED A SIGNIFICANT THREAT TO THE SUSTAINABLE PROVISION OF GOODS (E.G., FOOD PRODUCTION AND FOOD SAFETY) AND SERVICES (E.G., CLEAN AIR AND WATER) FOR THE MISSOURIANS. IN ALIGNMENT WITH THE USDA-NIFA'S RESEARCH PRIORITIES, LINCOLN UNIVERSITY'S COOPERATIVE RESEARCH (LUCR) PROGRAM HAS BEEN CONDUCTING RESEARCH IN THE FOLLOWING AREAS: 1) ANIMAL SCIENCE, 2) SOIL HEALTH AND CROP SCIENCES, 3) FOOD NUTRITION AND SAFETY, 4) NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, AND 5) SOCIAL-ECONOMICS. LUCR AIMS TO CONTINUE DEVELOPING IMPACTFUL, INNOVATIVE, AND MULTIDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH PROGRAMS THAT EFFECTIVELY ADDRESS EMERGING AND CRITICAL ISSUES FACING MISSOURI'S NATURAL RESOURCES, AGRICULTURAL INDUSTRY, AND RURAL COMMUNITIES AS WELL AS STRENGTHEN LINCOLN UNIVERSITY'S CAPACITY TO BETTER ADDRESS THE NEEDS OF MISSOURI FARMERS AND RANCHERS. LUCR FACULTY MEMBERS HAVE BEEN CONTRIBUTING TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF CLIMATE-RESILIENT AGRICULTURAL AND FOOD SYSTEMS FOR SUSTAINING PRODUCTION, ENHANCING ECOSYSTEM HEALTH, AND SAFEGUARDING HUMAN HEALTH AND QUALITY OF LIFE FOR MISSOURI RESIDENTS. THE LUCR PROGRAM AND ITS MULTIFACETED RESEARCH PROJECTS SPECIFICALLY TARGET THOSE WHO HAVE BEEN HISTORICALLY UNDERSERVED, WHILE ALSO CONTRIBUTING TO THE DIVERSITY OF THE NATION'S FUTURE STEM-AGRICULTURAL WORKFORCE. OF THE SIX CRITICAL ISSUES IDENTIFIED, LUCR CAPACITY RESEARCH EFFORTS ARE PRIMARILY FOCUSED ON THE FOLLOWING THREE AREAS: 1) SUSTAINABLE AND RESILIENT AGRICULTURE SYSTEMS, 2) ENVIRONMENTAL AND NATURAL RESOURCES, AND 3) HEALTH AND HEALTHY FUTURES. UNDER THE CRITICAL ISSUE OF ENVIRONMENT AND NATURAL RESOURCES, LUCR CURRENT CAPACITY RESEARCH PROJECTS THAT HAVE BEEN INITIATED AND APPROVED BY NIFA ARE FOCUSED ON THE AREAS OF CLIMATE CHANGE IMPACTS, SOIL HEALTH AND REGENERATIVE AGRICULTURE, AGROFORESTRY, RENEWABLE BIOENERGY, AND GIS/REMOTE SENSING TECHNOLOGY APPLICATIONS. CAPACITY RESEARCH PROJECTS UNDER THE CRITICAL ISSUE OF HEALTH AND HEALTHY FUTURES ARE CURRENTLY FOCUSED ON THE AREAS OF SENSOR DEVELOPMENT FOR DETECTION OF FOODBORNE PATHOGENS, DRINKING WATER QUALITY AND SAFETY, AND EMERGING ENVIRONMENTAL CONTAMINANTS. THE GEORGIA PLAN OF WORK (POW) ENCOMPASSES A FIVE-YEAR PERIOD BEGINNING OCTOBER 1, 2022. THE PLAN ADDRESSES MAJOR AGRICULTURAL ISSUES AS WELL AS MANY OTHER PROBLEMS FACING RURAL AND URBAN AREAS, THE ENVIRONMENT, FAMILIES AND YOUTH. THE PLAN REPRESENTS A COORDINATED EFFORT BETWEEN THE STATE'S 1890 AND 1862 LAND-GRANT INSTITUTIONS, FORT VALLEY STATE UNIVERSITY (FVSU) AND THE UNIVERSITY OF GEORGIA (UGA), AND INCLUDES JOINT PLANNING BETWEEN EXPERIMENT STATIONS AND COOPERATIVE EXTENSION UNITS AT BOTH UNIVERSITIES. GEORGIA, ONE OF THE ORIGINAL 13 COLONIES, HAS A LAND AREA OF 57,701 SQUARE MILES AND A WATER AREA OF 1,706 SQUARE MILES, WHICH MAKES IT THE LARGEST STATE EAST OF THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER (21TH OVERALL). GEORGIA FALLS WITHIN FIVE MAJOR PHYSIOGRAPHIC REGIONS: THE BLUE RIDGE MOUNTAINS IN THE NORTHEAST; THE RIDGE AND VALLEY PROVINCE AND THE CUMBERLAND PLATEAU IN THE NORTHWEST; THE PIEDMONT ACROSS CENTRAL GEORGIA; AND THE COASTAL PLAIN IN THE SOUTH. ELEVATIONS RANGE FROM SEA LEVEL TO 4,784 FEET AT BRASSTOWN BALD IN THE BLUE RIDGE MOUNTAINS. THE 2020 CENSUS ESTIMATED GEORGIA'S POPULATION WAS 10,711,908 AND REPORTED 23.8% OF GEORGIANS ARE UNDER AGE 18 AND 13.9% ARE 65 OR OLDER. ACCORDING TO THE CENSUS,51.9% OF GEORGIANS IDENTIFY THEMSELVES AS WHITE/CAUCASIAN, 31% AS BLACK/AFRICAN-AMERICAN, 4.5% AS ASIAN,.5% AS AMERICAN INDIAN/ALASKA NATIVE, .1% AS NATIVE HAWAIIAN/PACIFIC ISLANDER, AND 6.9% AS MORE THAN ONE RACE. IT WAS ALSO REPORTED THAT 10.5% OF GEORGIANS IDENTIFY AS HISPANIC OR LATINO. GEORGIA'S COOPERATIVE EXTENSION PROGRAM HAS 167 OFFICES, WITH PROGRAMMING IN ALL OF GEORGIA'S 159 COUNTIES. FVSU AND UGA PERSONNEL ARE HOUSED JOINTLY IN COUNTY OFFICES. EXTENSION DELIVERS PROGRAMMING IN AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCES, FAMILY AND CONSUMER SCIENCES, AND 4-H YOUTH DEVELOPMENT AS BOTH INDIVIDUAL COUNTY EFFORTS AND AS MULTICOUNTY PROGRAMS. STATE FACULTY MEMBERS DELIVER TRAINING TO COUNTY AGENTS AND PROGRAMMING DIRECTLY TO CLIENTELE, WHEN APPROPRIATE. FVSU AND UGA RESEARCHPROGRAMS ARE CONDUCTED THROUGH THE AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION SYSTEM. GEORGIA HAS SEVERAL CAMPUSES THROUGHOUT THE STATE; ITS FOUR LARGEST ARE LOCATED IN ATHENS, FORT VALLEY, TIFTON AND GRIFFIN. GEORGIA HAS ELEVEN RESEARCH AND EDUCATION CENTERS STRATEGICALLY LOCATED THROUGHOUT THE STATE. THIS JOINT PLAN OF WORK WAS DEVELOPED AROUND CORE PROGRAMS AND TARGETED ISSUES. USING A STRUCTURED PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT SYSTEM, GEORGIA DEVELOPS CORE PROGRAM DIRECTIONS AND IDENTIFIES TARGETED ISSUES. THE GEORGIA PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT MODEL IS A MULTISTEP PROCESS THAT IS OPERATIONAL EVERY YEAR. THE MODEL INCLUDES A METHOD FOR ASSESSING NEEDS AND IDENTIFYING PROBLEMS. IT ALSO INCLUDES PROGRAM EVALUATION TO DETERMINE IMPACT. THE GEORGIA PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT MODEL WORKS IN UNISON WITH MULTIPLE ADVISORY SYSTEMS AT BOTH COUNTY AND STATE LEVELS. INPUT SOLICITED DIRECTLY FROM ACADEMIC DEPARTMENTS AT FVSU'S COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE, FAMILY SCIENCES AND TECHNOLOGY AS WELL AS UGA'S COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCES (CAES) AND COLLEGE OF FAMILY AND CONSUMER SCIENCES AS PART OF THE ANNUAL NEEDS ASSESSMENT IS AN INTEGRAL PART OF DEVELOPING THIS PLAN OF WORK. FACULTY MEMBERS ASSOCIATED WITH THIS PLAN ARE WORKING ON CUTTING-EDGE PROGRAMS. THEY PROVIDE INFORMATION AND INPUT FROM BOTH THE ACADEMIC LITERATURE AND PERSONAL KNOWLEDGE. THIS INPUT IS EQUALLY IMPORTANT TO PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT AS IS A STRONG ADVISORY SYSTEM. THE GEORGIA FEDERAL PLAN OF WORK DOES NOT ATTEMPT TO CAPTURE ALL OF THE WORK OF THE COLLEGES' FACULTY MEMBERS. IT IS INTENDED TO DOCUMENT THE PLANS AND ACTIONS OF THE FACULTY MEMBERS RECEIVING SPECIFIC FORMULA FUNDS. THE MAJORITY OF THESE FUNDS ARE USED TO SUPPORT STATE-LEVEL CORE PROGRAMS. THESE CORE PROGRAMS COVER A WIDE RANGE OF TOPICS, INCLUDING TRADITIONAL ANIMAL AND PLANT PRODUCTION, POSITIVE YOUTH AND FAMILY DEVELOPMENT, URBAN AGRICULTURE, PERSONAL HEALTH AND WELL- BEING, AND EMERGING ISSUES, SUCH AS BIOFUELS. THE GOALS OF THESE PROGRAMS ARE TO DEMONSTRATE SHORT-AND LONG-TERM IMPACT. HOWEVER, THE GREATEST IMPACTS OF THESE CORE PROGRAMS ARE THE FOUNDATIONS CREATED TO SUPPORT AND LEVERAGE ADDITIONAL RESOURCES BEYOND STATE-MATCHING FUNDS. THE OUTPUTS OF THESE LEVERAGED PROGRAMS ARE CONSIDERED A DIRECT, SHORT-TERM OUTCOME OF THE CORE PLANNED PROGRAMS WITHIN THE GEORGIA FEDERAL PLAN OF WORK. THE GEORGIA FEDERAL PLAN OF WORK IS CENTERED ON EIGHT PLANNED PROGRAMS. THESE WORK IN CONJUNCTION WITH EACH OTHER TO ADDRESS IMPORTANT ISSUES ON COUNTY, STATE, REGIONAL, NATIONAL AND GLOBAL LEVELS. THE OVERALL GOAL OF THE COOPERATIVE AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH CENTER (CARC) IS TO CONDUCT AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH PROJECTS THAT WILL HELP SOLVE EVERYDAY PROBLEMS AND ISSUES. COLLABORATION WITH RESEARCHERS IN PLANT AND ANIMAL SCIENCES WILL BE EMPHASIZED AND FOSTERED. THE CULMINATION OF THESE ISSUES WILL FOCUS ON IMPROVING PRODUCTIVITY WITH A VARIETY OF AGRICULTURAL ANIMALS. FOCUS WILL BE ON IMPROVING LIVESTOCK MANAGEMENT, ENHANCING TECHNOLOGIES AND PRACTICES THAT INCREASE LIVESTOCK PRODUCTIVITY, AND CONDUCTING MULTIPLE LEVELS OF RESEARCH INVESTIGATING METHODS TO INCREASE THE HEALTH AND PRODUCTIVITY OF LIVESTOCK THROUGH OPTIMIZING NUTRITION AND REPRODUCTION AT THE GENETIC LEVEL TO STUDY ALL ASPECTS OF FOOD AND ANIMAL PRODUCTION. CROP PRODUCTION <(>&<)> UTILIZATION: DISCOVERING NEW KNOWLEDGE ABOUT GENETICS, GROWTH, AND DISEASE RESISTANCE OF FIELD, GRAIN, FRUIT, AND VEGETABLE CROPS AND PROVIDING AGRONOMIC INFORMATION ON HYBRIDS AND VARIETY. THIS INCLUDES HIGH-VALUE, LOW-VOLUME SPECIALTY CROP PRODUCTION AND MAJOR CROPS. RESEARCH WILL FOCUS ON UNDER-UTILIZED FRUITS AND VEGETABLES, MEDICINAL PLANTS, LEGUMES, AND ROOT CROPS AND ACTIVELY INVESTIGATE CORN, SOYBEAN, WHEAT, FORAGE, OATS, AND ALFALFA. THE COOPERATIVE AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH CENTER (CARC) WILL ACHIEVE RESILIENCY THROUGH RESEARCH ON THE DEMONSTRATION FARM WITH AGRONOMIC CROPS, FOOD, FIBER, AND ECOLOGICAL SYSTEMS; INCORPORATE EXPERIENTIAL EDUCATION ON THE FARM; AND RENOVATE RESEARCH SPACE, BEEF CATTLE, GOAT AND POULTRY OPERATION; AND CREATE COLLABORATIONS AMONG FEDERAL, STATE, AND LOCAL EN TITIES TO ENGAGE IN NEW RESEARCH FOR EMERGING SPECIALTY AGRONOMIC CROPS, EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT, AND DISASTER EDUCATION TO COUNTY AGENTS. THE GEORGIA PLAN OF WORK (POW) ENCOMPASSES A FIVE-YEAR PERIOD BEGINNING OCTOBER 1, 2025. THE PLAN ADDRESSES MAJOR AGRICULTURAL ISSUES AS WELL AS MANY OTHER PROBLEMS FACING RURAL AND URBAN AREAS, THE ENVIRONMENT, FAMILIES AND YOUTH. GEORGIA'S POW REPRESENTS A COORDINATED EFFORT BETWEEN THE STATE'S 1890 AND 1862 LAND-GRANT INSTITUTIONS, FORT VALLEY STATE UNIVERSITY (FVSU) AND UNIVERSITY OF GEORGIA (UGA), THUS PRESENTING ONE JOINT POW AND ANNUAL REPORT TO USDA. THE JOINT POW INCLUDES CORE PROGRAMS AND TARGETED ISSUES SUCH AS PLANT AND ANIMAL PRODUCTION, COMMUNITY/HOME AND LIFE SKILLS, FOOD SAFETY AND QUALITY, HEALTH AND WELLNESS, SUSTAINABILITY/CONSERVATION AND THE ENVIRONMENT, YOUTH AND FAMILY DEVELOPMENT, URBAN AGRICULTURE, AND EMERGING ISSUES (I.E. AI-POWERED DRONES AND AUTONOMOUS TRACTORS IN AGRICULTURE). USDA FUNDS FOR THESE CORE PROGRAMS SUPPORT STATE-LEVEL CORE AND TARGETED ISSUES FACING GEORGIA AND AMERICAN CITIZENS. THE GEORGIA PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT IS A MULTISTEP PROCESS THAT IS OPERATIONAL ANNUALLY. THE RESEARCH PORTION OF THE PLAN OF WORK UNDERGOES SCIENTIFIC PEER REVIEW PRIOR TO EACH PROJECT BEING SUBMITTED. ALL SCIENTISTS ARE REQUIRED TO HAVE ACTIVE PROJECTS FOR EXPENDITURES TO BE MADE. EACH PROJECT IS PEER-REVIEWED BY BOTH INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL REVIEWERS AND MUST BE APPROVED BY THE APPROP RIATE DEAN AND DIRECTOR PRIOR TO SUBMISSION TO THE NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF FOOD AND AGRICULTURE. CURRENT ANIMAL RELATED PROJECTS INVOLVE EFFICIENT ASSISTED REPRODUCTIVE TECHNOLOGY AND NUTRITION, ANIMAL HEALTH AND WELLBEING WITH INTERNAL PARASITE CONTROL USING SHEEP, GOATS, AND CATTLE AS MODELS. A NEW MULTISTATE EVANS-ALLEN PROJECT WAS INTRODUCED THIS YEAR ALONG WITH OTHER 1890 INSTITUTIONS UNDER THE TITLE ECOLOGICAL RESILIENCE AND EXTREME WEATHER EVENTS: IMPACTS ON FARMERS, LANDOWNERS AND COMMUNITIES. THE FOOD SAFETY PROGRAM EMPHASIZES NON-THERMAL METHODS TO CONTROL FOOD BORNE PATHOGENS IN MEAT AND NUTS. PLANT PRODUCTION PROGRAMS ENCOMPASS A BROAD ARRAY OF TARGETED FIELDS OF STUDY INCLUDING ENTOMOLOGY, PLANT PATHOLOGY, NEMATOLOGY, PLANT BREEDING AND GENETICS, SOIL SCIENCE, AND POSTHARVEST PHYSIOLOGY. SOME OF THESE PROJECTS ARE DONE IN COLLABORATION WITH ARS SCIENTISTS ON COMMODITY OF GREAT IMPORTANCE TO THE STATE OF GEORGIA. FUNDING FROM THE FEDERAL ALLOCATION AND THE CORRESPONDING MATCHING FUND FROM THE STATE ARE USED TO COVER EXPENSES RELATED TO THESE ACTIVITIES. ADDITIONAL FUNDS COME FROM EXTERNAL GRANTS SECURED BY THE RESEARCH SCIENTISTS. APPLIED RESEARCH PROJECTS USING THESE FUNDS TARGET MAINLY LIMITED-RESOURCE PRODUCERS IN THE STATE BUT SCIENTIFIC DISCOVERIES IMPACT THE CITIZEN OF STATE OF GEORGIA, THE COUNTRY, AND THE WORLD.

VIRGINIA STATE UNIVERSITY'S AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH STATION (ARS) ADVANCES THE LAND-GRANT MISSION THROUGH SCIENCE-BASED DISCOVERY AND INNOVATION THAT ENHANCE THE PRODUCTIVITY, PROFITABILITY, AND RESILIENCE OF AGRICULTURE FOR ALL FARMERS. GUIDED BY THE VIRGINIA STATE UNIVERSITY COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE'S VISION FOR TRANSDISCIPLINARY INTEGRATION, ARS APPLIES ADVANCED TECHNOLOGIES, SUSTAINABLE PRACTICES, AND COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH TO STRENGTHEN THE COMMONWEALTH'S FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS WHILE CONTRIBUTING SOLUTIONS TO REGIONAL AND NATIONAL CHALLENGES. ARS'S RESEARCH PORTFOLIO CONTINUES TO EVOLVE FROM A TRADITIONAL EMPHASIS ON SMALL RUMINANTS TOWARD A MULTI-LIVESTOCK APPROACH THAT INCLUDES BEEF CATTLE, SHEEP, AND SMALLSCALE POULTRY PRODUCTION SYSTEMS. COMPLEMENTARY EFFORTS IN BOTH CONTROLLED-ENVIRONMENT AND FIELD-BASED AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS ARE EXPANDING OPPORTUNITIES FOR SUSTAINABLE CROP, FORAGE, AND HORTICULTURAL PRODUCTION. ACROSS THESE ENTERPRISES, ARS SCIENTISTS EMPLOY DATA ANALYTICS, AUTOMATION, AND PRECISION AGRICULTURE TOOLS TO IMPROVE PRODUCTION EFFICIENCY, RESOURCE STEWARDSHIP, AND ECONOMIC PERFORMANCE. ALIGNED WITH THE FY 2026 PLAN OF WORK, ARS RESEARCH ADDRESS ES THE FOLLOWING CRITICAL ISSUE AREAS: 1. AGRICULTURAL VIABILITY, PROFITABILITY, AND SUSTAINABILITY: DEVELOP RESILIENT AND ECONOMICALLY EFFICIENT PRODUCTION SYSTEMS THROUGH DATAINFORMED DECISION-MAKING, IMPROVED SOIL AND FORAGE MANAGEMENT, AND OPTIMIZED INTEGRATION OF LIVESTOCK AND CROP ENTERPRISES. 2. BIOTECHNOLOGY, BIOMATERIALS, AND BIOENERGY: IDENTIFY AND CHARACTERIZE GENES THAT ENHANCE TOLERANCE TO ENVIRONMENTAL STRESSES SUCH AS DROUGHT, HEAT, AND METAL TOXICITY; APPLY GENOMIC AND BIOTECHNOLOGICAL TOOLS TO BREED ADAPTI VE CROPS; AND EXPLORE BIO-BASED AND RENEWABLE PRODUCTS TO STRENGTHEN THE BIOECONOMY. 3. AGRICULTURE INNOVATION: EMPLOY TRANSDISCIPLINARY STRATEGIES TO ACCELERATE THE DISCOVERY, ADAPTATION, AND TRANSLATION OF TECHNOLOGIES, INCLUDING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, ROBOTICS, AND CYBER-BIOSECURITY, TO ADDRESS BIOSECURITY THREATS, IMPROVE DIGITAL INTEGRATION, AND PREPARE A TECHNOLOGY-ENABLED AGRICULTURAL WORKFORCE. 4. NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENT: ADVANCE SCIENCE-BASED PRACTICES THAT ENHANCE SOIL HEALTH, CONSERVE WATER RESOURCES, AND SUSTAIN BIODIVERSITY WHILE IMPROVING THE RESILIENCE OF AGRICULTURAL ECOSYSTEMS TO EXTREME WEATHER AND ENVIRONMENTAL PRESSURES. 5. FOOD, NUTRITION, AND HEALTH: ENHANCE FOOD SAFETY, NUTRITION, AND PUBLIC HEALTH THROUGH INNOVATIONS IN VALUE-ADDED, FUNCTIONAL, AND NUTRACEUTICAL FOODS DERIVED FROM ANIMAL AND PLANT SYSTEMS, IMPROVING HEALTH OUTCOMES AND MARKET COMPETITIVENESS. THROUGH THIS INTEGRATED AND FORWARDFOCUSED RESEARCH AGENDA, THE VSU AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH STATION IS CULTIVATING INNOVATION, SUSTAINABILITY, AND SCIENTIFIC LEADERSHIP - DRIVING A MODERN, INCLUSIVE, AND RESILIENT AGRICULTURAL ENTERPRISE FOR VIRGINIA AND BEYOND.

ALABAMA AGRICULTURAL AND MECHANICAL UNIVERSITY (AAMU) CONDUCTS RESEARCH PROJECTS THAT MEET THE NEEDS OF THE CITIZENS OF ALABAMA AND THE NATION. TO FULFILL OUR OBLIGATIONS UNDER THE USDANIFA EVANS ALLEN ACT OF 1890 (SECTION 1445) FOR THE FISCAL YEAR 2026, THERE ARE SEVERAL PROJECTS BEING SUBMITTED FOR APPROVAL. RESEARCH AREAS OF INTEREST ARE: FOOD SYSTEMS AND FOOD SAFETY; GLOBAL FOOD SECURITY AND HUNGER; NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY; HUMAN NUTRITION, WELL-BEING, HEALTH AND OBESITY; AND COMMUNITY AND REGIONAL PLANNING. ALL THESE ARE ALIGNED WITH THE USDA PRIORITIES.  FOOD SYSTEMS AND FOOD SAFETY: RESEARCH AND EXTENSION-INTEGRATED ACTIVITIES ENHANCE FOOD SYSTEMS, FOOD SAFETY, AND AGRICULTURAL BIOSECURITY. THE GOAL OF THIS CRITICAL ISSUE IS TO DEVELOP TECHNOLOGY AND METHODS TO PROTECT AND ENHANCE THE SAFETY OF AGRICULTURE AND FOOD, REDUCE EPIDEMICS OF FOOD-BORNE ILLNESSES, AND TO DEVELOP THE KNOWLEDGE AND METHODOLOGIES FOR RAPID DETECTION OF THREAT AGENTS, INCLUDING EXISTING AND EMERGING DISEASES OF PLANTS AND ANIMALS, RISK ASSESSMENT, AND FACILITY AND PERSONNEL SECURITY.  GLOBAL FOOD SECURITY AND HUNGER: THE GOAL IS TO ENHANCE THE COMPETITIVENESS AND SUSTAINABILITY OF FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL INDUSTRIES IN ALABAMA THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF BEST PRACTICES OR TECHNOLOGIES. THIS CRITICAL ISSUE ADDRESSES TWO BROADLY DEFINED PRIORITY AREAS; I) PLANT HEALTH AND PRODUCTION AND PLANT PRODUCTS, INCLUDING IMPROVED CROPPING SYSTEMS, PLANT BREEDING/GENOMICS, INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT, PRECISION AGRICULTURE, AND ALTERNATIVE SPECIALTY CROPS; AND II) ANIMAL HEALTH AND PRODUCTION, INCLUDING IMPROVED FOOD-ANIMAL SYSTEMS AND STOCKS. OF PARTICULAR INTEREST ARE PROGRAMS AND PROJECTS THAT INCLUDE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES THAT PRESENT INNOVATIVE SYNERGIES OF DISCIPLINES AND PERSPECTIVES.  HUMAN NUTRITION, WELL-BEING, HEALTH AND OBESITY: OBESITY, DIABETES, HIGH BLOOD PRESSURE, AND VASCULAR ISSUES ARE MOSTLY CAUSED BY THE LACK OF NUTRIENTS, THE LACK OF EXERCISE, POOR LIFESTYLE CHOICES, AND STRESS OF THE INVOLVED INDIVIDUALS. AS A RESULT OF THE GROWING HEALTH CONCERNS FOR ALABAMA CITIZENS, THERE HAS BEEN A COMBINED EFFORT TO EDUCATE AND MOTIVATE CITIZENS THROUGHOUT THE STATE TO MAKE BETTER HEALTH DECISIONS. THE OBJECTIVE IS TO IMPROVE THE HEALTH OF ALABAMIANS, TARGETING LIMITED-RESOURCE FAMILIES, THROUGH CHRONIC DISEASE AWARENESS, PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, NUTRITION EDUCATION, HEALTH LITERACY, AND ACCESS TO AND CONSUMPTION OF FRESH FRUITS AND VEGETABLES. NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY: THIS PROGRAM PLAN WILL GENERATE KNOWLEDGE TO MANAGE AGRICULTURAL AND NATURAL SYSTEMS IN WAYS THAT SUPPORT ENERGY INDEPENDENCE, RESOURCE EFFICIENCY, AND RURAL ECONOMIC GROWTH. SPECIFIC AREAS INCLUDE: SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS, ENERGY UTILIZATION STRATEGIES (INCLUDING AGRICULTURAL WASTE-TO-ENERGY CONVERSION); WATER RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, SOIL HEALTH ENHANCEMENT, AND PRECISION AGRICULTURE. REMOTE SENSING AND TECHNOLOGY-DRIVEN APPROACHES WILL BE PRIORITIZED TO IMPROVE PRODUCTIVITY, REDUCE COSTS, AND ENSURE LONG-TERM RESOURCE SECURITY. ENVIRONMENTAL INITIATIVES WILL BE FRAMED AROUND SUPPORTING ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITY, RURAL-URBAN INTERFACE SOLUTIONS, AND COMMUNITY RESILIENCE.  COMMUNITY AND REGIONAL PLANNING: THIS AREA IS DESIGNED TO MAINTAIN THE INTEGRITY OF AGRICULTURAL LANDS THROUGH RURAL AND URBAN PLANNING PROGRAMS. APPROPRIATED FUNDS WILL BE USED FOR EXPENSES IN RESEARCH, WHICH WILL INCLUDE FACULTY AND STAFF SALARIES, STUDENT SUPPORT, DISSEMINATION OF RESEARCH RESULTS, ADMINISTRATIVE PLANNING AND DIRECTION, EQUIPMENT PURCHASE AND MAINTENANCE, AND SUPPLIES PURCHASE (AMONG OTHER APPROVED SPENDING).

ALABAMA'S RESEARCH AND EXTENSION SEEK TO ADDRESS SELECTED QUESTIONS THAT LEAD TO IDENTIFICATION OF CRITICAL ISSUES OF STRATEGIC IMPORTANCE. THESE ISSUES INCLUDE, BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO: (1) ENHANCING THE SUSTAINABILITY, COMPETITIVENESS, BIOSECURITY, AND PROFITABILITY OF U.S. FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS; (2) PLAYING A GLOBAL LEADERSHIP ROLE TO ENSURE A SAFE, SECURE, NUTRITIOUS, AND ABUNDANT FOOD SUPPLY FOR THE U.S. AND THE WORLD; (3) ADVANCING NATURAL RESOURCE STEWARDSHIP THROUGH PRACTICAL MANAGEMENT PRACTICES FOR FOOD AND WATER SYSTEMS, INCLUDING ADAPTATION TO CHANGING AGRICULTURAL CONDITIONS; (4) IMPROVING HUMAN HEALTH, NUTRITION, AND WELLBEING OF THE US POPULATION; (5) PROMOTING COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT, RURAL HEALTH, PROSPERITY AND RESILIENCE; (6) BUILDING CAPACITY OF INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES IN THE CONTEXT OF LEARNING, CULTURE, AND COMMUNITY; AND (7) SUPPORTING ENERGY SECURITY AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE BIO-ECONOMY FROM RENEWABLE NATURAL RESOURCES IN THE U.S. AS PART OF THE COMBINED ALABAMA LAND GRANT PLAN OF WORK, TUSKEGEE UNIVERSITY'S INTEGRATIVE RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS ARE PLANNED TO ADDRESS THE NATIONAL USDA FOOD, AGRICULTURE, NATURAL RECOURSES AND HUMAN SCIENCES STRATEGIC GOALS; NIFA PRIORITY SCIENCE AREAS AND THE ALABAMA AGRICULTURAL CRITICAL ISSUES AS IDENTIFIED BY THE STAKEHOLDERS. OUR PROGRAMS ARE THEREFORE FOCUSED ON THE FOLLOWING CRITICAL ISSUES: (1) GLOBAL FOOD SECURITY AND HUNGER; (2) NATURAL RESOURCE CONSERVATION AND MANAGEMENT: PRACTICAL APPROACHES TO WATER CONSERVATION, SOIL HEALTH, AND AGRICULTURAL RESILIENCE; (3) FOOD SYSTEM AND FOOD SAFETY; (4) HUMAN NUTRITION, WELL-BEING, HEALTH AND OBESITY; (5) SUSTAINABLE ENERGY; (6) COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT; AND (7) FAMILY, HOME AND 4-H AND YOUTH DEVELOPMENT. OUR PROGRAMS ARE DESIGNED TO PARTICULARLY ADDRESS THE ALABAMA BLACK BELT REGION AND FOCUS ON SMALL?SCALE, LIMITED?RESOURCE, AND RURAL PRODUCERS. SPECIFIC RESEARCH PROJECTS ARE THEREFORE FOCUSED ON: EFFICIENT WATER USE AND ADAPTATION TO AGRICULTURAL VARIABILITY TO SUPPORT SMALL AND LIMITED?RESOURCE FARMERS: MEAT GOAT PRODUCTION SYSTEMS TO IMPROVE PRODUCTIVITY FOR SMALL?SCALE PRODUCERS; APPROACHES AND MARKETING STRATEGIES TO INCREASE YIELDS OF VEGETABLES AND FRUITS FOR RURAL FARMERS IN ALABAMA; ALTERNATIVE POULTRY PRODUCTION: A SUSTAINABLE INTEGRATIVE POULTRY PRODUCTION MODEL FOR SMALL SCALE PRODUCERS; INTEGRATIVE APPROACHES TO OBESITY PREVENTION IN ALABAMA BLACK BELT COUNTIES; STRENGTHENING PROGRAMS IN ORGANIC FARMING IN ALABAMA THROUGH RESEARCH AND EDUCATION; AND DEVELOPMENT AND EVALUATION OF FARM BASED ENERGY SOLUTIONS THAT IMPROVE EFFICIENCY AND SUPPORT RURAL COMMUNITIES IN ALABAMA.

LANGSTON UNIVERSITY'S LAND-GRANT RESEARCH PROGRAMS, PRIMARILY FUNDED BY EVANS ALLEN AND RELATED COST SHARE APPROPRIATIONS, AIM TO GENERATE SUBSTANTIAL POSITIVE IMPACT ON INDIVIDUALS AND COMMUNITIES BY ENHANCING AND EXPANDING RESEARCH IN THE FIELDS OF FOOD, AGRICULTURE, HUMAN, NATURAL SCIENCE, AND CONSUMER ISSUES. SPECIFICALLY, THE RESEARCH PROGRAM SEEKS TO IDENTIFY CHALLENGES, EXPLORE SOLUTIONS, AND ACHIEVE TANGIBLE RESULTS ON CONTEMPORARY AND EMERGING AGRICULTURAL AND RELATED CHALLENGES AT THE LOCAL, STATE, NATIONAL, AND INTERNATIONAL LEVELS. THIS ENCOMPASSES THE IMPROVEMENT OF AGRICULTURAL METHODOLOGIES AND PRODUCTS, AS WELL AS THE ENHANCEMENT OF THE WELLBEING AND QUALITY OF LIFE FOR COMMUNITIES. LANGSTON UNIVERSITY HAS MADE SIGNIFICANT PROGRESS IN EXPANDING ITS RESEARCH PROGRAMMING AND HAS CURRENTLY ALLOCATED FUNDING TO SIXTEEN INDIVIDUAL EVANS ALLEN PROJECTS ACROSS VARIOUS DISCIPLINES, INCLUDING ANIMAL SCIENCE, ANIMAL PRODUCTS, PLANT SCIENCE (ENCOMPASSING HORTICULTURE AND BIOTECHNOLOGY), AQUACULTURE, AND AGRIBUSINESS. PROGRAMS AND METHODS OF DELIVERY ARE DESIGNED TO ADDRESS THE NEEDS OF HOUSEHOLDS, BUSINESSES, AND THE ENTIRE POPULATIONS THROUGHOUT THE STATE, IN BOTH RURAL AND URBAN AREAS. LU-SL/SAAS RESEARCH AND RELATED EXTENSION PROGRAM OBJECTIVE: THE OBJECTIVE OF THE LU-SL/SAAS RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS IS TO GENERATE BOTH SHORT-TERM AND LONG-TERM POSITIVE IMPACTS ON INDIVIDUALS AND COMMUNITIES BY ENHANCING AND EXPANDING RESEARCH IN THE FIELDS OF FOOD, AGRICULTURE, AND CONSUMER ISSUES. THE RESEARCH PROGRAM ACHIEVES THESE OBJECTIVES BY CONCENTRATING ON THE FOLLOWING EVANS ALLEN RESEARCH PROJECT AREAS, WHICH ARE DISTINCT YET INTERCONNECTED IN UNIQUE WAYS. DUE TO THE DISTINCTIVE TRIPARTITE MISSION OF THE LAND-GRANT UNIVERSITIES, ALL RESEARCH PROJECTS ARE INTERCONNECTED TO LU-SL/SAAS EXTENSION CLUSTERS. THE EVANS ALLEN PROJECTS ARE AS FOLLOWS: ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED: RESEARCH PROJECTS: EVANS ALLEN-FEDERAL AND STATE MATCH: ONE EVANS ALLEN RESEARCH ADMINISTRATION (ADMINISTRATION AND OPERATIONS), FIVE EVANS ALLEN: GOAT MANAGEMENT, PRODUCTION AND PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT, ONE EVANS ALLEN: DAYLILY (PLANT BIOTECHNOLOGY), TWO EVANS, ALLEN: AQUACULTURE, TWO EVANS ALLEN: HORTICULTURE, AND NATURAL RESOURCES, TWO EVANS ALLEN: AGRIBUSINESS MANAGEMENT AND APPLIED ECONOMICS, ONE EVANS ALLEN: RESEARCH COMMUNICATIONS: (SUPPORT), ONE EVANS ALLEN VALUE-ADDED PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT, ONE EVANS ALLEN SOILS, AND ECOLOGICAL RESILIENCE.

ALCORN STATE UNIVERSITY, FOUNDED IN 1871, IS THE NATION'S FIRST 1890 HBCU LAND-GRANT UNIVERSITY, LOCATED IN LORMAN, MISSISSIPPI. IT PROVIDES A WIDE RANGE OF AGRICULTURAL RESEARCH AND EXTENSION SERVICES TO THE COMMUNITIES IT SERVES. RESEARCH AT ALCORN SPANS DIVERSE FIELDS INCLUDING AGRONOMY, PLANT BREEDING, PATHOLOGY, ENTOMOLOGY, MYCOLOGY, VIROLOGY, SOIL AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCES, ANIMAL SCIENCE, PLANT BIOTECHNOLOGY, BIOFUELS, BIOPROCESSING, AGRICULTURAL ECONOMICS, AGRIBUSINESS, AGRICULTURAL MECHANICS, AND SMART AGRICULTURE TECHNOLOGIES. A KEY COMPONENT OF THIS MISSION ALSO INVOLVES EXPANDING AWARENESS OF AGRICULTURE WHILE RECRUITING, TRAINING, AND MENTORING STUDENTS FROM HIGH SCHOOLS AND COMMUNITY COLLEGES, THEREBY CONTRIBUTING TO WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT AND PREPARING SKILLED PROFESSIONALS FOR THE AGRICULTURAL SECTOR. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH PROGRAM ADDRESSES CRITICAL ISSUES SUCH AS SOIL AND WATER QUALITY DEGRADATION AND MITIGATION; USE OF COVER CROPS AND ORGANIC FERTILIZERS; CROP BREEDING AND GENETIC IMPROVEMENT; VEGETABLE AND FRUIT PRODUCTION, PROCESSING, AND STORAGE; EVALUATION OF NOVEL BIOFERTILIZERS SUCH AS BIOCHARS FOR CROP PRODUCTIONS; ANIMAL NUTRITION AND FEED RESEARCH; SOIL SURVEYS; AND IRRIGATION MANAGEMENT TO IMPROVE CROP POTENTIAL AND RESOURCE CONSERVATION. ADDITIONAL FOCUS AREAS INCLUDE DEVELOPMENT AND APPLICATION OF PEST DIAGNOSTIC AND MANAGEMENT TECHNOLOGIES, EVALUATION OF SPECIALTY CROPS FOR SMALL FARM INTEGRATION AND ECONOMIC IMPACT, EDUCATION PROGRAMS TO STRENGTHEN RURAL COMMUNITIES, ADOPTION OF NOVEL BIOTECHNOLOGY (INCLUDING GENOME EDITING FOR YIELD AND QUALITY IMPROVEMENT), APPLICATION OF ROBOTICS AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN PRODUCTION SYSTEMS, ZOONOTIC DISEASE RESEARCH, AND PUBLIC HEALTH EDUCATION. RESEARCH ACTIVITIES WILL BE CONDUCTED ON- AND OFF-CAMPUS BY FACULTY, STAFF, AND STUDENTS. EXPECTED DELIVERABLES INCLUDE DETAILED RESEARCH REPORTS, NEW GERMPLASM AND CULTIVARS, IMPROVED PROCESSING AND STORAGE METHODS, CROP PERFORMANCE DATA, FINDINGS ON ANIMAL AND HUMAN HEALTH THROUGH MODIFIED DIETS, ENHANCED SOIL AND WATER MANAGEMENT PRACTICES, DIAGNOSTIC TOOLKITS FOR PEST MANAGEMENT, INTEGRATION OF SPECIALTY CROPS INTO SMALL FARM OPERATIONS, ADOPTION OF ROBOTICS AND AI TECHNOLOGIES, EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS FOR OUTREACH, AND INCREASED PUBLIC AWARENESS OF ZOONOTIC DISEASES. DISSEMINATION WILL OCCUR THROUGH EXTENSION PROGRAMS, OUTREACH SERVICES, CONFERENCE PRESENTATIONS, AND PEER-REVIEWED PUBLICATIONS. THIS INTEGRATED EFFORT WILL BENEFIT ALCORN STATE UNIVERSITY, SURROUNDING COMMUNITIES, THE STATE OF MISSISSIPPI, THE AGRICULTURAL INDUSTRY, AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC BY ADVANCING SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE, SUPPORTING SMALL FARMERS, STRENGTHENING THE AGRICULTURAL WORKFORCE, AND IMPROVING COMMUNITY RESILIENCE.

NINETY PERCENT OF FLORIDA'S FARMS FIT THE DEFINITION OF A SMALL FARM, MAKING OUR MISSION PARTICULARLY CRUCIAL IN ENHANCING THE STATE'S OVERALL ECONOMY. FAMU LIVESTOCK AND CROP IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM. LASTLY, FAMU LIVESTOCK AND CROP IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM WILL INCLUDE LIVESTOCK IMPROVEMENT, HAY PRODUCTION, FORAGE SYSTEMS IMPROVEMENT, SPECIALIZED HORTICULTURAL CROPS SUCH AS INDUSTRIAL HEMP, OLIVES, AQUACULTURE, AND BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES FOR LIVESTOCK AND CROP PRODUCTION. THE KEY AREAS OF FOCUS FOR OUR RESEARCH PROGRAMS INCLUDE: VITICULTURE AND SMALL FRUITS; PRESERVING AND PROTECTING WATER QUALITY OF NORTH FLORIDA WATERSHEDS; STRATEGIC RESEARCH FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF INVASIVE PEST SPECIES, AND FAMU LIVESTOCK AND CROP IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM.

COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE AND ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCES (CAES) AT NCA<(>&<)>T ENCOURAGES INNOVATIVE AND INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH NECESSARY TO ADVANCE AMERICAN AGRICULTURAL TECHNOLOGY, SOLVE THE PROBLEM OF FOOD INSECURITY AND PROMOTE SUSTAINABLE PRACTICES. CAES USES DIGITAL AND PRECISION INSTRUMENTS, CLOUD BASED STATISTICAL ANALYTICS PLATFORM ALONG WITH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES TO CONDUCT CROSS CUTTINGEDGE RESEARCH ON THE UNIVERSITY FARM, AT THE CENTER FOR ENVIRONMENTAL FARMING SYSTEMS IN GOLDSBORO (CEFS), AT THE CENTER OF EXCELLENCE IN POST-HARVEST TECHNOLOGIES (CEPHT) IN KANNAPOLIS, AND ON CAMPUS IN LABORATORIES WHERE INVESTIGATIONS INCLUDE AGRICULTURAL ECONOMICS, ANIMAL SCIENCE, SOIL SCIENCE, PLANT SCIENCE, HUMAN NUTRITION, FOOD SCIENCE AND BIOENERGY. THE COMPLETION OF URBAN FOOD COMPLEX AND HIGH-TECH GREEN HOUSE WILL ENHANCE THE COLLEGE'S CAPABILITIES IN RESEARCH, TEACHING AND OUTREACH. THE CAES ENGAGES IN FRONTIER RESEARCH AND PROMOTES INTEGRATIVE, CROSS-DISCIPLINARY APPROACHES, INCLUDING OUTREACH ACTIVITIES THAT BUILD CRITICAL MASS AND ENHANCE IMPACT AMONG GROWERS, CONSUMERS, AND SCIENTISTS ACROSS NORTH CAROLINA AND THE NATION. OUR PORTFOLIO OF SOLUTION-DRIVEN, CUTTING-EDGE RESEARCH GENERATES NEW KNOWLEDGE AND TECHNOLOGIES THAT ARE SHARED WITH ALL NORTH CAROLINIANS THROUGH NC COOPERATIVE EXTENSION. THE RESULTS ARE ALSO DISSEMINATED WITHIN THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY THROUGH CONFERENCES AND PEER-REVIEWED PUBLICATIONS.  BY TRANSFORMING SCIENTIFIC DISCOVERY INTO PRACTICAL, EVERYDAY SOLUTIONS, WE ENHANCE QUALITY OF LIFE AND EMPOWER INDIVIDUALS AND COMMUNITIES TO LIVE HEALTHIER, MORE PROSPEROUS LIVES. TO MOVE FORWARD WITH THIS AIM WE ARE FOCUSING ON FOUR INTEGRATIVE CLUSTERS (PRIORITIES): ENHANCING FOOD SAFETY, NUTRITION AND HEALTH: CAES RESEARCHERS WILL FOCUS ON DEVELOPING NEW FOOD PRODUCTS TO IMPROVE HUMAN HEALTH, REDUCE OBESITY, INCREASE IMMUNITY AND PREVENT DISEASES. THE RESEARCH WILL FOCUS ON THE PRODUCTION OF FUNCTIONAL FOODS, WHOLE GRAIN CEREALS, HUMAN HEALTH AND HUMAN NUTRITION, FOOD ALLERGIES, FOOD PRODUCTION PROCESSES, BIOACTIVE COMPOUNDS OF FOOD, POST-HARVEST TECHNOLOGY AND FOOD SECURITY. ENRICHING YOUTH, FAMILY AND COMMUNITY WELL-BEING: CAES RESEARCHERS ARE DEDICATED TO WORKING WITH BOTH NC'S RURAL AND URBAN POPULATIONS; OFFERING A WIDE VARIETY OF RESEARCH-BASED PROGRAMS TO OVERCOME THE CHALLENGES OF FAMILIES AND COMMUNITIES. RESEARCHERS WILL FOCUS ON HEALTHY EATING HABITS, EARLY CHILDHOOD DEVELOPMENT, PARENTING AND CHILDHOOD OBESITY, COMMUNITY-BASED ACTIVITIES FOR DISASTER PREPAREDNESS. ENVIRONMENTAL AND NATURAL RESOURCES: RESEARCHERS WILL INVESTIGATE AN ADVANCED BIOLOGICAL SYSTEM TO PRODUCE ALTERNATIVE ENERGY, TREAT AGRICULTURAL AND INDUSTRIAL WASTE, AND PROTECT AND IMPROVE WATER QUALITY. CAES RESEARCHERS WILL ALSO STUDY THE EFFICIENT WAY IRRIGATE CROPS, ADD AESTHETIC VALUE OF THE LAND VIA LANDSCAPING, AND WILL BE INVOLVED IN A MULTISTATE WEATHER RESILIENCE PROJECT TO STUDY THE IMPACT OF WEATHER AND NATURAL DISASTERS ON FARMERS AND COMMUNITIES. RESEARCHERS WILL BE DEVELOPING ADAPTATION AND MITIGATION SOLUTIONS TO IMPROVE AGRICULTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCES. IMPROVING PLANT AND ANIMAL AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS: IN ANIMAL SYSTEMS, RESEARCHERS WILL STUDY THE EFFICIENCY OF DIFFERENT FEEDING SOURCES TO IMPROVE ANIMAL PRODUCTIVITY AND GUT HEALTH. ALSO, RESEARCHERS WILL STUDY TO FIND THE SOLUTION FOR VIRAL, BACTERIAL, AND PARASITIC EFFECTS IN ANIMALS AND POULTRY. IN PLANT SYSTEMS, THE FOCUS WILL BE ON SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE, ALTERNATIVE AND HIGH VALUE CROP PRODUCTION, SEASON EXTENSION, WEATHER RESILIENCE PRACTICES, VALUE ADDED AGRICULTURE, DIGITAL AGRICULTURE, SOIL HEALTH, PEST CONTROL, AND AGROECONOMICS. SUBRECIPIENT ACTIVITIES INCLUDE COLLABORATING WITH THE UNIVERSITY OF NORTH CAROLINA AT GREENSBORO TO UNDERSTAND THE PHYSIOLOGICAL AND MOLECULAR RESPONSES TO DROUGHT STRESS OF INDIGENOUS VEGETABLES WITH UNTAPPED POTENTIAL FOR NUTRITION, HEALTH, AND FOOD SECURITY IN THE FACE OF GLOBAL CHANGE.

positiveFlows.title: IN 2024, SC STATE UNIVERSITY ADVANCED ITS MISSION OF TEACHING, RESEARCH, AND OUTREACH BY DELIVERING IMPACTFUL PROGRAMS ACROSS 32 SOUTH CAROLINA COUNTIES. THE UNIVERSITY FOCUSED ON FIVE CRITICAL ISSUES: AGRIBUSINESS AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT, AGRISYSTEMS PRODUCTIVITY AND PROFITABILITY, ENVIRONMENTAL AND NATURAL RESOURCES CONSERVATION, FAMILY AND YOUTH DEVELOPMENT, AND FOOD SAFETY, SECURITY, AND NUTRITION. THESE INITIATIVES AIMED TO IMPROVE THE QUALITY OF LIFE FOR CITIZENS THROUGH EDUCATION, INNOVATION, AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT. UNDER AGRIBUSINESS AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT, SC STATE ADDRESSED CHALLENGES SUCH AS UNEMPLOYMENT, POVERTY, AND ENVIRONMENTAL HAZARDS. STAFF FACILITATED 20 WORKSHOPS, 7 IN-PERSON, 7 HYBRID, AND 6 VIRTUAL, REACHING 9,269 DIRECT CONTACTS OVER 1,948 HOURS AND 37,727 INDIRECT CONTACTS OVER 1,402 HOURS. NINETY PERCENT OF PARTICIPANTS REPORTED KNOWLEDGE GAINS, AND SIX JOBS WERE CREATED THROUGH A RURAL BUSINESS ENTERPRISE GRANT. IN AGRISYSTEMS PRODUCTIVITY AND PROFITABILITY, THE SMALL FARMS TEAM CONDUCTED 58 WORKSHOPS AND WORKED WITH OVER 577 SMALL FARMERS. THEY LOGGED 3,969 DIRECT CONTACT HOURS WITH 16,269 INDIVIDUALS AND 1,516 INDIRECT HOURS WITH 9,678 CONTACTS. PROGRAMMING COVERED ANIMAL PRODUCTION, SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE, AND RISK MANAGEMENT. TOPICS INCLUDED BEEF CATTLE HERD HEA LTH, COLLABORATIVE MARKETING, AGRICULTURAL TAXES, AND NRCS SERVICES. NINETY PERCENT OF PARTICIPANTS HAD ACRES IMPACTED BY INTEGRATED CROP MANAGEMENT, REFLECTING A 56% INCREASE FROM THE PREVIOUS YEAR. A TOTAL OF 117 FARMERS REPORTED PROFIT GAINS, AND 650 PRODUCERS ADOPTED RECOMMENDED PRACTICES. FAMILY AND YOUTH DEVELOPMENT EFFORTS INCLUDED 400 WORKSHOPS FOCUSED ON CIVIC ENGAGEMENT, HEALTHY LIFESTYLES, FINANCIAL LITERACY, S.T.R.E.A.M. (SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY, READING, ENGINEERING, AGRICULTURE/ARTS, AND MATHEMATICS), AND THE AGRICULTURE INNOVATION SCHOLARSHIP PROGRAM. STAFF MADE 43,896 DIRECT CONTACTS OVER 4 ,360 HOURS AND REACHED 1,484,408 INDIVIDUALS INDIRECTLY OVER 2,004 HOURS. YOUTH PARTICIPATED IN HANDS-ON LEARNING SUCH AS CODING, DRONE EXPLORATION, AND ROBOTICS, FOSTERING LIFELONG SKILLS AND CIVIC RESPONSIBILITY. FOOD SAFETY, SECURITY, AND NUTRITION INITIATIVES WERE DELIVERED THROUGH 1,181 WORKSHOPS PROMOTING HEALTHY BEHAVIORS AND DISEASE PREVENTION. STAFF COLLABORATED WITH ADVISORY COUNCILS AND STAKEHOLDERS TO DESIGN EVIDENCE-BASED NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAMS. THEY MADE 22,720 DIRECT CONTACTS OVER 2,969 HOURS AND 332,595 INDIRECT CONTACTS OVER 1,289 HOURS. SIXTY-EIGHT PERCENT OF PARTICIPANTS GAINED NUTRITION KNOWLEDGE. EIGHTEEN MEMORANDUMS OF UNDERSTANDING WERE SIGNED WITH EXTERNAL AGENCIES. STAFF EARNED SERVSAFE AND UTAH STATE NUTRITION CERTIFICATIONS. THE EFNEP EXPLORERS CAMP GRADUATED 636 YOUTH, ALL OF WHOM REPORTED INTENTIONS TO DRINK MORE WATER AND EAT MORE FRUITS. SC STATE'S RESEARCH PORTFOLIO INCLUDED SIX PROJECTS: AI AND DATA ANALYSIS, PHYTOCHEMICALS FROM SWEET POTATOES, FOOD HUB NETWORKS, AIENABLED SMART FARMING IOT SYSTEMS, POLYCYCLIC AROMATIC HYDROCARBONS IN SOIL, AND ATMO SPHERIC WATER GENERATION FROM RECYCLED PLASTICS. THREE PROJECTS CONCLUDED IN JULY 2025 AND PREPARED BULLETINS FOR PUBLICATION; THREE REMAIN ACTIVE. THESE RESEARCH EFFORTS HAVE BROAD IMPLICATIONS FOR SUSTAINABILITY, INNOVATION, AND AGRICULTURAL ADVANCEMENT. COLLECTIVELY, SC STATE UNIVERSITY'S PROGRAMS AND RESEARCH INITIATIVES DEMONSTRATE A STRONG COMMITMENT TO COMMUNITY EMPOWERMENT, SCIENTIFIC PROGRESS, AND INCLUSIVE EDUCATION, SERVING AS A CATALYST FOR POSITIVE CHANGE ACROSS SOUTH CAROLINA.

THE HEALTH OF AIR, LAND/SOIL, AND WATER RESOURCES DIRECTLY IMPACTS AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTIVITY AND RURAL QUALITY OF LIFE. THESE RESOURCES FACE INCREASING PRESSURE FROM INPUT-DEPENDENT, HIGHLY SPECIALIZED CROP AND LIVESTOCK SYSTEMS COMBINED WITH VARIABLE WEATHER CONDITIONS SUCH AS RECORD-SETTING TEMPERATURES, FLOODING, AND DROUGHTS. THESE CHALLENGES POSE SIGNIFICANT RISKS TO THE SUSTAINABLE PROVISION OF FOOD, CLEAN WATER, AND OTHER ESSENTIAL SERVICES FOR MISSOURIANS.  IN ALIGNMENT WITH THE USDA-NIFA'S RESEARCH PRIORITIES, LINCOLN UNIVERSITY'S COOPERATIVE RESEARCH (LUCR) PROGRAM HAS BEEN CONDUCTING RESEARCH IN THE FOLLOWING AREAS: 1) ANIMAL SCIENCE, 2) SOIL HEALTH AND CROP SCIENCES, 3) FOOD NUTRITION AND SAFETY, 4) NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, AND 5) SOCIAL-ECONOMICS. LUCR AIMS TO CONTINUE DEVELOPING IMPACTFUL, INNOVATIVE, AND MULTIDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH PROGRAMS THAT EFFECTIVELY ADDRESS EMERGING AND CRITICAL ISSUES FACING MISSOURI'S NATURAL RESOURCES, AGRICULTURAL INDUSTRY, AND RURAL COMMUNITIES AS WELL AS STRENGTHEN LINCOLN UNIVERSITY'S CAPACITY TO BETTER ADDRESS THE NEEDS OF MISSOURI FARMERS AND RANCHERS. LUCR FACULTY MEMBERS CONTRIBUTE TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF RESILIENT AGRICULTURAL AND FOOD SYSTEMS THAT SUSTAIN PRODUCTION, IMPROVE ECOSYSTEM HEALTH, AND SAFEGUARD HUMAN HEALTH. THE PROGRAM EMPHASIZES PRACTICAL SOLUTIONS FOR SMALL FARMERS, RANCHERS, AND FOREST LANDOWNERS TO IMPROVE PRODUCTIVITY AND ADAPT TO CHANGING AGRICULTURAL CONDITIONS.  OF THE SIX CRITICAL ISSUES IDENTIFIED, LUCR CAPACITY RESEARCH EFFORTS ARE PRIMARILY FOCUSED ON: 1) SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE SYSTEMS - INCLUDING SMALL RUMINANT BREEDING, GRAZING MANAGEMENT, POULTRY OPERATIONS, AQUACULTURE, HYDROPONICS, INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT, SPECIALTY CROPS, VEGETABLE DISEASE CONTROL, AND ORGANIC FARMING. 2) NATURAL RESOURCE STEWARDSHIP - INCLUDING SOIL HEALTH, AGROFORESTRY, AND TECHNOLOGY APPLICATIONS SUCH AS GIS AND REMOTE SENSING TO IMPROVE LAND MANAGEMENT. 3) HEALTH AND FOOD SAFETY - INCLUDING SENSOR DEVELOPMENT FOR DETECTION OF FOODBORNE PATHOGENS, DRINKING WATER QUALITY, AND MONITORING OF CONTAMINANTS RELEVANT TO AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION. THE OVERALL GOAL OF CAPACITY RESEARCH EFFORTS IN THE LUCR PROGRAM IS TO HELP FARMERS AND RURAL COMMUNITIES ADOPT MANAGEMENT PRACTICES THAT STRENGTHEN AGRICULTURAL SUSTAINABILITY, IMPROVE NATURAL RESOURCE STEWARDSHIP, AND PROTECT HUMAN HEALTH THROUGH SAFE FOOD AND WATER SYSTEMS. CONTINUED SUPPORT FROM NIFA AND THE STATE OF MISSOURI IS CRITICAL TO EXPANDING LINCOLN UNIVERSITY'S RESEARCH CAPACITY AND ENSURING THAT MISSOURI'S FARMERS AND RANCHERS-PARTICULARLY SMALL-SCALE PRODUCERS-HAVE THE TOOLS AND KNOWLEDGE NEEDED TO THRIVE IN THE FACE OF AGRICULTURAL CHALLENGES

negativeFlows.title: LANGSTON UNIVERSITY LAND-GRANT PROGRAMS ARE DEDICATED TO SERVING ALL CITIZENS OF OKLAHOMA. HOWEVER, PROGRAMS AND METHODS OF DELIVERY ARE DESIGNED TO ADDRESS THE NEEDS OF UNDERSERVED AND UNDERREPRESENTED DIVERSE POPULATIONS OF THE STATE, ESPECIALLY SMALL FARMERS, AND LIMITED RESOURCE CONSUMERS. PROJECTED OUTCOMES AND IMPACTS INCLUDE DELIVERABLES THAT CONTRIBUTE TO ENHANCING THE ECONOMIC STATUS, HEALTH, AND QUALITY OF LIFE FOR THE CITIZENS OF OKLAHOMA; AND TO MAKE THEM MORE COMPETITIVE AS VIABLE PRODUCERS AND CONSUMERS IN NICHE MARKETS AND IN THE BROADER GLOBAL MARKETPLACE. ALL RESEARCH AND EXTENSION ACTIVITIES SATISFY STRATEGIC GOALS INCLUDED IN THE USDA 2023-2026 STRATEGIC PLAN. CONCEPTS THAT ADDRESS CLIMATE CHANGE AND ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIPS ARE KEENLY ADDRESSED; (2) PROVIDE EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES FOR STUDENTS AND OTHER STAKEHOLDERS IN THE FOOD, AGRICULTURAL NATURAL RESOURCES, AND HUMAN SCIENCES (FANH). IN ALIGNMENT WITH THE USDA-NIFA'S TOP RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PRIORITY AREAS, LINCOLN UNIVERSITY'S COOPERATIVE EXTENSION AND RESEARCH PROGRAM CONDUCT RESEARCH AND EXTENSION ACTIVITIES IN ANIMAL SCIENCE, PLANT SCIENCE, FOOD SAFETY, NATURAL RESOURCE, SOCIAL ECONOMICS, HUMAN HEALTH, AND YOUTH AREAS THAT ADDRESS EMERGENT AND CRITICAL ISSUES FACING MISSOURI FARMS AND AGRICULTURE COMMUNITIES. THE PROGRAM ESPECIALLY TARGETS UNDERREPRESENTED, UNDERSERVED, SMALL FAMERS AND COMMUNITY AND FIRST GENERATION STUDENTS. THE EXTENSION AND RESEARCH PROGRAM IS CURRENTLY FOCUSED ON FIVE (5) IDENTIFIED CRITICAL ISSUES OF SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE, HEALTH, SOCIAL JUSTICE AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT, ENVIRONMENTAL AND NATURAL RESOURCES, AND EDUCATION AND CO MMUNICATION WITH UNDERSERVED POPULATIONS IN MISSOURI THROUGH THE INTEGRATIVE, INNOVATIVE APPROACH FOR RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMMING. THE PROGRAM IS LAUNCHING SIX INITIATIVES: ORGANIC FARMING, URBAN AGRICULTURE, INDUSTRIAL HEMP, FOOD SAFETY TRAINING, ANDFOREST ECOSYSTEM, AND SMALL RUMINANT, IN AN EFFORT TO MEET THE CRITICAL, GROWING NEEDS OF THE STATE AND STAKEHOLDERS. IN ADDITION, IN 2022, THE EXTENSION AND RESEARCH PROGRAM HAS ALSO JOINED THE GROUP EFFORTS OF THE 1890 MULTISTATE CLIMATE CHANGE PROJECT AND PARTICIPATED IN ALL FOUR PROJECT OBJECTIVES FOCUSING ON 1) SOIL HEALTH AND ADOPTIVE AG PRACTICES NEEDS ASSESSMENT AND TRAINING PROGRAM FOR SOCIALLY DISADVANTAGED FARMERS; 2) WATER RESOURCE AND CLIMATE CHANGE ASSESSMENT; 3) ENVIRONMENTAL JUSTICE AND EQUITY FOR LOW-INCOME COMMUNITIES; AND 4) ANALYSIS OF CLIMATE CHANGE POLICY. THE LU RESEARCH PROGRAM CONTINUES TO CONDUCT CUTTING-EDGE, IMPACTFUL FOOD AND AGRICULTURE RESEARCH THROUGH MULTI-INSTITUTION AND MULTIDISCIPLINARY COLLABORATIONS. THESE PROGRAMS SEEK TO EFFECTIVELY ADDRESS URGENT, EMERGENT ISSUES AND DEVELOP SUSTAINABLE SOLUTIONS TO THE PROBLEMS FACING MISSOURI'S AGRICULTURE INDUSTRY AND RURAL COMMUNITIES AS WELL AS TO STRENGTHEN THE UNIVERSITY'S CAPACITY TO PROVIDE BETTER SERVICE FOR THE NEEDS OF MISSOURI'S SMALL FARMERS, ESPECIALLY UNDERSERVED FARMERS. THE RESEARCH PROGRAM HAS FIVE RESEARCH FOCUSES: 1) ANIMAL PRODUCTION; 2) CROP AND VEGETABLE PRODUCTION, 3) FOOD SAFETY, 4) NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, AND 5) SOCIAL ECONOMICS, WITH AN EMPHASIS OF SMALL RUMINANTS, AQUACULTURE, SOIL HEALTH, SPECIALTY CROPS, ORGANIC PRODUCTION, FOOD SAFETY DETECTION, WATER QUALITY, FOREST HEALTH, AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT. THE FACULTY MEMBERS IN THE PROGRAM ACTIVELY PURSUE EXTRAMURAL FUNDING TO SUPPORT CURRENT RESEARCH AND LEVERAGE RESOURCES PROVIDED BY FEDERAL AND STATE PARTNERS. THE LU EXTENSION EFFORTS AIM TO IMPROVE THE EDUCATION AND ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES TO UNDERREPRESENTED POPULATIONS IN KANSAS CITY, ST. LOUIS, AND CENTRAL, SOUTHEAST AND SOUTHWEST MISSOURI. THE PROGRAMS WILL ASSIST FARMERS, FAMILIES, YOUTH AND THE ELDERLY AS WELL AS ENTIRE COMMUNITIES WITH UNDERSERVED AND UNDERREPRESENTED POPULATIONS THROUGH FOLLOWING OUTREACH ACTIVITIES: 1) 4-H AND YOUTH DEVELOPMENT, 2) FAMILY DEVELOPMENT, 3) COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT, 4) HEALTH AND AGING, 5) FOOD AND NUTRITION, AND 6) URBAN GARDENING. THE PAULA J. CARTER CENTER ON MINORITY HEALTH AND AGING WILL PROVIDE PROGRAMS ADDRESSING HEALTH LITERACY, HEALTH DISPARITY REDUCTION AND CHRONIC DISEASE PREVENTION FOR UNDERSERVED AUDIENCE WITH AGES OF FIFTY AND OVER.

ALABAMA AGRICULTURAL AND MECHANICAL UNIVERSITY (AAMU) CONDUCTS RESEARCH PROJECTS THAT MEET THE NEEDS OF THE CITIZENS OF ALABAMA AND THE NATION. TO FULFILL OUR OBLIGATIONS UNDER USDA-NIFA EVANS ALLEN ACT OF 1890 (SECTION 1445) FOR FISCAL YEAR 2023, THERE ARE SEVERAL APPROVED PROJECTS. BROADLY, RESEARCH AREAS OF INTERESTS ARE: FOOD SYSTEMS AND FOOD SAFETY; GLOBAL FOOD SECURITY AND HUNGER; NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY; HUMAN NUTRITION, WELL-BEING, HEALTH AND OBESITY; AND COMMUNITY AND REGIONAL PLANNING. FOOD SYSTEMS AND FOOD SAFETY: RESEARCH AND EXTENSION INTEGRATED ACTIVITIES ENHANCE FOOD SYSTEMS, FOOD SAFETY AND AGRICULTURAL BIOSEC URITY. THE GOAL OF THIS CRITICAL ISSUE IS TO DEVELOP TECHNOLOGY AND METHODS TO PROTECT AND ENHANCE THE SAFETY OF AGRICULTURE AND FOOD, REDUCE EPIDEMICS OF FOOD-BORNE ILLNESSES, AND TO DEVELOP THE KNOWLEDGE AND METHODOLOGIES FOR RAPID DETECTION OF THREAT AGENTS, IN CLUDING EXISTING AND EMERGING DISEASES OF PLANTS AND ANIMALS, RISK ASSESSMENT, AND FACILITY AND PERSONNEL SECURITY. GLOBAL FOOD SECURITY AND HUNGER: THE GOAL IS TO ENHANCE COMPETITIVENESS AND SUSTAINABILITY OF FOOD AND AGRICULTURAL INDUSTRIES IN ALABAMA THROUGH DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF BEST PRACTICES OR TECHNOLOGIES. THIS CRITICAL ISSUE ADDRESSES TWO BROADLY DEFINED PRIORITY AREAS; I) PLANT HEALTH AND PRODUCTION AND PLANT PRODUCTS, INCLUDING IMPROVED CROPPING SYSTEMS, PLANT BREEDING/GENOMICS, INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT, PRECISION AGRICULTURE, ALTERNATIVE SPECIALTY CROPS; AND II) ANIMAL HEALTH AND PRODUCTION, INCLUDING IMPROVED FOOD-ANIMAL SYSTEMS AND STOCKS. OF PARTICULAR INTEREST ARE PROGRAMS AND PROJECTS THAT INCLUDE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES AND THAT PRESENT INNOVATIVE SYNERGIES OF DISCIPLINES AND PERSPECTIVES. HUMAN NUTRITION, WELL-BEING, HEALTH AND OBESITY: OBESITY, DIABETES, HIGH BLOOD PRESSURE, AND VASCULAR ISSUES ARE MOSTLY CAUSED BY THE LACK OF NUTRIENTS, THE LACK OF EXERCISE, POOR LIFESTYLE CHOICES, AND STRESS OF THE INVOLVED INDIVIDUALS. AS A RESULT OF THE GROWING HEALTH CONCERNS FOR ALABAMA CITIZENS, THERE HAS BEEN A COMBINED EFFORT TO EDUCATE AND MOTIVATE CITIZENS THROUGHOUT THE STATE TO MAKE BETTER HEALTH DECISIONS. THE OBJECTIVE IS TO IMPROVE THE HEALTH OF ALABAMIANS, TARGETING LIMITED-RESOURCE FAMILIES, THROUGH CHRONIC DISEASE AWARENESS, PHYSICAL ACTIVITY, NUTRITION EDUCATION, HEALTH LITERACY AND ACCESS TO AND CONSUMPTION OF FRESH FRUITS AND VEGETABLES. NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY: THIS PROGRAM PLAN WILL GENERATE KNOWLEDGE TO MANAGE AGRICULTURAL AND NATURAL SYSTEMS IN THE FACE OF CLIMATE CHANGE AND THE NEED TO SUSTAIN NATURAL RESOURCES. SPECIFIC AREAS INCLUDE: CLIMATE-SMART SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS, ENERGY CONSERVATION AND UTILIZATION OF RENEWABLE ENERGY RESOURCES; UNDERSTANDING THE LAND-WATER INTERFACE; CONSEQUENCES AND SOLUTIONS OF GLOBAL CLIMATE CHANGE; WATER QUALITY AND QUANTITY, CARBON SEQUESTRATION, NATURAL SYSTEMS RESTORATION, SURFACE AND GROUND WATERCONSERVATION; MANAGEMENT OF AGRICULTURAL WASTE RESIDUE; SUSTAINABLE SOIL HEALTH ENHANCEMENT; SUSTAINABLE ECO- AND AGRI-TOURISM; RURAL-URBAN INTERFACE ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES; REMOTE SENSING AND PRECISION AGRICULTURE. COMMUNITY AND REGIONAL PLANNING: THIS AREA IS DESIGNED TO MAINTAIN THE INTEGRITY OF AGRICULTURAL LANDS THROUGH RURAL AND URBAN PLANNING PROGRAMS. APPROPRIATED FUNDS WILL BE USED FOR EXPENSES IN CONDUCTING RESEARCH TO INCLUDE FACULTY AND STAFF SALARIES, STUDENT SUPPORT, DISSEMINATION OF RESEARCH RESULTS, ADMINISTRATIVE PLANNING AND DIRECTION, EQUIPMENT PURCHASE AND MAINTENANCE, AND SUPPLIES PURCHASE (AMONG OTHER APPROVED SPENDING).

THE UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE, FOOD AND ENVIRONMENT AND KENTUCKY STATE UNIVERSITY (KSU) COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE, COMMUNITIES, AND THE ENVIRONMENT WERE FOUNDED AS LAND-GRANT INSTITUTIONS (1862 AND 1890, RESPECTIVELY), OFFERING ACCESS TO KNOWLEDGE AND LEARNING TO ENHANCE THE LIVES OF KENTUCKIANS. THE TWO PROGRAMS ARE FUNDAMENTALLY INTERDISCIPLINARY, APPLYING THE BIOLOGICAL, PHYSICAL, AND SOCIAL SCIENCES TO CHALLENGES IN AGRICULTURAL, FOOD, AND ENVIRONMENTAL SYSTEMS. OUR WORK ENCOMPASSES FARMS AND FORESTS, FOOD AND FIBER, FAMILIES, AND COMMUNITIES. THE UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE, FOOD AND ENVIRONMENT HOLDS A UNIQUE POSITION AS THE HOME OF THE KENTUCKY AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION AND THE KENTUCKY COOPERATIVE EXTENSION SERVICE (KCES). THE TEACHING, RESEARCH, AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS ARE PART OF A NATIONAL SYSTEM THAT MAINTAINS A STATEWIDE PRESENCE AND LINKS LOCAL, STATE, NATIONAL AND GLOBAL ISSUES. THE KSU LAND GRANT PROGRAM AND COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE, COMMUNITIES AND THE ENVIRONMENT FOCUSES ON TEACHING, RESEARCH, AND EXTENSION TO ADDRESS THE NEEDS OF THE SMALL-SCALE AND LIMITED- RESOURCE FARMERS; MINORITY AND UNDERSERVED/DISPARITY COMMUNITIES, AS WELL AS DIVERSE AND AT-RISK YO UTHS. THESE PROGRAMS INCLUDE RESEARCH TO IDENTIFY NEW AND NICHE PRODUCTS AND MARKETS FOR SMALL-SCALE, LIMITED RESOURCE, AND MINORITY FARMERS, TO ENHANCE AVAILABILITY AND SAFETY OF LOCALLY PRODUCED, NUTRITIOUS FOODS, AND REDUCE FERTILIZER AND PESTICIDE RUNOFF TO IMPROVE SOIL AND WATER QUALITY WHILE REDUCING FARMER AND FORESTER EXPENSES. OUR VISION IS TO BE RECOGNIZED FOR EXCELLENCE IN FOSTERING LEARNING THAT CHANGES LIVES, DISCOVERIES THAT CHANGE THE WORLD AND OPPORTUNITIES THAT SHAPE THE FUTURE. RESEARCH AND EXTENSION, AS FULL PARTNERS WITH EXPANDING LINKAGES THROUGHOUT THE UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY AND KSU AND WITH SUPPORT FROM EVERY KENTUCKY COUNTY, SEEK TO 1) FACILITATE LIFELONG LEARNING INFORMED BY SCHOLARSHIP AND RESEARCH, 2) EXPAND KNOWLEDGE THROUGH CREATIVE RESEARCH AND DISCOVERY, AND 3) SERVE KENTUCKIANS BY SHARING AND APPLYING KNOWLEDGE. RESEARCH AND EXTENSION SEEK TO SUSTAIN THE LAND-GRANT HERITAGE OF ACHIEVEMENT IN THESE CHALLENGING TIMES, BUT THE COMMONWEALTH AND THE UNIVERSITIES ARE UNDERGOING MANY SIGNIFICANT CHANGES. AS KENTUCKY CONTINUES TO MOVE FROM A TOBACCO-BASED AGRICULTURAL ECONOMY AND EXPLORES NEW OPTIONS AND COMMODITIES, LAND-GRANT PROGRAMS FACE INCREASED DEMANDS AND EXPECTATIONS. TECHNOLOGY IS REDEFINING THE WAY PEOPLE ACQUIRE AND DISTRIBUTE INFORMATION AND HOW THEY SOLVE PROBLEMS. WHILE URBANIZATION IS CLAIMING FARMLAND, IT IS ALSO CREATING NEW MARKETS FOR TRADITIONAL AND NON-TRADITIONAL AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS. CHANGING LIFESTYLES AND DEMOGRAPHICS ARE CHALLENGING US WITH OPPORTUNITIES FOR GREATER INVOLVEMENT IN YOUTH, FAMILY, AND COMMUNITY PROGRAMS. WITH NEARLY 80,000 FARMS IN THE STATE AND AN AVERAGE 171 ACRES PER OPERATION, KENTUCKY IS DOMINATED BY SMALL FAMILY FARMS. HOWEVER, MANY OF THESE FARMS ARE MAJOR PRODUCERS OF TRADITIONAL AGRICULTURAL COMMODITIES, SUCH AS LIVESTOCK, TOBACCO, AND GRAIN. SOME SEEK NEW OPPORTUNITIES IN SPECIALTY CROPS AND INDUSTRIAL HEMP. OTHERS OPERATE ON A PART- TIME BASIS OR INVOLVE LIMITED RESOURCES.
